```text
# Cloud Agents Overview

## What They Are
Cloud agents operate on the same fundamentals as local agents but execute in isolated VMs with complete development environments. They include "cloned repos, installed dependencies, secrets, startup commands, and network access."

## Where They Run
Cloud agents run in isolated virtual machines in the cloud rather than locally. These VMs have full development environments comparable to a laptop setup, enabling agents to build, test, and verify work.

## Launch Methods
Agents can be initiated from:
- Cursor iOS app
- cursor.com/agents (web interface)
- Cursor Desktop (Cloud dropdown option)
- Slack (@cursor command)
- GitHub/Bitbucket (comment @cursor on PR/issue)
- Linear (@cursor command)
- API

## Conversation Location
The page doesn't explicitly specify where conversations are stored, but mentions agents are "visible to members of the Cursor team they were started under" and can be shared via URL.

## Local Handoff
The page doesn't describe a direct "open in Cursor" or checkout-to-local workflow. It mentions agents "produce merge-ready PRs" as the handoff mechanism.

## Privacy/Modes
No privacy mode discussion appears in this content.

## Pricing & Availability
"Cloud Agents are charged at API pricing for the selected model." Requires a paid Cursor plan.

## Related Documentation Links
- Cloud agent capabilities
- Cloud agent setup
- Cloud Agent Builds
- Cloud Agent security
- OIDC tokens
- Agent metadata
- Cloud agent settings
```

```text
# Cloud Agent Builds Summary

## What Are Builds?

Builds are bootable snapshots of prepared Cloud Agent environments. As described, "A Build is a bootable snapshot of a prepared Cloud Agent environment. Cursor creates Builds ahead of agent runs and keeps the latest successful one ready to start."

## Key Benefits

- **Faster initialization**: Repository cloning and dependency setup occur beforehand
- **Reliability**: Agents boot from the most recent successful Build, preventing broken configurations from disrupting operations
- **Traceability**: Complete visibility into Build history, logs, and which Build each agent used

## Build Lifecycle

1. **Trigger** – Initiated by schedule, configuration save, manual request, or agent request
2. **Prepare** – System clones repositories at default branches and executes installation commands
3. **Snapshot** – Disk state is saved with environment version and exact commit SHAs
4. **Activate** – Successful Builds become the active environment
5. **Start agents** – New agents launch from the active Build

## Build Triggers

| Type | Timing |
|------|--------|
| **Recurring** | Regular schedule for every environment |
| **Configuration change** | When environment configuration or secrets are saved |
| **Manual** | User-initiated via Builds tab |
| **Agent-requested** | During agent testing or setup |

Recurring Builds may be **skipped** if nothing changed since the last completion (no new commits, no config/secret changes).

## Commands and Phases

| Command | Phase | Purpose |
|---------|-------|---------|
| **install** | During Build | Dependencies, code generation, compilation, cache warming |
| **start** | Agent startup | Docker, databases, tunnels, services |
| **terminals** | Agent startup | App processes in tmux terminals |

The install command must be idempotent and repeatable. Builds preserve only disk state—running processes, shell variables, and in-memory caches are not retained.

## Configuration Elements

Builds incorporate:
- Base images
- Dockerfiles
- `.cursor/environment.json` configuration
- Install and startup commands
- Team and environment secrets (not user secrets)
- Network settings
- Saved snapshots

## Git State Management

- **Default branch**: Agents start from the commit recorded in the active Build. If "Update stale builds" is enabled and the Build exceeds the staleness threshold (default 24 hours), agents pull latest code at startup
- **Feature branches**: Checked out after Build starts, reusing prepared dependencies
- **Multi-repo environments**: Each repository's commit is recorded and prepared together

## Secrets Handling

- Team and environment secrets are available during Builds
- User secrets are added only at agent startup, not during Builds
- Changing environment secrets triggers a new Build

## Snapshot and Dockerfile Relationship

Builds do not replace snapshots or Dockerfiles. Instead, "a saved snapshot or Dockerfile defines the base machine used to create a Build. Cursor then clones the repositories, runs `install`, and creates a fresh bootable snapshot."

## Management Features

The Builds tab provides:
- View Build history (type, status, start time)
- Inspect Build details and logs
- Manually trigger Builds
- Activate/deactivate Builds
- Cancel in-progress Builds
- Start agents from specific Builds
- Configure staleness settings

## Important Notes

- Builds apply only to Cursor-hosted Cloud Agents; self-hosted machines ignore Builds
- Failed Builds don't interrupt existing agent workflows
- Build creation is included with Cloud Agents (no additional cost)
- Agents can manage Builds via the Cursor Cloud MCP

## Related Documentation Links

- [Cloud Environment Setup](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/setup.md)
- [Cloud Agent capabilities](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/capabilities.md)
- [Cloud Agents settings](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/settings.md)
- [Self-Hosted Machines](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/self-hosted.md)
```

```text
# Cursor Cloud Agents: Web & Mobile Overview

## Web Access (cursor.com/agents)

The primary web interface at **cursor.com/agents** serves as the central hub for cloud agent management. This platform handles core administrative functions that remain web-only, including "Editor, terminal, and file browser" access, secrets configuration, MCP server management, source control setup, and billing/admin functions.

## Mobile Cloud Agents (Cursor for iOS)

The iOS app provides full cloud agent workflow capabilities on mobile devices. Users can "Start agents, follow their work in real time, and review and merge their pull requests" directly from iPhone or iPad.

## Launching Agents

**On Mobile:**
- Download from App Store (iOS 26.0+)
- Sign in with Cursor account
- Select repository and branch
- Send task to agent and supervise work

**Cross-Device Continuity:**
- Agents started anywhere appear in mobile inbox automatically
- Mobile agents show up in desktop Cloud Agents panel and cursor.com/agents
- Sessions can move between devices via "Move to Cloud" or Remote Control features

## Remote Control Feature

Enables directing desktop agents from mobile: Users run `/remote-control` on their computer, then direct the session from their phone while "tool calls run on your computer."

## Conversation & History

The app features a cache-first design where "chats in the sidebar" remain visible on iPad, with live work stream following and follow-up message capability during active agent runs.

## Related Documentation Links

- Cloud agents overview
- Cloud agent capabilities
- Cloud agent setup
- Security and network
- Cloud Agent self-hosted pool/My Machines
- GitHub/GitLab integration docs
- MCP documentation
- HIPAA Business Associate Agreements
- Privacy Mode details
```

```text
# Cursor CLI Summary

## Command Name
The primary command is `agent` (not `cursor-agent`).

## Core Modes
- **Agent**: Default mode with full tool access
- **Plan**: Design-focused with clarifying questions
- **Ask**: Read-only exploration mode

## Key Flags & Options
- `-p` or `-prompt`: Specify initial prompt
- `--model`: Select model (e.g., "gpt-5")
- `--mode`: Switch modes (plan, ask)
- `--output-format`: Set output type (text)
- `--sandbox`: Control execution settings (enabled/disabled)
- `--continue` / `--resume`: Resume previous sessions

## Headless/Print Mode
Described as "non-interactive mode" for scripts and CI pipelines. Commands execute without user approval at each step.

## Cloud Agent
Prepend `&` to messages to handoff tasks to Cloud Agent, continuing work remotely. Resume cloud tasks at cursor.com/agents.

## Session Management
- `agent ls`: List previous chats
- `agent resume`: Open latest conversation
- `agent --resume="chat-id"`: Resume specific session
Settings persist locally across sessions.

## Local Storage
The document doesn't explicitly specify where chats/transcripts are stored locally, only that "sessions" are resumable and "settings persist across sessions."

## Sub-page Links
Only one documented link: `/llms.txt` (sitemap overview). No links to dedicated headless, reference, or configuration documentation pages appear in this content.
```

 `https://cursor.com/docs/hooks`

```text
# Cursor Agent Hooks: Comprehensive Reference

## Hook Event Names

Cursor supports three categories of hooks:

**Agent Hooks** (triggered during Cmd+K/Agent Chat sessions):
- `sessionStart` / `sessionEnd` – Session lifecycle
- `preToolUse` / `postToolUse` / `postToolUseFailure` – Generic tool execution
- `subagentStart` / `subagentStop` – Task tool lifecycle
- `beforeShellExecution` / `afterShellExecution` – Shell command control
- `beforeMCPExecution` / `afterMCPExecution` – MCP tool usage
- `beforeReadFile` / `afterFileEdit` – File access and modifications
- `beforeSubmitPrompt` – Prompt validation
- `preCompact` – Context window compaction observation
- `stop` – Agent completion handling
- `afterAgentResponse` / `afterAgentThought` – Response tracking

**Tab Hooks** (autonomous inline completions):
- `beforeTabFileRead` – File access control
- `afterTabFileEdit` – Post-edit processing

**App Lifecycle Hooks** (outside agent sessions):
- `workspaceOpen` – Workspace initialization

## Configuration File Locations

Hooks are defined in `hooks.json` files at multiple levels (priority order: Enterprise → Team → Project → User):

- **Enterprise (system-wide)**: `/Library/Application Support/Cursor/hooks.json` (macOS); `/etc/cursor/hooks.json` (Linux/WSL); `C:\\ProgramData\\Cursor\\hooks.json` (Windows)
- **Team (cloud-distributed, Enterprise only)**: Configured via web dashboard
- **Project**: `<project-root>/.cursor/hooks.json`
- **User**: `~/.cursor/hooks.json`

Scripts execute from their respective directories: project hooks run from the project root; user hooks run from `~/.cursor/`.

## Payload Fields (Common Base)

All hooks receive these base fields in addition to hook-specific ones:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `conversation_id` | string | Stable ID across turns |
| `generation_id` | string | Changes per user message |
| `model` / `model_id` | string | Model information |
| `model_params` | array | Selected parameters (thinking, context, effort) |
| `hook_event_name` | string | Which hook is running |
| `cursor_version` | string | Application version |
| `workspace_roots` | string[] | Workspace folder paths |
| `user_email` | string \| null | Authenticated user, if available |
| `transcript_path` | string \| null | Conversation transcript location |

App lifecycle hooks (`workspaceOpen`) omit `conversation_id`, `generation_id`, `model`, and `transcript_path`.

## Cloud Agent Support

**Supported in cloud agents** (command-based hooks only):
- `beforeShellExecution`, `afterShellExecution`
- `beforeReadFile`, `afterFileEdit`
- `preToolUse`, `postToolUse`, `postToolUseFailure`
- `subagentStart`, `subagentStop`
- `beforeSubmitPrompt`, `preCompact`
- `afterAgentResponse`, `afterAgentThought`
- `stop`

**Not available in cloud agents**:
- `sessionStart` / `sessionEnd` – "Deferred while cloud agents can still start in a read-only environment"
- `beforeMCPExecution` / `afterMCPExecution` – Similar timing concerns
- `beforeTabFileRead` / `afterTabFileEdit` – Tab is an IDE feature only
- `workspaceOpen` – IDE lifecycle hook

Cloud agents load hooks from `.cursor/hooks.json` in your repository; they do not access user-level `~/.cursor/hooks.json`. Enterprise deployments also support team and enterprise-managed hooks.

## Background Agent Behavior

The `sessionStart` hook input includes `is_background_agent` field to distinguish interactive sessions from background executions. However, specific details about hook availability in background mode are not extensively detailed in the documentation.

## CLI Support

The documentation mentions "Cursor desktop app and CLI" in relation to `workspaceOpen` hooks, indicating CLI support exists, though detailed CLI-specific hook behavior is not fully specified.

## Hook Execution Types

- **Command-based** (default): Shell scripts receiving JSON via stdin, returning JSON via stdout
- **Prompt-based**: LLM-evaluated conditions using natural language (not available in cloud agents due to authentication requirements)

Exit code `2` blocks actions; other non-zero codes fail open by default unless `failClosed: true` is configured.
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
116	            this.logger?.log(LogLevels.WARN, 'Absolute history paths not allowed, using default');
117	            return DEFAULT_OUTPUT_PATH;

119

125	            );
```

```text
49	        alias: 'deepseek',
50	        name: 'DeepSeek TUI',

55	/**
56	 * Returns true when every enabled provider has `type === 'ide'`,
57	 * meaning no CLI binary is needed on the remote machine.
58	 */
59	export function hasOnlyIdeProviders(): boolean {
60	    const enabled = vscode.workspace
61	        .getConfiguration('specstory.providers')
62	        .get<Record<string, boolean>>('enabled', {});
63	    const enabledProviders = Object.values(providersMap).filter(
64	        (provider) => enabled[provider.name] !== false
65	    );
66	    // If no providers are enabled, do not treat this as "only IDE providers".
67	    if (enabledProviders.length === 0) {
68	        return false;
69	    }
70	    return enabledProviders.every((p) => p.type === 'ide');
71	}
72	
73	/**
74	 * Returns the alias values (used as session.provider) for all enabled providers.
75	 * Providers can be enabled/disabled via the specstory.providers.enabled setting.
76	 * - Returns `undefined` when all providers are disabled
77	 * - Returns a non-empty comma-separated string when one or more providers are enabled.
78	 * - Returns an empty string when all providers are enabled.
79	 */
80	export function getEnabledProvidersArg(): string | undefined {
81	    const enabled = vscode.workspace
82	        .getConfiguration('specstory.providers')
83	        .get<Record<string, boolean>>('enabled', {});
84	    const providers = Object.values(providersMap);
85	    // Return undefined if all providers are disabled
86	    if (providers.every((provider) => enabled[provider.name] === false)) {
87	        return undefined;
88	    }
89	    // Return empty string if all providers are enabled
90	    if (providers.every((provider) => enabled[provider.name] !== false)) {
91	        return '';
92	    }
93	    return providers
94	        .filter((provider) => enabled[provider.name] !== false)
95	        .map((provider) => provider.alias)
96	        .join(',');
97	}
98	
99	/**
100	 * Map the host IDE to the CLI provider ID used by `--user-data-dir`.
101	 * The CLI currently accepts overrides for `cursoride` and `copilotide` only.
102	 */
103	function getIdeProviderIdForHost(): 'cursoride' | 'copilotide' | null {
104	    const appName = vscode.env.appName.toLowerCase();
105	    if (appName === 'cursor') {
106	        return 'cursoride';
107	    }
108	    if (
109	        appName === 'visual studio code' ||
110	        appName === 'visual studio code - insiders' ||
111	        appName === 'vscode' ||
112	        appName === 'vscode-insiders' ||
113	        appName === 'code - oss' ||
114	        appName === 'code-oss'
115	    ) {
116	        return 'copilotide';
117	    }
118	    return null;
119	}
120	
121	/**
122	 * Derive the `--user-data-dir <providerId>:<path>` args from the extension's
123	 * global storage path. VS Code's `globalStorageUri` is always
124	 * `<userDataDir>/User/globalStorage/<extensionId>`, so the user-data-dir is
125	 * three levels up. We always pass this (when the host is a supported IDE) so
126	 * the CLI uses the same data directory the IDE is actually running with,
127	 * regardless of whether the user launched with a custom `--user-data-dir`.
128	 */
129	export function getUserDataDirArgs(context: vscode.ExtensionContext): string[] {
130	    const providerId = getIdeProviderIdForHost();
131	    if (!providerId) {
132	        return [];
133	    }
134	    const globalStoragePath = context.globalStorageUri.fsPath;
135	    const userDataDir = path.dirname(path.dirname(path.dirname(globalStoragePath)));
136	    if (!userDataDir) {
137	        return [];
138	    }
139	    return ['--user-data-dir', `${providerId}:${userDataDir}`];
140	}
```

```text
    10	export type DatabaseTable = 'ItemTable' | 'cursorDiskKV';
    11	
    12	export class DatabaseService {
    13	    static loadDatabaseTable(
    14	        dbPath: string,
    15	        table: DatabaseTable = 'ItemTable',
    16	        keys?: string | string[]
    17	    ): Promise<Map<string, unknown> | undefined> {
    18	        let query = `SELECT * FROM ${table} WHERE value IS NOT NULL`;
    19	        let params: string[] = [];
    20	
    21	        if (typeof keys === 'string') {
    22	            query += ` AND key = ?`;
    23	            params = [keys];
    24	        } else if (Array.isArray(keys) && keys.length > 0) {
    25	            query += ` AND key IN (${keys.map(() => '?').join(',')})`;
    26	            params = keys;
    27	        }
    28	
    29	        return this.loadFromDatabase(dbPath, query, params);
    30	    }
    31	
    32	    /**
    33	     * Load Cursor conversation data from the database.
    34	     *
    35	     * For each composerId, we INCLUDE:
    36	     * - composerData:{composerId} (exact match, uses index)
    37	     * - bubbleId:{composerId}:* (prefix match with LIKE, uses index)
    38	     *
    39	     * We intentionally SKIP these key prefixes (not needed for rendering):
    40	     * - checkpointId:{composerId}:*
    41	     * - messageRequestContext:{composerId}:*
    42	     * - codeBlockDiff:{composerId}:*
    43	     * - codeBlockPartialInlineDiffFates:{composerId}:*
    44	     */
    45	    static loadCursorConversationData(
    46	        dbPath: string,
    47	        conversationIds: string[]
    48	    ): Promise<Map<string, unknown> | undefined> {
    49	        // If no specific IDs requested, return all non-null values
    50	        if (conversationIds.length === 0) {
    51	            const query = `SELECT * FROM cursorDiskKV WHERE value IS NOT NULL`;
    52	            return this.loadFromDatabase(dbPath, query);
    53	        }
    54	
    55	        // Build query with two parts:
    56	        // 1. Exact matches for composerData:{id} using IN clause (uses index)
    57	        // 2. Prefix matches for bubbleId:{id}:% using LIKE (uses index - no leading wildcard)
    58	
    59	        // Part 1: composerData exact matches
    60	        const composerDataPlaceholders = conversationIds.map(() => '?').join(',');
    61	
    62	        // Part 2: bubbleId prefix matches (LIKE 'prefix%' can use index)
    63	        const bubbleIdConditions = conversationIds.map(() => 'key LIKE ?').join(' OR ');
    64	
    65	        const query = `SELECT * FROM cursorDiskKV WHERE value IS NOT NULL AND (
    66	            key IN (${composerDataPlaceholders})
    67	            OR (${bubbleIdConditions})
    68	        )`;
    69	
    70	        // Build params array: first all composerData keys, then all bubbleId prefixes
    71	        const params = [
    72	            ...conversationIds.map(id => `composerData:${id}`),
    73	            ...conversationIds.map(id => `bubbleId:${id}:%`),
    74	        ];
    75	
    76	        return this.loadFromDatabase(dbPath, query, params);
    77	    }
    78	
    79	    private static loadFromDatabase(
    80	        dbPath: string,
    81	        query: string,
    82	        params?: string[]
    83	    ): Promise<Map<string, unknown> | undefined> {
    84	        const logger = LoggingService.getInstance();
    85	        
    86	        return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    87	            const data = new Map<string, unknown>();
    88	            
    89	            // First open the database in read-only mode
    90	            logger.log(LogLevels.DEBUG, `Opening database in read-only mode: ${dbPath}`);
    91	            const db = new sqlite3.Database(dbPath, sqlite3.OPEN_READONLY, (err: unknown) => {
    92	                if (err) {
    93	                    logger.log(LogLevels.ERROR, `Failed to open database`, { path: dbPath }, err as Error);
    94	                    reject(err);
    95	                    return;
    96	                }
    97	                
    98	                // Check if the database is in WAL mode
    99	                db.get('PRAGMA journal_mode;', [], (err: unknown, result: { journal_mode: string }) => {
   100	                    if (err) {
   101	                        logger.log(LogLevels.ERROR, 'Failed to check journal mode', {}, err as Error);
   102	                        db.close();
   103	                        reject(err);
   104	                        return;
   105	                    }
   106	                    
   107	                    const journalMode = result?.journal_mode?.toUpperCase();
   108	                    logger.log(LogLevels.DEBUG, `Current journal mode: ${journalMode}`, { path: dbPath });
   109	                    
   110	                    if (journalMode === 'WAL') {
   111	                        // Database is already in WAL mode, proceed with query
   112	                        return executeQuery(db);
   113	                    } else {
   114	                        // Need to set WAL mode - close read-only connection
   115	                        logger.log(LogLevels.DEBUG, `Setting database to WAL mode`, { path: dbPath });
   116	                        db.close((closeErr: unknown) => {
   117	                            if (closeErr) {
   118	                                logger.log(LogLevels.ERROR, 'Failed to close database', {}, closeErr as Error);
   119	                                reject(closeErr);
   120	                                return;
   121	                            }
   122	                            
   123	                            // Reopen in read/write mode to set WAL mode
   124	                            const rwDb = new sqlite3.Database(dbPath, sqlite3.OPEN_READWRITE, (rwErr: unknown) => {
   125	                                if (rwErr) {
   126	                                    logger.log(LogLevels.ERROR, 'Failed to open database in read/write mode', {}, rwErr as Error);
   127	                                    reject(rwErr);
   128	                                    return;
   129	                                }
   130	                                
   131	                                // Set WAL mode
   132	                                rwDb.exec('PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;', (walErr: unknown) => {
   133	                                    if (walErr) {
   134	                                        logger.log(LogLevels.ERROR, 'Failed to set WAL mode', {}, walErr as Error);
   135	                                        rwDb.close();
   136	                                        reject(walErr);
   137	                                        return;
   138	                                    }
   139	                                    
   140	                                    logger.log(LogLevels.DEBUG, 'Successfully set database to WAL mode', { path: dbPath });
   141	                                    
   142	                                    // Close the read/write connection
   143	                                    rwDb.close((rwCloseErr: unknown) => {
   144	                                        if (rwCloseErr) {
   145	                                            logger.log(LogLevels.ERROR, 'Failed to close r/w database', {}, rwCloseErr as Error);
   146	                                            reject(rwCloseErr);
   147	                                            return;
   148	                                        }
   149	                                        
   150	                                        // Reopen in read-only mode
   151	                                        logger.log(LogLevels.DEBUG, 'Reopening database in read-only mode after WAL mode change');
   152	                                        const roDb = new sqlite3.Database(dbPath, sqlite3.OPEN_READONLY, (roErr: unknown) => {
   153	                                            if (roErr) {
   154	                                                logger.log(LogLevels.ERROR, 'Failed to reopen database in read-only mode', {}, roErr as Error);
   155	                                                reject(roErr);
   156	                                                return;
   157	                                            }
   158	                                            
   159	                                            // Now execute the original query
   160	                                            return executeQuery(roDb);
   161	                                        });
   162	                                    });
   163	                                });
   164	                            });
   165	                        });
   166	                    }
   167	                });
   168	            });
   169	            
   170	            // Function to execute the original query
   171	            function executeQuery(database: any) { // eslint-disable-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
   172	                database.all(query, params, (err: unknown, rows: any) => { // eslint-disable-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
   173	                    if (err) {
   174	                        logger.log(LogLevels.ERROR, 'Error executing query', { query }, err as Error);
   175	                        database.close();
   176	                        reject(err);
   177	                        return;
   178	                    }
   179	                    
   180	                    rows.forEach((row: any) => { // eslint-disable-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
   181	                        try {
   182	                            data.set(row.key.toString(), JSON.parse(row.value.toString()));
   183	                        } catch {
   184	                            data.set(row.key.toString(), row.value.toString());
   185	                        }
   186	                    });
   187	
   188	                    database.close((err: unknown) => {
   189	                        if (err) {
   190	                            logger.log(LogLevels.ERROR, 'Error closing database', {}, err as Error);
   191	                            reject(err);
   192	                            return;
   193	                        }
   194	                        logger.log(LogLevels.DEBUG, 'Successfully completed database operation', { path: dbPath });
   195	                        resolve(data);
   196	                    });
   197	                });
   198	            }
   199	        });
   200	    }
   201	}
```

````text
# Cloud Environment Setup Reference

## `.cursor/environment.json` Schema

The configuration file supports these fields:

```json
{
  "snapshot": "snapshot-id",
  "build": {
    "dockerfile": "Dockerfile",
    "context": ".."
  },
  "install": "npm install",
  "start": "command",
  "terminals": ["process1", "process2"]
}
```

**Path behavior**: Dockerfile and context paths are relative to `.cursor`. When omitted, context defaults to `.cursor`. Special values (`.`, `./`, `..`) reference the repository root instead of `.cursor`. The install command runs from your project root.

## Install Script

The install script (the `install` field) runs during Build creation and must be **idempotent**. It executes before agent startup, making it ideal for dependency installation, code generation, and artifact compilation. Running processes and shell variables don't persist to the agent run.

## Startup Commands

After booting from a Build, Cursor executes the `start` command followed by `terminals`. These are intended for "long-running processes that should stay alive while the agent runs." Avoid placing services like Docker or databases in the install script; use startup commands instead.

## Snapshots

Environments can reference a snapshot ID: `"snapshot": "snapshot-20260212-..."`. This captures the disk state from a previous environment configuration.

## Secrets & Environment Variables

Secrets are exposed as environment variables through the Cursor dashboard. The documentation mentions "environment-scoped secrets" that apply only to specific environments and never reach self-hosted machines.

**AWS IAM Integration**: When configured, Cursor sets `AWS_PROFILE=cursor-cloud-agent`, `AWS_CONFIG_FILE`, and `AWS_SDK_LOAD_CONFIG=1`. Role credentials expire after 1 hour and refresh automatically.

## Base Image & User

The environment runs on Ubuntu machines. The recommended Dockerfile configuration creates an `ubuntu` non-root user with passwordless sudo access and Docker group membership.

## Network Access

Cloud agents can reach external services by default. Connectivity options include:
- **Tailscale**: Requires userspace networking mode (`--tun=userspace-networking`)
- **Cloudflare Tunnel**: Supported natively; runs in userspace

## What Persists

Only disk state persists between agent runs. Running processes, exported variables, and in-memory caches do not continue into subsequent agent sessions.

## GitHub Connection

During setup, users connect GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, or Bitbucket accounts and select repositories for cloning into the agent machine.

## Arbitrary Scripts & Background Processes

Background services belong in the `start` command or `terminals` configuration, not in the install script. The documentation specifies: "Keep long-running processes out of `install`."
````

```text
# Cloud Agent Features: Key Capabilities

Based on the provided documentation, here are the main features:

## Viewing & Following Agents
The page references a Cloud Agents dashboard and agents list but doesn't detail how to view or follow agents specifically.

## Computer Use & Desktop Control
Agents operate in isolated VMs with full desktop environments. Users can "take control of the agent's remote desktop to interact with the software the agent is building" and return control to let the agent continue working.

## Artifacts & Demonstrations
Agents create "screenshots, videos, and log references" attached to PRs. The dashboard allows opting into embedding artifacts directly in GitHub PRs using "long, unguessable URLs that are viewable without authentication."

## PR Creation & CI Management
Cloud Agents automatically attempt to fix GitHub Actions CI failures in their PRs. This auto-fix feature can be disabled via dashboard settings or per-PR with `@cursor autofix off` comments.

## Subscriptions & Follow-ups
Agents can subscribe to events and continue working autonomously—monitoring "Pull request activity (comments, reviews, and lifecycle changes)," Slack threads, Linear issues, or timers. Subscriptions last "at most 180 days."

## MCP Tools & Integrations
Agents access external tools via MCP servers (HTTP or stdio transport). A built-in "Cursor Cloud MCP" provides diagnostics without manual log collection.

## Runtime & Network
The documentation provided doesn't specify maximum runtime duration or internet access policies.

**Note:** Details about local IDE handoff, conversation storage, and checkout procedures aren't covered in this excerpt.
```

```text
# Cloud Agents Security & Network Summary

## VM Isolation
Each agent operates in dedicated infrastructure: "Every agent gets a dedicated environment, isolated from other agents and other users." Agents run on "Firecracker-based microVM infrastructure" with "a separate AWS account from the rest of Cursor's production infrastructure."

## Internet & Egress Access
Internet connectivity is enabled by default but configurable. Organizations can "Restrict outbound traffic to a default set plus your allowlist, or to your allowlist only." Enterprise admins may "lock the policy org-wide."

## Secrets Storage
Credentials are "encrypted at rest with KMS, encrypted in transit, and injected as environment variables at runtime." Sensitive values marked as Runtime Secrets are "kept out of the transcript, tool output, and commits."

## Data Retention
- **Runtime workspace**: Automatically recycled after runs idle
- **VM snapshots**: Deleted automatically after 90 days of inactivity
- **Conversation state**: "Kept indefinitely by default so you can revisit and resume runs; deletable on demand"
- **Secrets/tokens**: Retained until manually removed

## Privacy Mode
Cloud Agents operate under Privacy Mode, where "Cursor never trains on code accessed by Cloud Agents or on the prompts and responses their runs generate." Conversations remain stored in backend systems (encrypted per-agent).

## Access Control
"A Cloud Agent can only reach repositories the triggering user could already reach." Admins can implement Protected Git Scopes or repository blocklists for additional restrictions.

## Auto-Run Commands
Agents operate autonomously, executing terminal commands without per-step approval—a higher autonomy model requiring compensating controls like egress restrictions and draft PR reviews.
```

```text
# Cloud Agents Settings Summary

## Admin & Team Controls

**Default Settings:**
- Default model selection for runs without specified models
- Default repository assignment (optional; users choose if blank)
- Base branch configuration for pull requests

**Team Feature Settings:**
- "Long running agents" – admins control extended-duration capabilities
- "Computer use" – restricted to enterprise teams only

## Privacy & Visibility

**Display Controls:**
- Agent summary display toggling (file diffs, code snippets, file paths)
- External channel summary sharing for Slack and connected platforms

**Team Follow-ups Configuration:**
Three administrative options govern colleague message-sending to others' agents:
- *Disabled*: "Only the original creator can send follow-ups"
- *Service accounts only*: Follow-ups permitted only to service-account agents
- *All*: "Any team member can send follow-ups to any agent on the team"

## Repository & Network Access

**Environment Scoping:**
Environments apply to "one repo or to a group of repos"

**Network Restrictions:**
Three modes—allow all, default plus allowlist, or allowlist-only domains

## Security Considerations

The documentation emphasizes that "a user can influence the execution of a cloud agent that runs with *another user's* secrets and credentials" when team follow-ups are enabled, presenting escalation risks equivalent to "shared SSH keys or service credentials."
```

```text
# Agent Metadata in Cloud Agents

## What Agent Metadata Is

Agent metadata provides key-value information about the current run accessible from inside the Cloud Agent VM. It's served via a local Unix socket and includes details about the agent, owner, turn, and workspace.

## Environment Variables and Socket Access

The primary way to access metadata is through the Unix socket specified by `CURSOR_AGENT_SOCKET`, which defaults to `/run/cursor/api.sock` on Cursor-managed VMs.

**Key points:**
- "Requests are HTTP over a Unix socket. The hostname in the URL is ignored."
- Access requires `GET /v1/meta-data[/<path>]` requests
- The socket serves both metadata and OIDC tokens

## Available Metadata Categories

**Agent Information:**
- `agent/id` - Cloud Agent identifier (always present)
- `agent/name` - Dashboard display name
- `agent/source` - How agent started (e.g., WEBSITE, API, SLACK)
- `agent/runtime` - Returns `managed` for Cursor-managed VMs

**Owner Details:**
- `owner/user-id`, `owner/user-email`, `owner/service-account-id`, `owner/team-id`

**Turn Information** (only during active coding turns):
- `turn/id`, `turn/user-id`, `turn/user-email`, `turn/started-at`, `turn/model`

**Workspace Data:**
- `workspace/repo-url`, `workspace/repo-urls`, `workspace/branch-name`, `workspace/environment-id`, `workspace/automation-id`

## Rate Limits and Error Handling

The system allows "**120** metadata requests per minute, in bursts of up to 20" per VM, with maximum 8 concurrent connections. Missing keys return `404`; rate-limit errors return `429`.
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
# Self-Hosted Machines for Cloud Agents: Key Details

## How It Works

Self-Hosted Machines relocate Cloud Agent execution to your infrastructure while maintaining the user experience through Cursor's desktop app, web interface, and mobile platform. The architecture divides responsibilities: "Cursor runs the agent loop, inference, and planning. Your worker performs file edits and terminal commands."

## What Runs on Your Machine

The worker operates as a daemon through the Cursor CLI. Installation is straightforward:

> "curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash"

For pool workers, you run this as a long-lived process using systemd, launchd, Docker, or other process managers. The worker establishes an outbound connection to Cursor's backend, receiving agent tool calls and transmitting results back.

## Local Storage and Data

Your machine retains sensitive information: "The full checkout, build cache, and machine-local credentials stay on your machine." During execution, the worker sends Cursor only operational data—file contents, terminal output, diffs, screenshots, and routing metadata.

Conversation transcripts and agent artifacts (screenshots, videos, logs) are uploaded to "Cursor-managed storage so they can appear in pull requests and the dashboard." However, actual conversation history appears to remain in Cursor's cloud systems, not locally.

## Network Requirements

Workers need outbound HTTPS access to two endpoints:
- `api2.cursor.sh` and `api2direct.cursor.sh` for agent sessions
- `cloud-agent-artifacts.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` for artifact uploads

Notably: "No inbound ports, public IPs, or VPN tunnels are required."

## Two Deployment Models

**My Machines** suits personal workflows—connecting individual machines to your account with personal credentials.

**Team Pools** serves enterprise needs with shared capacity and service account authentication, allowing you to "select in the Cursor client UI" and route requests to appropriate workers.
```

```text
# Headless CLI Extraction

## Flags & Modes
- **Print mode**: `-p, --print` for "non-interactive scripting and automation"
- **Force flag**: `--force` (or `--yolo`) to "modify files in scripts"
- Note: "Without --force, changes are only proposed, not applied"

## Output Formats
- `text` - "clean, final-answer-only responses" (default with `--print`)
- `json` - "structured analysis"
- `stream-json` - "message-level progress tracking"
- `--stream-partial-output` - "incremental streaming of deltas"

## Authentication & Setup
- `export CURSOR_API_KEY=your_api_key_here` for script authentication
- Installation scripts provided for macOS/Linux/WSL and Windows PowerShell

## Notable Limitations
- No mentions of `--cloud`, cloud agent capabilities, `&` prefix, resume functionality, or local session storage locations in this content
```

```text
# Cursor Agent CLI Reference

## Global Flags

- `-v, --version` — Display version number
- `--api-key <key>` — API key for authentication (supports `CURSOR_API_KEY` environment variable)
- `-H, --header <header>` — Add custom headers to requests (repeatable)
- `-p, --print` — Output responses to console with full tool access
- `--output-format <format>` — Choose `text`, `json`, or `stream-json` (default: `text`)
- `--stream-partial-output` — Stream text deltas individually
- `--resume [chatId]` — Reopen a previous chat session
- `--continue` — Alias for `--resume=-1` (latest session)
- `--model <model>` — Specify which model to use
- `--mode <mode>` — Set `plan` or `ask` mode
- `--plan` — Shorthand for `--mode=plan`
- `--list-models` — Show available models
- `-f, --force` / `--yolo` — Allow commands without denial restrictions
- `--sandbox <mode>` — Enable or disable sandbox isolation
- `--approve-mcps` — Auto-approve MCP servers
- `--trust` — Skip prompts in headless mode
- `--workspace <path>` — Specify workspace directory
- `--plugin-dir <path>` — Load local plugins (repeatable)
- `-w, --worktree [name]` — Create Git worktree under `~/.cursor/worktrees/<reponame>/<name>`
- `--worktree-base <branch>` — Base branch for new worktree
- `--skip-worktree-setup` — Skip worktree setup scripts
- `-h, --help` — Display command help

## Session Management Commands

- `ls` — "Resume a chat session"
- `resume` — Reopen the latest chat
- `create-chat` — Generate new empty chat and return ID
- `--resume [chatId]` — Resume specific chat by ID

## Output Format Options

- `text` — Default human-readable output
- `json` — Structured JSON response
- `stream-json` — Streaming JSON with partial deltas
```

```text
# Cursor Admin API: Endpoints, Auth, and Data Exposure

## Authentication & Access
The Admin API uses "Basic Authentication with your API key as the username." Team API keys support scope-based access (`read:*`, `admin:*`, `models:read`, `models:*`), with reads generally requiring `read:*` and writes requiring `admin:*`.

## Core Endpoints & Data Exposed

**Team Management:**
- `GET /teams/members` - Returns member IDs, emails, names, roles, removal status
- `POST /teams/remove-member` - Remove users by ID or email
- `POST /teams/user-spend-limit` - Set individual spending caps (Enterprise)
- `POST /teams/user-spend-limits` - Bulk spending limit updates (Enterprise, Preview)

**Usage & Spending Data:**
- `POST /teams/daily-usage-data` - Daily metrics including lines added/deleted, AI applies/accepts, feature usage (Tab, Composer, Chat, Agent), model preference, client version
- `POST /teams/spend` - Current cycle spending by user with per-user limits and overrides
- `POST /teams/filtered-usage-events` - Granular events with "timestamp, userEmail, model, maxMode, token usage, chargedCents" and optional fields for service accounts, cloud agents, automations, and conversations

**Audit & Compliance:**
- `GET /teams/audit-logs` - Team activity filtered by date, event type, user, with 30-day limit per request

**Repository Controls:**
- `GET /settings/repo-blocklists/repos` - Configured repository blocklists with glob patterns
- `POST /settings/repo-blocklists/repos/upsert` - Add/update blocklists
- `DELETE /settings/repo-blocklists/repos/:repoId` - Remove blocklist

## Agent & Automation Data

The `/teams/filtered-usage-events` endpoint exposes:
- `cloudAgentId` - References cloud agent run attribution
- `automationId` - UUID linking usage to automations
- `conversationId` - Session identifier for "join key with other sources that expose conversation IDs"
- `isHeadless` - Distinguishes background agent requests
- `hostingType` filter - Isolates self-hosted vs. Cursor-hosted inference spend

Service account usage includes `serviceAccountId` and `serviceAccountName` fields.

## Group & Model Access

**Directory Groups** (`/teams/directory-groups`):
- Create, list, update, delete teams' directory groups
- Manage membership (bulk add/remove)
- Set per-group spending limits

**Billing Groups** (`/teams/groups`):
- List groups with current cycle spend and daily spend breakdowns
- Track current and former members with per-member spend

**Model Access** (Preview):
- Control provider/model enablement per team
- Configure parameter restrictions (reasoning effort, Fast mode, caching)
- Set defaults for new models

## Grok Bot Administration

- `POST /grok-bot/enable` & `POST /grok-bot/disable`
- `GET/PATCH /grok-bot/capabilities` - Cloud agents, template sharing, action recording, local execution
- `GET/PUT /grok-bot/auto-review` - Enforce Auto-Review with allow/block rules
- `GET/PUT /grok-bot/access` - Limit bot access to selected billing groups
- `GET/PUT /grok-bot/network` - Egress allowlist and policy locking
- `GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /grok-bot/team-rules` - Custom behavior instructions
- `GET/PUT/DELETE /grok-bot/setup-manifests` - Installation scripts

## Plan Availability

Most endpoints are available on Enterprise plans. Usage data endpoints exist across tiers; spending limits and bulk operations typically require Enterprise. Grok Bot features return `403` when unavailable to the team.

**Rate Limits:** Most endpoints allow 20 requests/minute per team; filtered usage events allow 60 requests/minute.
```

```text
I found comprehensive information about the Cursor Cloud Agents API. Here are the key findings:

## API Overview

The Cursor Cloud Agents API allows you to create and manage Cursor Cloud Agents programmatically with a run-based REST API.

## Conversation Endpoint

The conversation endpoint (GET /v0/agents/{id}/conversation) returns conversation history including user prompts and assistant responses, with message objects containing id, type (user_message or assistant_message), and text.

## Available v0/agents Endpoints

The v0/agents endpoints include:
- GET /v0/agents – List agents
- POST /v0/agents – Launch an agent
- GET /v0/agents/{id} – Agent status
- DELETE /v0/agents/{id} – Delete an agent
- GET /v0/agents/{id}/conversation – Agent conversation
- POST /v0/agents/{id}/followup – Add follow-up
- POST /v0/agents/{id}/stop – Stop an agent

## Authentication

The API is located at https://api.cursor.com/v1 with documentation at https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints, and authentication uses HTTP Basic Authentication with an API key generated in Cursor settings, using the key as the username with an empty password.
```

```text
Based on the search results from forum.cursor.com and related sources, here's what I found regarding background agents, cloud agents, and conversation transcript export/sync capabilities:

## Feature Requests for Export & Sync

There is a feature request to export conversations from a background agent in Cursor Web and paste it in Cursor to continue working locally. 

Users have reported that when opening the same project on different machines, the Agents list is empty, though transcript files are stored locally in the workspace under .cursor/projects/…/agent-transcripts/. A feature request exists to sync the Agent list with the workspace, so that when opening a project, agent-transcripts are displayed in the Agents panel on any machine.

Another request is for export/import functionality to allow exporting Agent chat lists and content to a file for cloud backup or migration across devices.

## Known Limitations with Export

When exporting chat transcripts, agent tool calls like terminal commands and file edits are not included—only the text parts of the conversation are exported.

Background agent conversations are stored in a remote database, separate from local history.

## Third-Party Solutions

A community tool called "cursaves" exports Cursor conversations to a private git repo by reading SQLite databases and compressing conversations as JSON snapshots, then can import them on another machine.
```

```text
Based on the search results, here's where Cursor CLI agent chats and transcripts are stored:

## Cursor CLI Agent Chat Storage Locations

CLI chats live under ~/.cursor/chats and resume via cursor-agent --resume <id>.

## Cursor Agent Transcripts (IDE)

Cursor stores all agent conversation transcripts in a centralized location (~/.cursor/projects//agent-transcripts/).

## Storage Map Summary

Agent transcript files are stored at ~/.cursor/projects/**/agent-transcripts/**/*.jsonl, while CLI Store files are at ~/.cursor/chats/**/store.db.

## Key Distinction

IDE chats live in the editor index / agent-transcripts (composer/conversation id), while CLI chats live under ~/.cursor/chats. These don't sync — the CLI and IDE maintain separate session stores.
```

```text
--grep
# Extension Architecture for Remote Workspaces

This document explains how the SpecStory CLI and VS Code extension work together across different workspace types (local, WSL, SSH remote), including the architectural decisions and trade-offs.

## Overview

The SpecStory extension can run in two modes:
- **Standalone CLI**: Run manually by users from command line
- **Extension-Integrated**: Run automatically by VS Code extension

Both modes must handle conversations from different tools stored in different locations, with different accessibility depending on where the CLI executes.

## Data Locality: Where Conversations Are Stored

Understanding where each tool stores its data is critical to the architecture:

### IDE Tools (Stored on Client Machine)

These tools always store conversations on the Windows client, even when working with remote workspaces:

| Tool | Storage Location | Accessible From |
|------|------------------|-----------------|
| **Cursor IDE** | `%APPDATA%\Cursor\User\workspaceStorage\{workspace-id}\state.vscdb` | Windows client only |
| **Copilot IDE** | `%APPDATA%\Code\User\workspaceStorage\{workspace-id}\chatSessions\*.jsonl` | Windows client only |

**Why on client?** These are VS Code/Cursor IDE extensions that run in UI mode on the client machine. Their storage follows the IDE, not the workspace.

### CLI/Agent Tools (Stored on Execution Machine)

These tools store conversations wherever they execute:

| Tool | Storage Location | Accessible From |
|------|------------------|-----------------|
| **Claude Code** | `~/.claude/projects/{project-name}/*.jsonl` | Machine where agent runs |
| **Cursor CLI** | `~/.cursor/chats/*.json` | Machine where CLI runs |
| **Gemini CLI** | `~/.gemini/tmp/{project-hash}/*.jsonl` | Machine where CLI runs |

**Why on execution machine?** These are CLI tools that run in terminals. They store data locally on whichever machine executes them.

## Architecture Decision: Run CLI on Client (Locally)

We decided to **always run the CLI on the Windows client** (where the extension runs), not on remote machines. Here's why:

### ✅ Advantages of Running Locally

1. **Direct access to IDE tool data** (Cursor IDE, Copilot IDE)
   - These are typically the primary conversation sources
   - Data is always on the client
   - No network access needed

2. **Single code path** for all workspace types
   - Same logic for local, WSL, and SSH workspaces
   - Simpler to maintain and debug

3. **No SSH access required**
   - CLI doesn't need SSH credentials
   - No additional authentication complexity

4. **Works with company VPNs/firewalls**
   - Some environments restrict SSH
   - Local execution always works

### ❌ Disadvantages of Running Locally

1. **Cannot access CLI/Agent tools on remote machines**
   - Claude Code conversations created on SSH remote are inaccessible
   - Would need separate mechanism to fetch remote agent data

### Why Not Run on Remote?

Running the CLI on a remote SSH machine creates significant problems:

#### SSH Remote: Major Issues ❌

| Aspect | Problem |
|--------|---------|
| **IDE Data Access** | Remote machine cannot access Windows `%APPDATA%` (no network path) |
| **Authentication** | Need SSH credentials, key management |
| **CLI Distribution** | Must copy CLI binary to remote machine |
| **Extension Complexity** | Need to spawn remote commands, handle SSH connections |
```

````text
# Cloud Agents API v1 Endpoints Reference

## Authentication
All endpoints accept Basic auth (`-u YOUR_API_KEY:`) or Bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`). Generate keys from [Cursor Dashboard → API Keys](https://cursor.com/dashboard/api) or use service account keys.

---

## Agent Management

### Create An Agent
**POST** `/v1/agents`

Launches a cloud agent and enqueues its initial run. Returns both the durable `agent` object and initial `run`.

**Auth:** User or service account API key

**Request Body (JSON):**
```json
{
  "prompt": {
    "text": "Add a README with setup instructions",
    "images": [
      {
        "url": "https://example.com/image.png"
      }
    ]
  },
  "model": {
    "id": "composer-2",
    "params": [
      { "id": "fast", "value": "true" }
    ]
  },
  "name": "Add README",
  "repos": [
    {
      "url": "https://github.com/your-org/your-repo",
      "startingRef": "main",
      "prUrl": "https://github.com/your-org/your-repo/pull/123"
    }
  ],
  "workOnCurrentBranch": false,
  "autoCreatePR": true,
  "skipReviewerRequest": false,
  "envVars": {
    "API_KEY": "secret-value"
  },
  "mcpServers": [
    {
      "name": "linear",
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.linear.app/sse",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer TOKEN"
      }
    }
  ],
  "customSubagents": [
    {
      "name": "reviewer",
      "description": "Code reviewer",
      "prompt": "Review this code",
      "model": "composer-2"
    }
  ],
  "mode": "agent",
  "agentId": "bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
}
```

**Response (201):**
```json
{
  "agent": {
    "id": "bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
    "name": "Add README with setup instructions",
    "status": "ACTIVE",
    "env": {
      "type": "cloud"
    },
    "repos": [
      {
        "url": "https://github.com/your-org/your-repo",
        "startingRef": "main"
      }
    ],
    "workOnCurrentBranch": false,
    "autoCreatePR": true,
    "url": "https://cursor.com/agents/bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
    "createdAt": "2026-04-13T18:30:00.000Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-04-13T18:30:00.000Z",
    "latestRunId": "run-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
  },
  "run": {
    "id": "run-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
    "agentId": "bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
    "status": "CREATING",
    "createdAt": "2026-04-13T18:30:00.000Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-04-13T18:30:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

**Key Parameters:**
- `prompt.text` (required): Task instruction
- `prompt.images`: Max 5 images, 15 MB each; types: `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`
- `model.id`: Explicit model (omit for default)
- `repos[].url`: Required; supports GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud, Azure DevOps
- `repos[].startingRef`: Branch or commit SHA
- `repos[].prUrl`: Work on PR branches instead
- `workOnCurrentBranch`: Push directly to source branch (default: false)
- `autoCreatePR`: Create PR on completion
- `envVars`: Max 50, names up to 255 bytes (not starting with `CURSOR_`), values up to 4096 bytes
- `agentId`: Client-supplied UUID for idempotent creates (incompatible with `envVars`)

**Error Codes:** `409 agent_id_conflict`, `400 repository_access`, `400 validation_error`

---

### List Agents
**GET** `/v1/agents`

Lists agents for authenticated user, newest first.

**Auth:** User or service account API key

**Query Parameters:**
- `limit`: 1–100 (default: 20)
- `cursor`: Pagination token from `nextCursor`
- `prUrl`: Filter by pull request URL
- `includeArchived`: Include archived agents (default: true)

**Request:**
```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url 'https://api.cursor.com/v1/agents?limit=20&cursor=abc123' \
  -u YOUR_API_KEY:
```

**Response (200):**
```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
      "name": "Add README with setup instructions",
      "status": "ACTIVE",
      "env": {
        "type": "cloud"
      },
      "url": "https://cursor.com/agents/bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
      "createdAt": "2026-04-13T18:30:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2026-04-13T18:45:00.000Z",
      "latestRunId": "run-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": "bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002"
}
```

**Note:** `nextCursor` is omitted when no more pages exist. List returns only identity fields; call `GET /v1/agents/{id}` for full metadata.

---

### Get An Agent
**GET** `/v1/agents/{id}`

Retrieves durable agent metadata and status.

**Auth:** User or service account API key

**Path Parameters:**
- `id`: Agent identifier (e.g., `bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001`)

**Request:**
```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.cursor.com/v1/agents/bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 \
  -u YOUR_API_KEY:
```

**Response (200):**
```json
{
  "id": "bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
  "name": "Add README with setup instructions",
  "status": "ACTIVE",
  "env": {
    "type": "cloud"
  },
  "repos": [
    {
      "url": "https://github.com/your-org/your-repo",
      "startingRef": "main"
    }
  ],
  "workOnCurrentBranch": false,
  "autoCreatePR": true,
  "url": "https://cursor.com/agents/bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
  "createdAt": "2026-04-13T18:30:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-04-13T18:30:00.000Z",
  "latestRunId": "run-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
}
```

**Status Enums:**
- `ACTIVE`: Turn running, waiting on background work, or starting; keep machine up
- `IDLE`: Last turn finished; machine may hibernate
- `ARCHIVED`: Terminal; workspace can be deleted

---

## Run Management

### Create A Run
**POST** `/v1/agents/{id}/runs`

Sends follow-up prompt to existing active agent using current conversation and workspace state.

**Auth:** User or service account API key

**Path Parameters:**
- `id`: Agent identifier

**Request Body (JSON):**
```json
{
  "prompt": {
    "text": "Also add troubleshooting steps",
    "images": []
  },
  "mcpServers": [
    {
      "name": "docs",
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://example.com/mcp"
    }
  ],
  "mode": "agent"
}
```

**Response (200):**
```json
{
  "run": {
    "id": "run-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002",
    "agentId": "bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
    "status": "CREATING",
    "createdAt": "2026-04-13T18:50:00.000Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-04-13T18:50:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

**Error Codes:** `409 agent_busy` (another run active)

**Constraint:** Only one run active per agent at a time.

---

### List Runs
**GET** `/v1/agents/{id}/runs`

Lists runs for an agent, newest first.

**Auth:** User or service account API key

**Path Parameters:**
- `id`: Agent identifier

**Query Parameters:**
- `limit`: 1–100 (default: 20)
- `cursor`: Pagination token

**Request:**
```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url 'https://api.cursor.com/v1/agents/bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/runs?limit=20' \
  -u YOUR_API_KEY:
```

**Response (200):**
```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "run-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002",
      "agentId": "bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
      "status": "RUNNING",
      "createdAt": "2026-04-13T18:50:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2026-04-13T18:51:00.000Z",
      "git": {
        "branches": [
          {
            "repoUrl": "github.com/your-org/your-repo",
            "branch": "cursor/add-readme-a1b2"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### Get A Run
**GET** `/v1/agents/{id}/runs/{runId}`

Retrieves run status, timestamps, and (for terminal runs) final result and pushed branches.

**Auth:** User or service account API key

**Path Parameters:**
- `id`: Agent identifier
- `runId`: Run identifier (e.g., `run-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001`)

**Request:**
```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.cursor.com/v1/agents/bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/runs/run-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 \
  -u YOUR_API_KEY:
```

**Response (200):**
```json
{
  "id": "run-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
  "agentId": "bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
  "status": "FINISHED",
  "createdAt": "2026-04-13T18:30:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-04-13T18:45:00.000Z",
  "durationMs": 12357,
  "result": "Added README.md with installation instructions and usage examples.",
  "git": {
    "branches": [
      {
        "repoUrl": "github.com/your-org/your-repo",
        "branch": "cursor/add-readme-a1b2",
        "prUrl": "https://github.com/your-org/your-repo/pull/123"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Status Enums:** `CREATING`, `RUNNING`, `FINISHED`, `ERROR`, `CANCELLED`, `EXPIRED`

**Terminal Run Fields:**
- `durationMs`: Wall-clock milliseconds
- `result`: Final assistant text
- `git.branches[]`: Pushed branches with optional PR URLs

---

### Stream A Run
**GET** `/v1/agents/{id}/runs/{runId}/stream`

Streams Server-Sent Events (SSE) for one run.

**Auth:** User or service account API key

**Headers:**
- `Accept: text/event-stream`
- `Last-Event-ID`: Resume from opaque event id (optional)

**Request:**
```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.cursor.com/v1/agents/bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/runs/run-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/stream \
  -u YOUR_API_KEY: \
  --header 'Accept: text/event-stream'
```

**Event Types:**
- `status`: `{ runId, status }`
- `assistant`: `{ text }` — assistant text delta
- `thinking`: `{ text }` — thinking delta
- `tool_call`: `{ callId, name, status, args?, result?, truncated? }`
- `interaction_update`: Richer SDK-shape payload
- `heartbeat`: `{}`
- `result`: `{ runId, status, text?, durationMs?, git? }`
- `error`: `{ code, message }`
- `done`: `{}`

**Example Stream:**
```
event: status
data: {"runId":"run-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001","status":"RUNNING"}

id: 1713033000000-0
event: assistant
data: {"text":"I'll update the README now."}

id: 1713033005000-0
event: tool_call
data: {"callId":"call-1","name":"read_file","status":"running","args":{"path":"README.md"}}

id: 1713033006000-0
event: tool_call
data: {"callId":"call-1","name":"read_file","status":"completed","result":{"success":{"content":"# Project"}}}

id: 1713033010000-0
event: result
data: {"runId":"run-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001","status":"FINISHED","text":"Added README.md","durationMs":12357}

event: done
data: {}
```

**Retention:** Response includes `X-Cursor-Stream-Retention-Seconds` header. After expiry, may return `410 stream_expired`; use [Get A Run](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints.md#get-a-run) instead.

---

### Cancel A Run
**POST** `/v1/agents/{id}/runs/{runId}/cancel`

Cancels the active run. Terminal and irreversible.

**Auth:** User or service account API key

**Path Parameters:**
- `id`: Agent identifier
- `runId`: Run identifier

**Request:**
```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.cursor.com/v1/agents/bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/runs/run-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/cancel \
  -u YOUR_API_KEY:
```

**Response (200):**
```json
{
  "id": "run-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
}
```

**Error Codes:** `409 run_not_cancellable` (already terminal or never active)

---

## Agent Lifecycle

### Archive An Agent
**POST** `/v1/agents/{id}/archive`

Archives agent. Archived agents remain readable but reject new runs until unarchived.

**Auth:** User or service account API key

**Path Parameters:**
- `id`: Agent identifier

**Request:**
```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.cursor.com/v1/agents/bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/archive \
  -u YOUR_API_KEY:
```

**Response (200):**
```json
{
  "id": "bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
}
```

**Note:** Idempotent; no status check required.

---

### Unarchive An Agent
**POST** `/v1/agents/{id}/unarchive`

Unarchives agent to accept new runs.

**Auth:** User or service account API key

**Path Parameters:**
- `id`: Agent identifier

**Request:**
```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.cursor.com/v1/agents/bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/unarchive \
  -u YOUR_API_KEY:
```

**Response (200):**
```json
{
  "id": "bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
}
```

**Note:** Idempotent.

---

### Delete An Agent Permanently
**DELETE** `/v1/agents/{id}`

Permanently deletes agent. Irreversible action.

**Auth:** User or service account API key

**Path Parameters:**
- `id`: Agent identifier

**Request:**
```bash
curl --request DELETE \
  --url https://api.cursor.com/v1/agents/bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 \
  -u YOUR_API_KEY:
```

**Response (200):**
```json
{
  "id": "bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
}
```

---

## Usage

### Get Agent Usage
**GET** `/v1/agents/{id}/usage`

Retrieves token usage per run.

**Auth:** User or service account API key

**Path Parameters:**
- `id`: Agent identifier

**Query Parameters:**
- `runId`: Scope to single run (optional)

**Request:**
```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.cursor.com/v1/agents/bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/usage \
  -u YOUR_API_KEY:
```

**Response (200):**
```json
{
  "totalUsage": {
    "inputTokens": 12480,
    "outputTokens": 3110,
    "cacheWriteTokens": 18200,
    "cacheReadTokens": 42600,
    "totalTokens": 76390
  },
  "runs": [
    {
      "id": "run-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002",
      "usageUuid": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002",
      "usage": {
        "inputTokens": 6320,
        "outputTokens": 1450,
        "cacheWriteTokens": 7100,
        "cacheReadTokens": 21300,
        "totalTokens": 36170
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## Artifacts

### List Artifacts
**GET** `/v1/agents/{id}/artifacts`

Lists artifacts produced by agent.

**Auth:** User or service account API key

**Path Parameters:**
- `id`: Agent identifier

**Request:**
```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.cursor.com/v1/agents/bc-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/artifacts \
  -u YOUR_API_KEY:
```

**Response (200):**
```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "path": "artifacts/screenshot.png",
      "sizeBytes": 12345,
      "updatedAt": "2026-04-13T18:45:00.000Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### Download An Artifact
**GET** `/v1/agents/{id}/artifacts/download`

Retrieves presigned S3 URL (15-minute expiry).

**Auth:** User or service account API key

**Path Parameters:**
- `id`: Agent identifier

**Query Parameters:**

## Environments

### Create An Environment
**POST** `/v1/environments`

Creates a saved environment.

**Auth:** User or service account API key

**Request Body (JSON):**
```json

## Summary

| Endpoint | Method | Auth | Key Points |
|----------|--------|------|-----------|
| Create Agent | POST `/v1/agents` | User/SA | Returns agent + initial run; supports image inputs, MCP, custom subagents |
| List Agents | GET `/v1/agents` | User/SA | Pagination: `limit`, `cursor`; `nextCursor` omitted at end |
| Get Agent | GET `/v1/agents/{id}` | User/SA | Full metadata; status: `ACTIVE`, `IDLE`, `ARCHIVED` |
| Create Run | POST `/v1/agents/{id}/runs` | User/SA | Follow-up prompt; `409 agent_busy` if run active |
| List Runs | GET `/v1/agents/{id}/runs` | User/SA | Pagination: `limit`, `cursor` |
| Get Run | GET `/v1/agents/{id}/runs/{runId}` | User/SA | Terminal runs include `durationMs`, `result`, `git` |
| Stream Run | GET `/v1/agents/{id}/runs/{runId}/stream` | User/SA | SSE events; `Last-Event-ID` for resume; `410 stream_expired` when retention lapses |
| Cancel Run | POST `/v1/agents/{id}/runs/{runId}/cancel` | User/SA | Terminal; `409 run_not_cancellable` if already terminal |
| Archive Agent | POST `/v1/agents/{id}/archive` | User/SA | Idempotent soft delete |
| Unarchive Agent | POST `/v1/agents/{id}/unarchive` | User/SA | Idempotent |
| Delete Agent | DELETE `/v1/agents/{id}` | User/SA | Irreversible |
| Agent Usage | GET `/v1/agents/{id}/usage` | User/SA | Token breakdown; optional `runId` filter |
| List Artifacts | GET `/v1/agents/{id}/artifacts` | User/SA | Relative paths under `artifacts/` |
| Download Artifact | GET `/v1/agents/{id}/artifacts/download` | User/SA | Presigned 15-minute S3 URL via `path` query |
| Create Environment | POST `/v1/environments` | User/SA | `409` on name conflict; max 100 repos |
| Get Environment | GET `/v1/environments/{id}` | User/SA | Includes `environmentJson`, `versionId` |
| Delete Environment | DELETE `/v1/environments/{id}` | User/SA | Irreversible |
| API Key Info | GET `/v1/me` | User/SA | Returns auth details; omits `userId` for SA keys |
| List Models | GET `/v1/models` | User/SA | Includes parameters and variants |
| List Repos | GET `/v1/repositories` | User/SA | GitHub only; `1/min`, `30/hour` rate limits; may take 10–30s |
| List Workers | GET `/v0/private-workers` | SA | Pagination: `limit`, `pageToken` |
| List Pools | GET `/v0/private-workers/pools` | SA | Includes utilization metrics |
| Pending Requests | GET `/v0/private-workers/pending-requests` | SA | Includes claimed-but-offline entries; `streamCursor` for watch |
| Watch Requests | GET `/v0/private-workers/pending-requests/stream` | SA | SSE; events: `created`, `claimed`, `expired`; cursor expires 5min after list |
| Claim Request | POST `/v0/private-workers/claim` | SA | Optional `sessionToken`; binds worker to agent |
| Release Claim | POST `/v0/private-workers/claims/{id}/release` | SA | Frees worker; `400` if turn active, `404` if no claim |

---

**General Notes:**
- "The Cloud Agents API v1 is in public beta. APIs may change before general availability."
- Webhooks are coming; legacy v0 API still supports them.
- Image limit: 15 MB per image (max 5), types: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP.
- Pagination: `limit` (default 20–50), `cursor` / `pageToken` (omitted when no more pages).
- Rate limits and auth details in [API Overview](https://cursor.com/docs/api.md).
- Service account API keys required for worker/pool endpoints and user-scoped token minting.
````

```text
# Webhooks Summary

**Events Supported:**
"Currently, only `statusChange` events are supported, specifically when an agent encounters an `ERROR` or `FINISHED` state."

**Payload Example & Fields:**
The JSON payload includes: `event`, `timestamp`, `id`, `status`, `source` (repository, ref), `target` (url, branchName, prUrl), and `summary`. "Some fields are optional and will only be included when available."

**Headers:**
- `X-Webhook-Signature` – HMAC-SHA256 signature as `sha256=<hex_digest>`
- `X-Webhook-ID` – Unique delivery identifier
- `X-Webhook-Event` – Event type
- `User-Agent` – Set to `Cursor-Agent-Webhook/1.0`

**Signature Verification:**
"Compute the expected signature and compare it with the received signature" using HMAC-SHA256 with your webhook secret. Use the raw request body (before parsing) for verification.

**Retries:**
"Webhooks may be retried if your endpoint returns an error status code."

**Configuration:**
The documentation doesn't specify how to configure webhooks on launch—only that "when you create an agent with a webhook URL, Cursor will send HTTP POST requests."
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
# Cursor APIs: Concise Overview

## Available APIs

Cursor offers eight programmatic interfaces:

- **Admin API**: Team management, settings, usage, spending, model access
- **Analytics API**: Usage insights, AI metrics, active users, model data
- **AI Code Tracking API**: Track AI-generated code at commit/change levels
- **Bugbot API**: Trigger reviews, retrieve analytics
- **Cloud Agents API**: Create and manage AI-powered coding agents
- **Origin API**: Work with repositories, commits, PRs, installations
- **TypeScript SDK**: Run agents with local/cloud runtime support
- **Python SDK**: Sync/async clients for agent execution
- **SDK Bridge**: Build SDKs in other languages via open protocol

## Base URLs & Endpoints

Primary endpoint: `https://api.cursor.com/` (specific paths vary by API)

## Authentication

**Basic Auth** (Admin, Analytics, AI Code Tracking, Bugbot):
- Use API key as username, leave password empty
- Format: `Authorization: Basic {base64_encode('KEY:')}`

**Bearer Auth** (Cloud Agents API):
- Format: `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`

**API Key Creation:**
Navigate to dashboard API Keys page. Keys follow format: `crsr_[64 hex chars]`

**Scope Requirements:**
Admin and AI Code Tracking APIs require `admin:*` scope

## Plan Availability

| Feature | Availability |
|---------|--------------|
| Admin, Analytics, AI Code Tracking, Bugbot APIs | Enterprise teams only |
| Cloud Agents API | Beta (All Plans) |
| Origin API | Early Beta |
| TypeScript/Python SDKs, SDK Bridge | All users |

## Rate Limits

Default: "20 requests per minute" across most endpoints. Variations include 60-250 req/min for specific Admin API endpoints, 100 req/min for Analytics team-level endpoints. Exceeding limits returns `429 Too Many Requests` response.

## Caching

Analytics and AI Code Tracking APIs support HTTP caching via ETags. "304 Not Modified responses don't count against rate limits." Cache duration: 15 minutes.

## Notable Gaps

- No OpenAPI spec link provided in documentation
- No MCP server mentioned
- No versioning discussion (v0 vs v1)
```

```text
# Cloud Agents: Secrets, Network & Data Handling

## Secret Types

**Environment Variables**: Non-sensitive configuration visible to the agent, encrypted at rest and in transit.

**Runtime Secrets**: Credentials loaded as environment variables but "redacted from the agent's tool call results, chat transcript, commits, and commit messages" and replaced with `[REDACTED]`.

**Build Secrets**: Available only during Docker build processes, not exposed to the running agent.

## Network Access Modes

Three egress control options exist:

1. **Allow all network access** — No restrictions
2. **Default + allowlist** — "Cloud Agents can reach the default domains plus any domains you add to your allowlist"
3. **Allowlist only** — Only explicitly approved domains accessible

These policies apply at user, environment, and team levels, with team admins able to lock settings for Enterprise organizations.

## Artifact Uploads

When using allowlist modes, the domain `cloud-agent-artifacts.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` must be explicitly added; wildcards risk "exfiltration path for a prompt-injected agent."

## Data Retention

**Conversation history** is retained indefinitely by default; **environment snapshots** follow "a rolling 90-day inactivity window." Enterprise teams can configure custom retention policies capping data at 90 days or indefinite.
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
# Mobile-Web Agent Continuity in Cursor

## Cross-Device Agent Movement

**Desktop to Mobile:** Agents initiated anywhere automatically appear in the mobile inbox. Users can either "push your work to a cloud agent first with Move to Cloud" or "direct it from your phone with Remote Control" while keeping it on the computer.

**Mobile to Desktop:** Any agent started on mobile shows up in the desktop Cloud Agents panel and at cursor.com/agents, allowing seamless continuation.

## Remote Control Feature

Remote Control enables directing a local agent session from mobile. The mechanism: "The agent loop moves to the cloud while its tools keep running on your machine, so it reads your files, runs your tests, and uses your local setup."

**Activation:** Users run `/remote-control` in the agent's input on their computer, then the session becomes controllable from other devices.

**Data handling:** "Your repository, secrets, credentials, and build caches stay on your machine. Only tool results and the context the model needs cross to Cursor."

## Conversation Storage & Access

Agent conversations sync across devices—agents follow you across surfaces automatically. The mobile app is "cache-first. It reads from local data so the inbox and conversations open fast, then syncs once your connection returns."

## Notable Limitations

Remote Control requires:
- Cursor 3.9.8 or later
- Computer must remain awake and online (tool calls run locally)
- Cloud data storage enabled

No export or share options are documented in this content.
```

```text
# Cloud Agent & CLI Integration

## & Prefix for Cloud Handoff

The `&` prefix enables pushing conversations to Cloud Agent mid-session. As documented: `"Prepend & to any message to send it to the cloud."` Example usage includes tasks like `"& refactor the auth module and add comprehensive tests"`. You can then resume work on web or mobile at cursor.com/agents.

## Resuming Conversations

Multiple methods exist for continuing prior work:

- Use `agent resume`, `--continue`, or the `/resume` slash command to return to your most recent chat
- The `--resume [thread id]` flag loads a specific previous conversation with its context
- Running `agent ls` opens a list of previous chats for selection and resumption

## Limitations in Provided Documentation

The source material does not contain information about:
- Specific chat storage locations
- A `--cloud` flag
- Remote Control functionality

These topics may be covered elsewhere in Cursor's documentation but aren't addressed in this CLI guide excerpt.
```
