```text
97	## What a complete provider contains
98	
99	### Package and files
100	
101	The architecture is one-directional: 
102	
103	- `pkg/spi` defines the interfaces, the schema, and the shared helpers and imports no provider
104	- every provider imports `pkg/spi`
105	- `pkg/spi/factory/registry.go` imports every provider and is the only place that knows them all. 
106	- Nothing else in the CLI imports a provider package directly.
107	
108	The package is `pkg/providers/<agent>`: the product's own name, lowercased, with the spaces removed. That is the whole rule for ten of the twelve, including `cursoride`, because Code, CLI, TUI and IDE are part of what those products call themselves. The IDE-backed providers end in `ide`, which Cursor IDE's own name already supplies and VS Code Copilot does not, so it becomes `copilotide`. Pi is `piagent`, the one place a bare product name was too slight to stand on its own. The following file layout is recommended, not mandatory; add, combine, or split files where that makes the provider easier to understand:
109	
110	|                                      File                                      |                                          Purpose                                           |
111	| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
112	| `provider.go`                                                                  | The `Provider` struct, `NewProvider()`, `Check`, `DetectAgent`, session listing and lookup |
113	| `agent_session.go`                                                             | Conversion from the native format to `schema.SessionData`                                  |
114	| `jsonl_parser.go` (or `json_parser.go`, `transcript_parser.go`, `database.go`) | Native format decoding                                                                     |
115	| `markdown_tools.go`                                                            | Per-tool `Summary` and `FormattedMarkdown` rendering                                       |
116	| `watcher.go`                                                                   | fsnotify watcher used by `run` and `watch`                                                 |
117	| `<agent>_exec.go`                                                              | Command line parsing, resume arguments, process launch, exit handling                      |
118	| `path_utils.go`                                                                | Native store discovery and working directory encoding                                      |
119	| `reconstruct.go`                                                               | `ReconstructSession`, `NativeSessionPath`, `SupportsReconstruction`                        |
120	| `*_test.go`                                                                    | Tests alongside each source file                                                          |
121	| `testdata/`                                                                    | Inputs consumed by automated tests and expected outputs those tests actually compare      |
122	| `examples/`                                                                    | Captured examples, rendered histories, QA results and other human-review evidence          |
123	| `factory/`                                                                     | Software factory scripts (see below)                                                       |
124	
125	Keep related logic together and avoid unnecessary file sprawl. Small helpers usually belong in the file whose concern they serve; a separate file is reasonable when it groups a distinct concern, such as debug output. File organization may differ from this example while still meeting the provider's behavioral and architectural requirements.
126	
127	Add `var _ spi.Provider = (*Provider)(nil)` so the compiler enforces the interface, and the same assertion for any optional interface you implement.
128	
129	### Separate test fixtures from examples
130	
131	Reserve `testdata/` for files that automated tests actually consume as inputs or compare as expected outputs. For each fixture or fixture set, identify the consuming test and the behavior it asserts. A file does not become test data merely because a test helper copies the directory containing it.
132	
133	Put captured examples, manual QA results, version banners, tool audits, and generated JSON or Markdown that no test compares in `examples/`, following [Pi's examples](pkg/providers/piagent/examples/). Keep native captures in `testdata/` when parser or rendering tests consume them; link from the examples to those fixtures rather than duplicating them. A generated `session-data.json` or rendered history belongs in `testdata/` only if an automated test actually compares it as a golden file. Do not add a superficial test just to justify keeping a review artifact there.
134	
135	This distinction is required even when choosing a different source-file layout. Before submitting, audit every file under `testdata/` for an actual test consumer and move unused review artifacts to `examples/`. Update documentation and audit links after moving them.
136	
137	### Every SPI method, including the ones that are easy to miss
138	
139	Implement every method on `spi.Provider` in `pkg/spi/provider.go` (count them against the most recent version of the file). Beyond the obvious ones, review these carefully:
140	
141	- `ListAgentChatSessions` returns lightweight metadata without a full parse.
142	- `ListAllAgentChatSessions` enumerates every session in the native store across all projects, reading the originating working directory from inside each session. This powers `specstory reindex`, `search`, and `resume`.
143	- `ReconstructSession`, `NativeSessionPath`, and `SupportsReconstruction` implement cross-agent resume into your agent. `SupportsReconstruction` is a pure constant answer and must agree with the other two. `NativeSessionPath` only resolves the path; the CLI creates the directory and writes the file.
144	- The `progress` callback on `GetAgentChatSessions` is invoked once per session file, including skipped and failed ones, so the progress bar reaches its total.
145	- The optional capabilities are also defined in [pkg/spi/provider.go](pkg/spi/provider.go). `spi.PathSessionReader` (`GetAgentChatSessionByPath`) lets reindex open a session by its known path instead of searching by id. `spi.ProgressEnumerator` (`ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress`) adds live scan counts. Implement either, both, or neither; reindex falls back to the required methods when they are absent. Both are recommended for JSONL stores, which can use `spi.ScanSessionsInParallel` for enumeration (it walks `*.jsonl` files only; other store kinds implement enumeration themselves).
146	
147	### Wiring outside the package
148	
149	- `pkg/spi/factory/registry.go`: register under a short lowercase id (`muse`, `antigravity`, `droid`).
150	- `pkg/config/config.go`: a `<id>_cmd` entry in the default config template, a `ProvidersConfig` field, a `GetProviderCmd` case with its doc comment updated, and rows in the config tests. `specstory run <id>` must honor it; `specstory check <id> -c` honors the flag only. **All three parts are required and none of them fails loudly on its own** — TOML accepts a key with no struct field, and `GetProviderCmd` returns `""` for an unknown id — so a partial wiring ships a config key that silently does nothing. Two tests enforce it: `config.TestProvidersConfigIsFullyWired` checks each `ProvidersConfig` field reaches both the template and a `GetProviderCmd` case, and `cmd.TestEveryRegisteredProviderHasACommandOverride` checks every registered provider id resolves to one.
151	- `pkg/cmd/session_tui_browser.go`: add an accent color in `colorForAgent` as a hex code (`#RRGGBB`), based on a color associated with the agent's own brand. Check it on both dark and light terminal backgrounds and adjust the shade if needed for legibility. The maintainer may replace it.
152	- `pkg/skills/agents.go`: a row when the agent supports agent skills (it has a project or global skills directory). Its `Name` is the public `npx skills` canonical id, not the provider id.
153	- `README.md` in this directory: the intro sentence, the Agent Support table row, the `[providers]` example block, the Configuration Options row, and the Debug Raw Mode provider list. Write a prose paragraph only if the provider behaves differently from wrapping a terminal process.
154	- `../README.md` at the monorepo root: the ASCII diagram line, the Installation table row (leave the Min Version to the maintainer), the lead-in sentence, and a `specstory run <id>` example.
155	- `changelog.md`: an entry under a placeholder heading such as `## Unreleased`. Use the fixed announcement sentence from the previous provider's entry, listing every previously released provider, followed by a sentence on resume in each direction. State a version floor as the version you tested; the maintainer replaces it with the release-day version and moves your entry under the release heading. Do not also add it under an existing version, and do not add an "Improvements" section for a provider that has never shipped.
156	- IDE providers only: the per-save line during `run` and the restart note after `resume` are printed by the CLI and keyed to the registry id in `main.go` and `pkg/cmd/resume.go`; those need a change too.
157	
158	### Naming layers
159	
160	Five identifiers exist and they are not the same string:
161	
162	|                                         Identifier                                         |                                                    Convention                                                     |     Example      |
163	| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
164	| Package name                                                                               | `<agent>`                                                                                                         | `antigravitycli` |
165	| Registry id (CLI argument, `<id>_cmd`, statistics, index, check-event `provider` property) | short lowercase agent name                                                                                        | `deepseek`       |
166	| `ProviderInfo.ID` in session data                                                          | the registry id, for every provider from Muse Code onward                                                         | `muse`           |
167	| `Name()` and `ProviderInfo.Name`                                                           | the product's own name and casing; also the `agent_provider` analytics property and the telemetry agent attribute | `DeepSeek TUI`   |
168	| Skills registry `Name` in `pkg/skills/agents.go`                                           | the public `npx skills` canonical id                                                                              | `claude-code`    |
169	
170	Go identifiers follow the brand's casing (`DeepSeekCmd`, not `DeepseekCmd`).
171	
172	## Rules that will otherwise get your submission changed
173	
174	These are the changes reviewers make most often. Each one is a real review finding from a past provider.
175	
176	### Reuse the shared helpers in pkg/spi
177	
178	Every helper below replaced copies that had drifted apart across providers. Do not reimplement them.
179	
180	- Use `schema.CurrentSchemaVersion` and the shared `schema.ContentTypeText` / `schema.ContentTypeThinking` constants when constructing `SessionData`, rather than repeating their string values. Native record fields and code-fence language labels follow their own formats.
181	- `spi.CodeFence` for every fenced block, sized past any backtick run in the content. Never write a literal triple backtick, and never backslash-escape backticks.
182	- `spi.ReadRecordLine` with `spi.MaxRecordLineSize` for every JSONL session file. It is the only correct way to cap a record: a cap applied after `bufio.Reader.ReadString` returns has already allocated the oversized record it exists to prevent. A capped `bufio.Scanner` is still right for sidecar and index files, where losing the remainder of the file is acceptable.
183	- `spi.CapRunes` for truncation. Never slice a string by bytes.
184	- Compare a sentinel error with `errors.Is` and match an error type with `errors.As`. Never `err == io.EOF` or `err.(*exec.ExitError)`: a wrapped error fails both, and wrapping gets added later by someone who has no reason to look for a bare comparison.
185	- `spi.LanguageFromPath`, `spi.RenderGenericJSON`, `spi.TodoSymbol`, `spi.FormatDiffBlock`, `spi.StringValue`, `spi.NormalizeToolName` for tool rendering.
186	- `spi.LookPathForCheck` for binary lookup, `spi.ClassifyCheckError` for lookup/storage errors, and `spi.ClassifyCheckExecutionError` for probe failures after the binary was found. Populate `CheckResult.ErrorType` with the same `spi.CheckError*` value sent to analytics; leave it empty on success. Empty `--version` output on a successful run is a success reported as `"unknown"`, not a failure (`spi.CheckErrorNoOutput` is a legacy shape).
187	- `analytics.CheckAttempt` populated once per `Check`, with the event emitted by `analytics.TrackCheckSuccess` or `analytics.TrackCheckFailure`. No inline `analytics.TrackEvent` calls in a provider.
188	- `spi.SplitCommandLine` for custom commands; `spi.EnsureResumeArgs` when the agent resumes via a subcommand, or `spi.EnsureResumeFlagArgs` when it uses a flag.
189	- `spi.AgentExitError` to report a non-zero agent exit. Never call `os.Exit` inside a provider; it skips the final session save (the reason is in `pkg/spi/exit.go`).
190	- `spi.GetDebugDir` for debug output paths. See [Native debug output](#native-debug-output) for the provider's export responsibilities; the CLI writes `session-data.json` itself.
191	- `spi.NormalizePath` and `spi.ExtractShellPathHints` for path hints; `spi.CanonicalizePathOrClean` for local path comparison; `spi.FileURIToPath` for any `file://` URI.
192	- `spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage`, `spi.GenerateReadableName`, and `spi.ReadableTitleFromSessionData` for slugs, names, and titles. If the agent records its own title or summary for a session, prefer it for `Name` and fall back to the shared generator.
193	- `spi.PrepareTurns`, `spi.ResolveWorkspaceRoot`, `spi.ReconstructRole`, `spi.RFC3339Millis`, `spi.ResumedSessionTitle` in `ReconstructSession`.
194	- `spi.NewFSWatcher` to create every fsnotify watcher, in production code and tests alike. Never call `fsnotify.NewWatcher` or `fsnotify.NewBufferedWatcher` directly; see [The watcher](#the-watcher) for why.
195	- `spi.WatchWindowDays`, `spi.WatchWindowCutoff`, `spi.DateDirWithinWatchWindow` when watched paths can grow without limit and the store layout supports a rolling date window. A fixed set of directory watches does not need a rolling window merely because the number of session files grows.
196	- `spi.DeliverSession` for synchronous callback delivery with panic recovery. If using `spi.DispatchSession` for asynchronous delivery, track and join every callback before shutdown.
197	- SQLite stores: open every read handle as `file:<path>?mode=ro&` plus `spi.BusyTimeoutPragma`. The `file:` scheme is required; the driver ignores `mode=` on a bare path and opens read-write-create. Call `spi.EnsureWALMode` once at watcher startup, never on a read path.
198	
199	Providers must never import `pkg/utils`, `pkg/session`, or `pkg/cloud` (the import graph cycles through the registry), nor `pkg/telemetry` (layering).
200	
201	### Honest data over convenient data
202	
203	- `CheckResult.Version` is the agent's version string or empty. Never a label.
204	- `ProviderInfo.Version` is the agent's version when the native data records it, otherwise the literal `"unknown"`. The model name is not a substitute; it belongs on each agent message's `Model` field, and it is the real model, never a placeholder such as an automatic-mode label.
205	- `SessionData.WorkspaceRoot` is never empty: the workspace the agent stated, then the caller's project path, then the process working directory as a documented last resort. These fallbacks support path normalization and rendering; they are not evidence that the session belongs to the caller's project.
206	- `GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd` records the session's originating working directory. Leave it empty when the origin cannot be determined; do not fill it from a rendering fallback. Global enumeration still returns the session, and the CLI assigns the `"unknown"` project ID. The literal `"unknown"` belongs in neither `OriginCwd` nor `WorkspaceRoot`.
207	- Never infer project membership from the paths that tools touched; one read of `~/.gitconfig` would attach the session to every project under the home directory. Session-to-project matching uses containment of stated paths, never a rendering fallback or a guessed common ancestor.
208	- `GetAgentChatSession` returns `nil, nil` for not found. Errors are for real failures.
209	- A by-id lookup on a global store must still check that the session belongs to the requested project, or one project's conversation will be written into another's history.
210	- On an IDE store the same session can appear under several matching workspace entries, and an empty copy can come first; mark an id as seen only after the content check, and keep an empty copy only as a fallback.
211	- `AgentChatSession.RawData` carries the native transcript on every session you return, whether or not debug output is enabled; SpecStory Cloud stores it. Build it from the records you already parsed, never by reading the file a second time: a session being written grows between the two reads, so the raw transcript would describe turns the converted session never saw, and during `run` that happens on nearly every save. `RawData` contains the accepted native records from the same parsing snapshot; malformed or oversized records skipped during parsing are excluded.
212	- `Usage` carries only the token fields the native data distinguishes; a session total is not an input count, so leave it nil with a why-comment rather than guess. A token kind not already in `schema.Usage` is a shared change to ask for.
213	- Timestamps come from the record, never from `time.Now()` in a parse or render path, are consistent across every code path, and are RFC 3339 parseable.
214	
215	### Comments explain why, and stay true
216	
217	- Every non-obvious line carries a "why" comment. Restating the code is noise.
218	- Comments are self-contained. Do not reference other providers ("Claude Code uses X here"), plan documents, decision numbers, or the history of how the code came to be.
219	- Magic values carry their provenance ("as observed in sessions written by version 3.12").
220	- A comment that contradicts its code will be treated as a bug.
221	- Every exported identifier, in particular each SPI method, carries a Go doc comment consistent with the siblings.
222	
223	### Parsing
224	
225	- For JSONL session files, read each record with `spi.ReadRecordLine(reader, spi.MaxRecordLineSize)`. It bounds allocation as the record is read and reports an oversized record instead of returning it, so one bad record degrades to one bad record rather than an aborted file. Log the skip at Warn with the file and line and carry on. Sidecar and index files may use a `bufio.Scanner` capped at `spi.MaxRecordLineSize`, mapping `ErrTooLong` to a clear error.
226	- When a record holds `json.RawMessage`, unmarshal from a copy of the line (`scanner.Text()`, never `scanner.Bytes()`); the scanner reuses its buffer.
227	- A record that fails to parse is skipped, never silently: log at Warn with the file and line ("Skipping corrupted JSONL line" is the established message shape).
228	- Preserve the agent's native ordering and branch-selection semantics. Use sequence numbers where provided, parent links for tree formats, and file order where the native format defines it. Test supported out-of-order cases and branch selection where applicable.
229	- Identify tool-result records using the native format's result markers or envelope; an unfamiliar record is not automatically a tool result. A recognized tool result with an unfamiliar payload type degrades to a generic result instead of vanishing. Pair results to calls using the native correlation fields, preferring an explicit call id; use tool type or first-in-first-out only where the native format makes that pairing unambiguous.
230	- The parser's kind switch enumerates every record kind observed in real data, rendering it or naming it as known-nothing-to-render with the reason, so the default "unknown kind" log fires only for genuinely new kinds.
231	- Preserve unsupported native content in `RawData` when its record is accepted, and document what is omitted from normalized data and Markdown in `<AGENT>-FORMAT.md`. Preserve meaningful conversation text where the shared schema can represent it faithfully. Reserve "known-nothing-to-render" for records with no conversational content to display; an unfamiliar role or missing tool-call pairing is not sufficient reason to discard meaningful content.
232	- Scan and watch only the durable session file; never read a scratch file the agent rewrites in place.
233	
234	### Native debug output
235	
236	`--debug-raw` helps provider authors, reviewers, and future maintainers inspect what the agent actually stored, compare it with SpecStory's interpretation, and diagnose missing content or format changes. The provider saves readable native input alongside the normalized `session-data.json` written by the CLI. Populating `AgentChatSession.RawData` does not create these native debug files; exporting them is a separate provider responsibility.
237	
238	- Honor `debugRaw` in single-session and bulk reads, live `run`/`watch` updates, and optional by-path reads. Write under `spi.GetDebugDir(sessionID)`, which defaults to `.specstory/debug/<session-id>/` and respects `--debug-dir`. When the flag is false, this export creates no files.
239	- For JSONL, write one pretty-printed file per accepted native record, numbered from `1.json`, `2.json`, etc. in sequenced source order. For JSON or database stores, write pretty-printed session objects or individual records with native identifiers. Preserve native fields and envelopes, including unfamiliar fields, relevant headers, and sidecar data used during conversion. Keep source identity and ordering clear enough to trace an output back to its input.
240	- Generate the export from the same input snapshot used for conversion. Do not reread a changing transcript or substitute a reduced typed structure that drops unknown fields or records omitted from Markdown. Those details may be exactly what a maintainer needs to understand a format change. Malformed or oversized records may be skipped under the parsing rules above, with the required diagnostic.
241	- Refresh the export when the session changes, removing obsolete provider-owned files so earlier records cannot masquerade as current data. Preserve CLI-owned files such as `session-data.json`. Log export failures with the session and path, without aborting session processing.
242	- Test that a field the provider does not recognize still appears in the saved native JSON, and that `--debug-dir` puts the files in the requested directory. For numbered files, export a session with three records, then export the same session with only two: the old `3.json` must be removed. Check that live updates produce current debug files, and that not using the debug flag creates none. Keep test output isolated with `spi.SetDebugBaseDir(t.TempDir())` and reset the override during cleanup.
243	
244	### The watcher
245	
246	- Filesystem events through fsnotify are the primary change signal. Supplement them with bounded periodic reconciliation to recover missed events, including writes to files that were not yet watched. Keep reconciliation scoped to the relevant session paths and prune idle watches where applicable.
247	- Create the watcher with `spi.NewFSWatcher`, never `fsnotify.NewWatcher`. On Windows, fsnotify has a single I/O goroutine that both delivers `Events`/`Errors` and services `Add`/`Remove`. `Add` and `Remove` wait for that goroutine to reply, and the goroutine waits for someone to receive the event or error it is sending. Nearly every watcher calls `Add` or `Remove` from the same loop that drains those channels (adopting a new session directory, re-scoping to an ancestor, pruning idle watches). With a plain fsnotify watcher, that loop deadlocks as soon as another event or error is ready. The watcher then hangs silently and no more sessions are saved. `spi.NewFSWatcher` returns an ordinary `*fsnotify.Watcher` whose channels are relayed through a lossless, ordered queue, so the I/O goroutine is never blocked. Keep `select` on `watcher.Events` and `watcher.Errors` exactly as with fsnotify. The same applies to tests that construct a watcher and call `Add`/`Remove` without draining its channels. macOS and Linux never show this failure, so only the Windows CI job will catch it, and only intermittently.
248	- Establish a startup baseline without emitting existing, unchanged sessions merely because the watcher started. New or changed sessions after startup count as activity, including changes made while the initial watches and baseline are being established. Each watcher architecture must establish this boundary reliably so initialization neither republishes history nor absorbs new activity into the baseline.
249	- If a session directory appears after startup, walk it once and adopt the files that arrived inside it, even when they carry old preserved modification times. Arrival is new activity. A pre-existing directory discovered later during the initial scan is part of the baseline, not a late arrival.
250	- Never let the watcher silently disable itself. If the agent's directory does not exist yet, watch the nearest existing ancestor and wait.
251	- When the store is keyed by project, watch only this project's subtree, never every project's directory. Walks and watches stop at the session directory; a session's own subdirectories (tool outputs, subagent logs) are neither watched nor walked.
252	- Watch every path the agent writes session content to, including asynchronous sidecar files. Change detection uses an on-disk signature (size and modification time) of every file the session spans, not a parsed field that a title-only rename would not touch.
253	- A debounced burst is re-processed once after the burst ends; the burst's last write is often the completed response.
254	- Deliver callbacks in order (one worker) or synchronously; contain panics in the consumer callback; close the race between `Stop` and in-flight work under one lock. Track goroutines with `wg.Go`, never `wg.Add(1)` paired with `defer wg.Done()`.
255	- Make the watcher restartable: create the context per start, not in `init()`.
256	- File descriptor usage stays bounded over a months-long watch. When watched paths can grow without limit, bound them with a strategy appropriate to the store layout: for date-organized stores, use `spi.WatchWindow*`, prune watches at rollover, and re-watch a dormant file when its modification time moves. A single-directory watch or another fixed set of watches already satisfies the descriptor bound and does not need a rolling date window.
257	- The command layer fingerprints every delivered session and suppresses unchanged parses; add no content-equality guard of your own.
258	
259	The startup boundary and shutdown behavior must satisfy these acceptance cases:
260	
261	| Scenario                                                                                             | Expected behavior                                                |
262	| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
263	| A session file is written just before startup and remains unchanged                                  | No emission merely because the watcher starts                    |
264	| A session file changes while the initial watches and baseline are being established                  | The update is eventually emitted, not absorbed into the baseline |
265	| A directory appears after startup containing session files with old preserved modification times     | The arriving sessions are adopted and emitted                    |
266	| A pre-existing directory is discovered later during the initial scan, with no activity since startup | No emission merely because discovery happened later              |
267	| Shutdown occurs with no new or pending session activity                                              | No emission merely because the watcher stops                     |
268	
269	Shutdown must still drain pending updates before returning. These cases define which activity counts, without prescribing a particular snapshot, watch-registration, or timestamp strategy.
270	
271	### Run and exec
272	
273	- Honor the custom command from `-c` and `<id>_cmd`; parse it with `spi.SplitCommandLine`.
274	- When a resume id is requested it wins over any id pinned in the configured command. Use `spi.EnsureResumeFlagArgs` for flag-style resume (`--resume <id>`), passing the agent's supported flag names. It replaces pinned ids, fills bare or empty flags, and preserves the caller's slice.
275	- Stop the watcher and join in-flight saves before returning the agent's exit status.
276	- For an IDE provider, `run` opens the project directory with the IDE's own CLI, canonicalizing the path first, prints install guidance if that CLI is missing, waits for the IDE to create the workspace, and then watches until Ctrl-C. No silent fallback to opening the app on its home screen.
277	
278	### Resume into your agent
279	
280	- Call `spi.PrepareTurns` to obtain the shared ordered user/agent text turns, then serialize them into your agent's native session format. The flattening policy lives in `pkg/spi/reconstruct.go`; providers must not implement their own conversion policy.
281	- User text remains user text. Agent speech and thinking become ordinary agent text, and tool activity becomes agent text through `Tool.Summary` and `Tool.FormattedMarkdown`. Do not reconstruct native tool calls, tool-result relationships, or signed thinking blocks. Preserve the prepared text and its order, adapting message grouping only where the target format requires it.
```

```text
# Cursor Cloud Agents via LiteLLM

LiteLLM provides pass-through support for the Cursor Cloud Agents API. Here are the key supported endpoints:

## Supported Endpoints

| Endpoint | Method | Purpose |
|----------|--------|---------|
| `/v0/agents` | GET | List agents |
| `/v0/agents` | POST | Launch an agent |
| `/v0/agents/{id}` | GET | Agent status |
| `/v0/agents/{id}` | DELETE | Delete an agent |
| `/v0/agents/{id}/conversation` | GET | Agent conversation |
| `/v0/agents/{id}/followup` | POST | Add follow-up |

- **No End-user Tracking**: Currently unsupported

## Quick Setup

Replace `https://api.cursor.com` with your `LITELLM_PROXY_BASE_URL/cursor` and authenticate using LiteLLM virtual keys instead of basic auth. Add your Cursor API key through the proxy's credentials interface.
```

```text
# Cursor Cloud Agents API v0 Details

Based on the GitHub repository content provided, here are the documented API specifications:

## Endpoint Paths

The API endpoints follow this pattern:
- **List agents**: `GET /v0/agents`
- **Get agent**: `GET /v0/agents/{id}`
- **Get conversation**: `GET /v0/agents/{id}/conversation`
- **Launch agent**: `POST /v0/agents`
- **Add followup**: `POST /v0/agents/{id}/followup`
- **Stop agent**: `POST /v0/agents/{id}/stop`
- **Delete agent**: `DELETE /v0/agents/{id}`
- **API key info**: `GET /v0/me`
- **List models**: `GET /v0/models`
- **List repositories**: `GET /v0/repositories`

## Launch Payload Structure

The documentation specifies these primary fields:
- `prompt` (required): Contains `text` (required string) and optional `images` array (max 5)
- `source` (required): Includes `repository` (GitHub URL) and optional `ref` (branch/tag/commit)
- `model` (optional): LLM model selection
- `target` (optional): `branchName`, `autoCreatePr`, `openAsCursorGithubApp`, `skipReviewerRequest`
- `webhook` (optional): `url` and optional `secret` (min 32 characters)

## Authentication

The system uses "Basic Authentication with your API key" in request headers.

## Rate Limits

The documentation notes that `list_repositories` has "strict limits (1/minute, 30/hour)" and recommends caching results.

**Note:** The provided content doesn't include the complete JSON response schemas for conversation messages, status enums, or comprehensive rate limit details beyond the repository endpoint.
```

```text
# Summary

**Bug Description:**
Cloud-origin agents spawned from Linear via `@cursor` lack a "Move to → Machine/Local" option in the Agents Window, while locally-started agents can move to cloud. This creates asymmetric handoff functionality—conversation context cannot transfer from cloud to local.

**Cursor Version:**
3.6.31 (Universal) with VSCode 1.105.1, reported June 4, 2026

**Staff Response:**
Dean Rie (deanrie) replied June 5, 2026, explaining this is "a known limitation, not a bug." The feature only activates when "there's already a local agent for the same repo in the Agents Window." Generic cloud-to-local migration "isn't being actively built out right now" with no ETA provided.

**Chat Context Behavior:**
According to the staff response, chat history does *not* transfer during handoff. Users can access preserved context by continuing in the cloud session at cursor.com/agents, "accessible from any machine."

**Workarounds:**
1. Open the repository locally and start a local agent first; the cloud agent will then show the migration option
2. Continue working in the cloud session where context is preserved
```

```text
| **cursorcli** (3,183 LOC) | SQLite + protobuf-ish blobs | byte-scan for field tags + entropy heuristic, then topological sort. Records **no cwd** — the md5 is one-way |

Birthtime and inode are machine-local filesystem facts. No cloud service and no hook payload can ever reconstruct them.

### 7.2 A hook-only design loses the half of the market you actually have

The one hard number on the record ([`ANALYTICS-DATA-RUNBOOK.md:83`](/Users/gdc/specstory-sync/scripts/ANALYTICS-DATA-RUNBOOK.md), full-corpus backfill 2026-07-02):

> 826,868 prod sessions · 249,449 with per-message token data (**30.2%**) · 577,419 token-less (**69.8%**)

Mapping through `PROVIDER_TOKEN_SUPPORT`, `hasTokens: true` is exactly claude-code, codex, gemini — all terminal agents. The 69.8% token-less bucket is, in the runbook author's own words, "Cursor/Copilot era."

**IDE chat is roughly 70% of the all-time cloud corpus.** Caveats: cumulative since 2024, cloud-syncing sessions only, 5 weeks stale. But directionally decisive.

A hook-only plugin keeps claudecode, geminicli, droidcli, and partial codexcli. It loses cursoride, copilotide, Codex's IDE extension and desktop app, Antigravity IDE and desktop, Cursor and Copilot cloud agents — **and all history predating install**, because hooks cannot backfill and a directory scan trivially can.

### 7.3 Server-side parsing breaks the privacy promise

The cloud **already receives `rawData` verbatim** — the untouched native transcript is uploaded alongside the rendered markdown and normalized `sessionData` (`pkg/cloud/sync.go:905`). So moving parsing server-side is technically reachable.

But redaction happens locally, before anything crosses the wire (`pkg/session/session.go:149-151` for markdown; `pkg/cloud/sync.go:801-805` for `rawData` and `sessionData` at send time), it is **default-on** (the flag is negative), and `ResolveProcessingOptions` is deliberately written so a command that forgets to register the flag still gets redaction ON.

The engine is betterleaks — several hundred rules, RE2 via a 4MB WASM module for 20–70× speed. **There is no shell implementation and no JS equivalent.** Moving detection into a Cloudflare Worker means the unredacted transcript is already on the network and already in the isolate before anything is masked. That contradicts the CLI README, the local-first positioning, and the "Privacy First / Your data stays yours" panel in the cloud sign-in UI.

Also: `specstory-sync/ADDING-A-PROVIDER.md:226-260` is an explicit standing commitment against this — *"The cloud is provider-agnostic on purpose… a new branch there is dead code by construction."* Adding a provider costs five cloud files today instead of thousands of lines.

### 7.4 Effort, honestly

~5,000 LOC of irreducible local work (discovery, canonical paths, project identity, idempotent write, token storage) that cannot realistically be written in `sh`, **plus** ~17,000–20,000 LOC of Go parsers ported to TypeScript inside a 128MB isolate, **plus** a redaction engine reimplementation, **plus** ingest chunking the current path lacks (50MB compressed cap, no chunking, 1,257 storage-upload failures already logged in 14 days at current payload sizes).

70:| npm packages | The plugin repo carries **zero bytes of binary**; Cursor's "No binaries are shipped" policy is satisfied; the install cliff disappears because the *client* runs `npx`, not the user |
```

```text
# Summary of Cloud-to-Local Agent Migration Discussion

**Question:**
User asks if a cloud agent can be converted to local mode when returning to their laptop, as continuing a cloud agent keeps changes in the cloud rather than updating local files.

**Dates:**
- Original post: July 9, 2026
- Staff response: July 11, 2026

**Staff Reply:**
Dean Rie confirms this is expected behavior and explains the current functionality.

**Exact Mechanics:**
To move a cloud agent to local:

1. Open the repository locally via File → Open Folder
2. Start a local agent within that repo
3. In the Agents Window, the cloud agent will then display "Move to → Local"
4. Selecting this option transfers the agent, preserving "its changes and chat context"

**Key Limitation:**
"Move to → Local only shows up for a cloud agent when there's already an open local agent for the same repo." The Editor Window lacks this switching capability—migrations only function through the Agents Window.

**Alternative:**
Users can run `git fetch` for the agent's branch, switch to it, and start a fresh chat, though this approach results in "losing the chat history."
```

 `https://cursor.com/docs/cli/changelog`

```text
# CLI Changelog Entries by Feature

## Cloud/Cloud Agents
**June 29, 2026**: "Cloud transfers preserve model and workspace context. For Git repositories with Cloud Agents access, transfers preserve the selected model"

**January 2026**: "Hand off to Cloud Agents. Type `&` to transfer the live conversation to a cloud agent and keep working."

## Resume
**July 6, 2026**: "Resume chats from any directory. `agent ls`, `agent --resume`, and `/resume` open All chats across workspaces by default."

**January 2026**: "`--continue`. Resume your most recent chat without looking up an ID; transcripts persist to disk for tooling and hooks."

## Hooks
**January 2026**: "Hooks. Session start/end, stop hooks with follow-up loops (autonomous 'keep going' patterns), pre-compaction, and subagent lifecycle hooks"

## Sessions/Chats Storage
**July 6, 2026**: "Subagents keep their context across resumes. Completed subagents persist checkpoints, so resuming one restores its prior context"

**January 2026**: "`--continue`. Resume your most recent chat without looking up an ID; transcripts persist to disk for tooling and hooks."

## Worktree
**February 2026**: "Git worktrees. `--worktree`/`-w` runs the agent in an isolated worktree (with `--worktree-base` for the base branch)"

## Headless
**August 11, 2026**: "Single-turn runs wait for their subagents. Headless and single-turn runs drain delegated subagents"

**May 14, 2026**: "Headless runs wait for MCP tools. Fixed a startup race where slow stdio MCP servers were missing"

## Stream-JSON
**May 2026**: "Token usage for scripts. Per-turn input/output/cache token totals and a `request_id` in `stream-json` output"

## ACP (Agent Client Protocol)
**March 2026**: "Editor integrations. Model and mode selection over the Agent Client Protocol (Zed, JetBrains)"
```

```text
I found relevant information about the Cursor SDK TypeScript documentation. Here are the key findings:

## Cloud Runtime & Agent Documentation

The Cursor TypeScript SDK (@cursor/sdk) runs Cursor agents programmatically. It supports the same agent across local workspaces and cloud runtimes, streams agent events as runs progress, and lets you manage prompts, models, cancellation, artifacts, and conversation state from code.

## Conversation Resume

Use Agent.resume() to reattach to an existing agent by ID. You can use this pattern across process boundaries: a cron that continues last night's cleanup, a webhook that extends a user's agent, an interactive CLI that reloads conversation state.

Conversation state from the previous run is loaded automatically. However, inline mcpServers are not persisted across resume — pass them again on the resume call.

## Cloud Runtime Features

Cloud sessions initiated from the SDK run on the same optimized runtime, with each agent getting its own dedicated VM with strong sandboxing, a clone of the repo, and a fully configured development environment. Agents keep going when your laptop sleeps or network drops, and you can stream the conversation and reconnect later.

For the complete official documentation, you can visit the Cursor TypeScript SDK docs at cursor.com/docs/sdk/typescript.
```

```text
Based on the search results, here's what I found about the Cursor Cloud Agents API v0 to v1 migration:

## Key Information

**API Version Changes:**
An updated Cloud Agents API (v1) has been released, reworked around durable agents and per-prompt runs with SSE streaming, reconnect support, explicit lifecycle controls (archive, unarchive, delete), and standardized response/error shapes.

**Architectural Differences:**
v1 separates a durable agent from one or more runs: each prompt submission creates a run on the agent.

**API Versions and Configuration:**
v0 and v1 accept different config keys, and Port sends every key you template (even when it resolves to null), so one node cannot mix API versions or pass both repos and env.

**v0 Endpoints:**
The v0 API includes endpoints like GET /v0/agents (paginated list), GET /v0/agents/{id} (detailed status), GET /v0/agents/{id}/conversation (conversation history), and POST /v0/agents (create and start a new agent).

**Message Format in v0:**
Response messages include objects with id, type (user_message | assistant_message), and text.

The search results show that v0 is the older version still in use, while v1 represents a significant architectural update with improved streaming, durable agent management, and standardized response shapes.
```

```text
## 0. First, read these three things out of the CLI

Every decision below follows from facts that live in the CLI repo, not here. Get them
first and you won't guess.

- **The exact `Name()` string** — `pkg/providers/<name>/*.go`, e.g. `providerName = "Antigravity CLI"`.
  This is the literal `metadata.agentName` the cloud receives, and every lookup here matches
  against it exactly or by substring. Off by one character and icons, display names, and the
  analytics provider resolver all silently fall back to defaults.
- **The provider id** — `pkg/spi/factory/registry.go`, e.g. `r.providers["antigravity"]`.
  This is what `specstory run <id>` takes. It is *not* the binary name: Antigravity's binary
  is `agy`, its id is `antigravity`.
- **`SupportsReconstruction()`** — `pkg/providers/<name>/reconstruct.go`. `true` means the
  agent is a resume *target*; `false` means source-only (we ingest, badge, and resume *out
  of* its sessions, but nothing we write can be resumed *into* it). Decides the `agents.ts`
  entry in step 4.

Also worth a look: the provider's format spec (`specstory-cli/docs/<NAME>-FORMAT.md`) — it
tells you whether the transcript carries per-message token usage, which decides step 5.

Sanity check the wiring assumption: confirm the provider is registered in
`registry.go` **and** that `pkg/session/session.go` syncs it like every other provider
(it passes `session.SessionData.Provider.Name` as the agent name and
`session.SessionDataJSON()` as the resume blob, unconditionally — there is no
per-provider opt-in). If both hold, everything in the "not needed" section stays true.

---

## 4. `sync-cloud/src/lib/agents.ts` — identity tint and resume eligibility

Add the `AgentId` union member and the `AGENTS` entry. The `id` doubles as a **substring
match key**: `agentMeta()` resolves a stored agent name by `agentName.toLowerCase().includes(m.id)`.
Check your new id doesn't collide with an existing one, in either direction, and note that
`AGENT_LIST` order decides who wins a tie.

For `color`, mirror the CLI's own accent for that agent
(`specstory-cli/pkg/cmd/session_tui_browser.go`, `colorForAgent()`) so the terminal and
the web app agree.

**If `SupportsReconstruction()` is `false`, set `resumeTarget: false`.** The Resume hub
renders `RESUME_TARGETS` (a filtered `AGENT_LIST`) under the words "Resume into:";
advertising an agent we cannot write a session for is a false promise to the user. The flag
is the only edit needed — `ResumeHub.tsx` already reads the filtered list, so don't touch
it. (The Antigravity commit does change that file, because it is where the
`AGENT_LIST` → `RESUME_TARGETS` split was introduced. That was one-time work.)

Note what `resumeTarget: false` does *not* mean: those sessions are still cloud-resumable
*out of*. The Resume button is gated on `sessionDataSize > 0`, not on the source agent, and
the CLI uploads a SessionData blob for every provider. An Antigravity session resumes fine
— into Claude Code, Codex, or any other target. The CLI's own picker excludes the
non-reconstructable ones.
```

```text
# Cursor Cloud Agents Integration for Port Workflows

The Cursor cloud agents integration action enables workflows to launch or manage Cursor cloud agents directly through Port. Here's what you need to know:

## Key Prerequisites
- A Cursor Cloud Agents integration installed in your Port organization
- Actions processing enabled (automatic for Port-hosted, must be explicitly enabled for self-hosted deployments)

## Two Core Actions

**Create Agent** (`create_agent`): Launches a new Cursor agent with an initial prompt against a repository, immediately starting a billable run.

**Trigger Agent** (`trigger_agent`): Sends follow-up prompts to existing agents via the v1 API, with serialized runs per agent.

## API Versions & Completion Tracking

The integration supports two Cursor API versions with different behaviors:

- **v0 + `reportCompletion: true`**: Uses webhooks; Port run remains in progress until Cursor completes (requires public URL)
- **v0 + `reportCompletion: false`**: Port run completes immediately after launch
- **v1**: Always completes immediately after launch; `reportCompletion` not supported

## Configuration Methods

Settings can be defined through:
1. Inline values in the workflow node (highest precedence)
2. Repository files (`.cursor/environment.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.cursor/agents/`)
3. Dashboard configuration (team-wide defaults)

The `config` object uses shallow merging—nested objects replace entirely rather than deep-merging.

## Supported Features

- **Models**: Specify model ID (v0) or model object with parameters (v1)
- **Workspaces**: Single repository with ref, PR URL, or named cloud environments
- **MCP Servers**: HTTP or stdio transports; can connect to Port's MCP server via OAuth
- **Custom Subagents**: Named helper agents defined inline or in `.cursor/agents/`
- **Environment Variables**: Session-scoped, encrypted at rest
- **Mode**: Choose between full editing (`agent`) or planning-only (`plan`)

## Important Security Notes

Inline values (including `envVars` and MCP credentials) appear in workflow run outputs, visible to anyone with run access. For durable secrets, use Cursor's dashboard Secrets tab or configured MCP instead of inline values.
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
## `git_id` — derived from the origin remote

Read from the `origin` remote in `.git/config`, normalized, then hashed. Identity
resolution **walks up** from the project directory to the enclosing git root
(`findGitRoot`), so running an agent from a subdirectory of a repo still resolves
to the repo's identity rather than minting a new one per subdirectory.

Normalization (`normalizeGitURL`) is **host-agnostic** — it is not a GitHub
special case. It strips a trailing `.git`, rewrites any `user@host:path` into
`host/path`, and strips any `scheme://` prefix. So every one of these hashes
identically:

| Origin URL                                             | Normalizes to                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| `https://github.com/patterns-ai-core/langchainrb.git`   | `github.com/patterns-ai-core/langchainrb` |
| `git@github.com:patterns-ai-core/langchainrb.git`       | `github.com/patterns-ai-core/langchainrb` |
| `github.com/patterns-ai-core/langchainrb`               | `github.com/patterns-ai-core/langchainrb` |

and the same collapsing applies to any other host — `git@gitlab.com:owner/repo`
and `https://gitlab.com/owner/repo` both normalize to `gitlab.com/owner/repo`.
Because the host is retained, two different forges with the same owner/repo path
do *not* collide.

The practical consequence: **`git_id` is stable across clones, machines, and
users**, so it is the join key for cross-project and cross-machine resume.
```
</details></tool-use>

````text
# Webhook Documentation Summary

## JSON Payload Example
```json
{
  "event": "statusChange",
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "id": "bc_abc123",
  "status": "FINISHED",
  "source": {
    "repository": "https://github.com/your-org/your-repo",
    "ref": "main"
  },
  "target": {
    "url": "https://cursor.com/agents?id=bc_abc123",
    "branchName": "cursor/add-readme-1234",
    "prUrl": "https://github.com/your-org/your-repo/pull/1234"
  },
  "summary": "Added README.md with installation instructions"
}
```

## Headers
- **`X-Webhook-Signature`** – Contains the HMAC-SHA256 signature in the format `sha256=<hex_digest>`
- **`X-Webhook-ID`** – A unique identifier for this delivery (useful for logging)
- **`X-Webhook-Event`** – The event type (currently only `statusChange`)
- **`User-Agent`** – Always set to `Cursor-Agent-Webhook/1.0`

## Verification Code Samples

**JavaScript:**
```javascript
const crypto = require("crypto");

function verifyWebhook(secret, rawBody, signature) {
  const expectedSignature =
    "sha256=" +
    crypto.createHmac("sha256", secret).update(rawBody).digest("hex");

  return signature === expectedSignature;
}
```

**Python:**
```python
import hmac
import hashlib

def verify_webhook(secret, raw_body, signature):
    expected_signature = 'sha256=' + hmac.new(
        secret.encode(),
        raw_body,
        hashlib.sha256
    ).hexdigest()

    return signature == expected_signature
```

## Important Note
"Always use the raw request body (before any parsing) when computing the signature."

**Note:** The documentation contains no references to v0/v1 support or "coming soon" features.
````

````text
# Cursor TypeScript SDK: Key Technical Details

## Cloud Runtime Specification

The cloud runtime is activated by passing a `cloud` configuration object to `Agent.create()`:

```typescript
const agent = await Agent.create({
  apiKey: process.env.CURSOR_API_KEY!,
  model: { id: "composer-2.5" },
  cloud: {
    repos: [{ url: "https://github.com/your-org/your-repo" }],
  },
});
```

The documentation states: `"Runtime is picked by which key you pass to Agent.create() (local or cloud)."` Cloud agents run in an isolated VM with your repository cloned in, managed by Cursor's infrastructure.

## Agent Resumption

Use `Agent.resume(agentId)` to reattach to existing agents. The runtime is automatically detected from the ID prefix—`bc-` indicates cloud agents, while other prefixes denote local agents. This enables continuing conversations after process restarts.

## Reading Conversation History

Several methods retrieve conversation data:

- **`run.conversation()`**: Returns a structured `ConversationTurn[]` showing per-turn transcript with steps
- **`Agent.messages.list(agentId)`**: Lists stored user and assistant messages for local agents
- **Streaming via `run.stream()`**: Yields normalized `SDKMessage` events including assistant text, thinking, and tool calls

Tool calls appear in streams as `SDKToolUseMessage` events with `status`, `args`, and `result` fields, though the documentation notes: `"Tool call schema is not stable...treat args and result as unknown."`

## Stream Events

The `run.stream()` method emits discriminated events including:
- `"assistant"` (model text output)
- `"thinking"` (reasoning content)
- `"tool_call"` (tool invocation lifecycle)
- `"status"` (cloud lifecycle transitions)
- `"usage"` (per-turn token counts)

## Artifacts

List and download files from agent workspaces:

```typescript
const artifacts = await agent.listArtifacts();
const buffer = await agent.downloadArtifact(artifacts[0].path);
```

Artifact support is runtime-dependent; local agents currently return no artifacts.

## State Storage

Local agents persist to disk via a configurable `LocalAgentStore` (defaults to SQLite). The documentation explains: `"Each call to agent.send() loads the latest checkpoint for that agent...the store survives process restarts."` Cloud agents persist server-side automatically.

## Plan Mode

Pass `mode: "plan"` or `mode: "agent"` to control whether runs explore first or implement directly.

## API Key Sources

The SDK resolves credentials in this order: explicit `apiKey` parameter → `CURSOR_API_KEY` environment variable → stored browser login via `Cursor.auth.login()`. Both user and service account keys are supported; Team Admin keys are not yet supported.
````

```text
// The callback includes the provider ID to help consumers route/filter sessions.
// The callback should not block as it may delay other provider notifications.
func WatchProviders(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, providers map[string]spi.Provider, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(providerID string, session *spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
	slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting multi-provider watch", "projectPath", projectPath, "providerCount", len(providers), "debugRaw", debugRaw)

	// Track a per-provider, per-session content fingerprint to suppress duplicate callbacks.
	// Providers fire callbacks on every session-file change, but not all changes
	// produce new content in the parsed SessionData (e.g. UI metadata updates).
	// The message count alone is not enough: patch-log providers (e.g. VS Code
	// Copilot) stream an agent response by growing the text of an existing
	// message in place, so the count stays flat while the content changes.
	var mu sync.Mutex
	lastFingerprint := make(map[string]sessionFingerprint)

	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	errChan := make(chan error, len(providers))

	for providerID, provider := range providers {
		wg.Go(func() {
			slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting watcher for provider", "providerID", providerID, "providerName", provider.Name())

			// Wrap the callback to deduplicate and include provider ID
			wrappedCallback := func(session *spi.AgentChatSession) {
				if session == nil || session.SessionData == nil {
					return
				}

				fingerprint := fingerprintSession(session)

				// Key by provider as well as session: the map is shared across all
				// provider goroutines, and without the scope two providers emitting
				// the same session ID would suppress each other's callbacks.
				dedupKey := providerID + "/" + session.SessionID

				// Skip if the parsed content hasn't changed for this session
				mu.Lock()
				prev, seen := lastFingerprint[dedupKey]
				if seen && prev == fingerprint {
					mu.Unlock()
					slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Skipping duplicate callback",
						"providerID", providerID,
						"sessionID", session.SessionID,
						"messages", fingerprint.messages,
						"contentBytes", fingerprint.contentBytes)
					return
				}
				lastFingerprint[dedupKey] = fingerprint
				mu.Unlock()

				slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Provider callback fired",
					"providerID", providerID,
					"sessionID", session.SessionID,
					"messages", fingerprint.messages,
					"contentBytes", fingerprint.contentBytes)

				sessionCallback(providerID, session)
			}

			err := provider.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, wrappedCallback)
			if err != nil {
				// Context cancellation is expected when user presses Ctrl+C, not an error
				if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
					slog.Info("WatchProviders: Provider watcher stopped", "provider", provider.Name())
					errChan <- nil
				} else {
					slog.Error("WatchProviders: Provider watcher failed", "provider", provider.Name(), "error", err)
					errChan <- fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", provider.Name(), err)
				}
			} else {
				errChan <- nil
			}
```

```text
# Privacy Mode and Data Storage Summary

## Privacy Mode Variants

The document mentions only **Privacy Mode** as the primary privacy control. It's described as ensuring "your code is never used for training by Cursor or other AI model providers." The document does not reference "Privacy Mode (Legacy)" or other variants.

## Chat History and Cloud Storage

The provided content **does not address whether chat history is stored on Cursor servers or synced across devices**. This information is absent from the page.

## Application to Cloud Agents

Privacy Mode applies uniformly across AI features. The document states: "Privacy Mode works the same for Grok 4.5 as for every other model. With Privacy Mode enabled, your code is never used for training."

For Cloud Agents specifically, the document notes that "the agent loop stays in Cursor's cloud" with Self-Hosted Machines, and Privacy Mode applies identically in this context.

## Data Deletion and Retention

Cursor maintains **zero data retention (ZDR)** agreements as the default, except when:
- Users employ their own API keys
- Specific models require provider-side retention (these are "off by default")

For personal data deletion requests, users should "contact support with your account email, the agent name, and a description of the files."
```

```text
# Audit Logs and Monitoring Features

## Audit Log Contents

Audit logs track administrative changes including "sign-ins, membership, roles, API keys, settings, integrations, Cloud Agent environments, Grok Bot configuration, and Origin repositories."

**Explicitly excluded:** Payloads "never" contain "prompts, agent output, generated code, or credentials." Failed login attempts and secret values are also omitted.

## Admin Monitoring Capabilities

Administrators can "view audit logs in the team dashboard" and "filter by date range, event type, actor, or application, then export the filtered result to CSV." The Admin API enables programmatic access via `GET /teams/audit-logs` and `GET /organizations/audit-logs` endpoints.

## Cloud Agent Events

The system logs Cloud Agent activities including secret creation/updates, environment lifecycle changes, protected Git scope access, and secret reads during automation runs.

## Data Retention & Export

The documentation specifies audit logs default to "the last 7 days" and support "up to a 30-day window." Organizations can stream events to external platforms (Splunk, Sumo Logic, webhooks, S3) for extended retention.

## OpenTelemetry Export

Beyond audit logs, the platform offers "OpenTelemetry Export" for "token, tool call, and cost metrics, API request and cloud agent logs, and recorded Grok Bot actions" on the Enterprise plan—a "separate pipeline" from audit-log streaming.
```

```text
78	// FindProjectComposerIDs returns the composer IDs associated with the project, merging
79	// the two association sources that exist across Cursor versions:
80	//
81	//  1. Workspace-DB references (composer.composerData / workbench.panel keys) — Cursor 2
82	//     and early Cursor 3 record every conversation there.
83	//  2. The workspaceIdentifier embedded in each global composerData row — in Cursor
84	//     >= 3.12 the workspace DB no longer records conversations at all, and the global
85	//     composer.composerHeaders key is flushed lazily (often not until Cursor exits),
86	//     so this embedded field is the only association that updates live.
87	//
88	// The global scan reads every composerData row (headers only, no bubbles), so the
89	// cost of parsing the composer rows is acceptable. Callers that already hold the
90	// scanned map should use projectComposerIDs directly instead of scanning again.
91	func FindProjectComposerIDs(globalDbPath, projectPath string, workspaces []vscode.WorkspaceEntry) ([]string, error) {
92		composers, err := LoadAllComposerDataLightweight(globalDbPath)
93		if err != nil {
94			// The workspace-DB IDs may still be usable (older Cursor versions), so degrade
95			// to source 1 rather than failing the whole lookup.
96			slog.Warn("Failed to load global composer data for workspaceIdentifier matching", "error", err)
97			composers = nil
98		}
99		return projectComposerIDs(composers, projectPath, workspaces)
100	}
101	
102	// projectComposerIDs is the load-free core of FindProjectComposerIDs: it matches an
103	// already-scanned composer map against the project. Split out so callers that need the
104	// scanned map for their own purposes too (e.g. the watcher's seeding, which also reads
105	// the timestamps) don't scan the global database twice.
106	func projectComposerIDs(composers map[string]*ComposerData, projectPath string, workspaces []vscode.WorkspaceEntry) ([]string, error) {
107		ids, err := LoadComposerIDsFromAllWorkspaces(workspaces)
108		if err != nil {
109			return nil, err
110		}
111		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(ids))
112		for _, id := range ids {
113			seen[id] = true
114		}
115	
116		canonicalProject, err := vscode.NormalizePathForComparison(projectPath)
117		if err != nil {
118			canonicalProject = projectPath
119		}
120		workspaceIDs := make(map[string]bool, len(workspaces))
121		for _, ws := range workspaces {
122			workspaceIDs[ws.ID] = true
123		}
124	
125		for composerID, composer := range composers {
126			if seen[composerID] || !composerBelongsToProject(composer, workspaceIDs, canonicalProject) {
127				continue
128			}
129			seen[composerID] = true
130			ids = append(ids, composerID)
131		}
132	
133		slog.Debug("Resolved project composer IDs", "count", len(ids), "projectPath", projectPath)
134		return ids, nil
135	}
136	
137	// composerBelongsToProject implements the embedded-workspaceIdentifier match of
138	// FindProjectComposerIDs (source 2 in its doc comment).
139	func composerBelongsToProject(composer *ComposerData, workspaceIDs map[string]bool, canonicalProject string) bool {
140		wi := composer.WorkspaceIdentifier
141		if wi == nil {
142			return false
143		}
144		if workspaceIDs[wi.ID] {
145			return true
146		}
147		if wi.URI == nil || wi.URI.FsPath == "" {
148			return false
149		}
150		canonicalComposer, err := vscode.NormalizePathForComparison(wi.URI.FsPath)
151		if err != nil {
152			canonicalComposer = wi.URI.FsPath
153		}
154		return canonicalComposer == canonicalProject
155	}
156	
157	// LoadComposerIDsFromAllWorkspaces loads and deduplicates composer IDs from all matching workspaces.
158	// This handles WSL environments where the same project may have multiple workspace entries.
159	// NOTE: this only covers Cursor 2 / early Cursor 3 — newer versions stopped recording
160	// conversations in the workspace DB entirely; use FindProjectComposerIDs for full coverage.
```

```text
The system enables developers to configure cloud environments in under 10 minutes. Regarding agent mobility: "Move agent sessions more reliably between your local computer and the cloud. You can offload long-running work from your machine and run as many cloud agents in parallel as you want. Pull a cloud agent back down to local to test changes yourself."
```
