```text
1	package spi
2	
3	import (
4		"os"
5		"path/filepath"
6		"regexp"
7		"strings"
8	)
9	
10	// Git origin helpers shared by project identity (pkg/utils) and by providers
11	// that match sessions to a project by repository rather than by directory. They
12	// live here because providers may not import pkg/utils, and a provider that
13	// normalized URLs its own way would attribute sessions to a different project
14	// than the git_id the rest of the CLI computes.
15	
16	// originRemoteURLRegex captures the origin remote's url value from a git config file.
17	var originRemoteURLRegex = regexp.MustCompile(`\[remote "origin"\][^\[]*url\s*=\s*([^\n\r]+)`)
18	
19	// NormalizeGitRemoteURL reduces a git remote URL to host/owner/repo so that the
20	// HTTPS, SSH and scheme-less spellings of one repository compare equal. It is
21	// the normalization the CLI hashes into a project's git_id.
22	func NormalizeGitRemoteURL(gitURL string) string {
23		normalized := strings.TrimSuffix(gitURL, ".git")
24	
25		// scp-like SSH form (git@host:owner/repo or user@host:owner/repo) becomes host/path.
26		if strings.Contains(normalized, "@") && strings.Contains(normalized, ":") {
27			parts := strings.SplitN(normalized, "@", 2)
28			if len(parts) == 2 {
29				hostAndPath := strings.SplitN(parts[1], ":", 2)
30				if len(hostAndPath) == 2 {
31					return hostAndPath[0] + "/" + hostAndPath[1]
32				}
33			}
34		}
35	
36		// Any scheme (https://, git://, ssh://) is dropped so only host/path remains.
37		if _, rest, ok := strings.Cut(normalized, "://"); ok {
38			return rest
39		}
40	
41		// Already host/owner/repo.
42		return normalized
43	}
44	
45	// GitOriginURL returns the origin remote URL of the repository containing dir,
46	// walking up to the git root first so a subdirectory of a repository resolves
47	// to that repository. Returns "" when dir is not inside a repository or the
48	// repository has no origin remote.
49	func GitOriginURL(dir string) string {
50		root, ok := FindGitRoot(dir)
51		if !ok {
52			return ""
53		}
54		configPath := gitConfigPath(root)
55		if configPath == "" {
56			return ""
57		}
58		return readOriginURL(configPath)
59	}
60	
61	// FindGitRoot walks up from dir to the nearest ancestor containing a .git entry and
62	// returns it. The .git entry may be a directory (normal clone) or a file (git
63	// worktree or submodule); both satisfy the search. Returns false if no .git is
64	// found before the filesystem root.
65	func FindGitRoot(dir string) (string, bool) {
66		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(dir); err == nil {
67			dir = abs
68		}
69		dir = filepath.Clean(dir)
70		for {
71			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, ".git")); err == nil {
72				return dir, true
73			}
74			parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
75			if parent == dir {
76				return "", false
77			}
78			dir = parent
79		}
80	}
81	
82	// readOriginURL returns the origin remote URL from a git config file, or "" if the
83	// file is unreadable or has no origin remote.
84	func readOriginURL(gitConfigPath string) string {
85		gitConfig, err := os.ReadFile(gitConfigPath)
86		if err != nil {
87			return ""
88		}
89		matches := originRemoteURLRegex.FindSubmatch(gitConfig)
90		if len(matches) < 2 {
91			return ""
92		}
93		return strings.TrimSpace(string(matches[1]))
94	}
95	
96	// gitConfigPath returns the path to the git config file that holds a root's
97	// remotes, handling both a normal .git directory and a .git file (worktrees and
98	// submodules, whose private gitdir points at a commondir that holds the shared
99	// config). Returns "" when it cannot be resolved.
100	func gitConfigPath(gitRoot string) string {
101		gitPath := filepath.Join(gitRoot, ".git")
102		info, err := os.Stat(gitPath)
103		if err != nil {
104			return ""
105		}
106		if info.IsDir() {
107			return filepath.Join(gitPath, "config")
108		}
109	
110		// A .git file reads "gitdir: <path>" and points at the worktree's private git
111		// dir; the shared config lives in the common dir, not that private dir.
112		data, err := os.ReadFile(gitPath)
113		if err != nil {
114			return ""
115		}
116		content := strings.TrimSpace(string(data))
117		if !strings.HasPrefix(content, "gitdir:") {
118			return ""
119		}
120		gitDir := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(content, "gitdir:"))
121		if gitDir == "" {
122			return ""
123		}
124		if !filepath.IsAbs(gitDir) {
125			gitDir = filepath.Join(gitRoot, gitDir)
126		}
127		commonDir := gitDir
128		if cd, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(gitDir, "commondir")); err == nil {
129			c := strings.TrimSpace(string(cd))
130			if !filepath.IsAbs(c) {
131				c = filepath.Join(gitDir, c)
132			}
133			commonDir = filepath.Clean(c)
134		}
135		return filepath.Join(commonDir, "config")
136	}
137
```

```text
34	// streamIdleTimeout bounds how long a stream read may see no bytes before the
35	// connection is treated as dead. The live stream sends a heartbeat event while
36	// the agent is quiet, so 90 seconds of silence means the connection is gone.
37	// A variable so tests can shorten it.

44	// apiError is a non-success HTTP response from the Cloud Agents API, carrying

46	type apiError struct {
47		Status  int
48		Code    string
49		Message string
50	}
51	
52	func (e *apiError) Error() string {
53		if e.Message != "" {
54			return fmt.Sprintf("cursor api: HTTP %d %s: %s", e.Status, e.Code, e.Message)
55		}
56		return fmt.Sprintf("cursor api: HTTP %d", e.Status)
57	}

59	// isNotFound reports whether err is a 404 from the API.
60	func isNotFound(err error) bool {
61		var ae *apiError
62		return errors.As(err, &ae) && ae.Status == http.StatusNotFound
63	}
64	
65	// rateLimiter spaces requests at least interval apart across every caller in
66	// the process: sync, watch polling and live streams all draw from one budget
67	// because the API limit is per key, not per connection.
68	type rateLimiter struct {
69		mu       sync.Mutex
70		interval time.Duration
71		next     time.Time
72		now      func() time.Time
73		sleep    func(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) error
74	}
75	
76	func newRateLimiter(interval time.Duration) *rateLimiter {
77		return &rateLimiter{interval: interval, now: time.Now, sleep: sleepContext}
78	}
79	
80	// wait blocks until the caller may send its request, reserving the slot before
81	// sleeping so concurrent callers queue behind each other instead of all waking
82	// at the same instant.
83	func (l *rateLimiter) wait(ctx context.Context) error {
84		l.mu.Lock()
85		now := l.now()
86		slot := l.next
87		if slot.Before(now) {
88			slot = now
89		}
90		l.next = slot.Add(l.interval)
91		l.mu.Unlock()
92	
93		if d := slot.Sub(now); d > 0 {
94			return l.sleep(ctx, d)
95		}
96		return nil
97	}
98	
99	// holdUntil pushes every future slot to at least t, so a 429 seen by one
100	// caller also slows the others rather than letting them hit the limit again.
101	func (l *rateLimiter) holdUntil(t time.Time) {
102		l.mu.Lock()
103		if l.next.Before(t) {
104			l.next = t
105		}
106		l.mu.Unlock()
107	}
108	
109	// sleepContext sleeps for d or until ctx is done.
110	func sleepContext(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) error {
111		timer := time.NewTimer(d)
112		defer timer.Stop()
113		select {
114		case <-ctx.Done():
115			return ctx.Err()
116		case <-timer.C:
117			return nil
118		}
119	}

124	// apiClient talks to the Cloud Agents API with one key.
125	type apiClient struct {

130		limiter    *rateLimiter
131	}
132	
133	// newAPIClient builds a client for key. JSON calls carry a whole-request
134	// timeout; stream calls cannot (a live run streams for minutes), so they rely
135	// on the idle deadline in openStream instead.
136	func newAPIClient(key string) *apiClient {
137		return &apiClient{
138			key:        key,
139			baseURL:    apiBaseURL,
140			jsonHTTP:   &http.Client{Timeout: jsonTimeout},
141			streamHTTP: &http.Client{},
142			limiter:    sharedLimiter,
143		}
144	}

146	// do sends one request built by build, waiting for the rate limiter first and
147	// retrying 429 and 5xx responses with Retry-After or exponential backoff. A
148	// 2xx response is returned open; anything else is returned as *apiError.
149	func (c *apiClient) do(ctx context.Context, httpClient *http.Client, build func(ctx context.Context) (*http.Request, error)) (*http.Response, error) {
150		backoff := initialBackoff
151		for attempt := 0; ; attempt++ {
152			if err := c.limiter.wait(ctx); err != nil {
153				return nil, err
154			}
155			req, err := build(ctx)
156			if err != nil {
157				return nil, err
158			}
159			req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+c.key)
160			resp, err := httpClient.Do(req)
161			if err != nil {
162				return nil, err
163			}
164			if resp.StatusCode >= 200 && resp.StatusCode < 300 {
165				return resp, nil
166			}
167	
168			apiErr := readAPIError(resp)
169			retryable := resp.StatusCode == http.StatusTooManyRequests || resp.StatusCode >= 500
170			if !retryable || attempt >= maxRetries {
171				return nil, apiErr
172			}
173	
174			delay := retryAfter(resp.Header.Get("Retry-After"), c.limiter.now())
175			if delay <= 0 {
176				delay = backoff
177				backoff = min(backoff*2, maxBackoff)
178			}
179			slog.Warn("Cursor API request throttled or failed, retrying",
180				"path", req.URL.Path, "status", resp.StatusCode, "delay", delay, "attempt", attempt+1)
181			c.limiter.holdUntil(c.limiter.now().Add(delay))
182		}
183	}

185	// readAPIError drains and closes resp, decoding the API's error envelope.
186	func readAPIError(resp *http.Response) *apiError {
187		defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
188		apiErr := &apiError{Status: resp.StatusCode}
189		// The error envelope is small; the cap only guards against a proxy page.
190		body, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 64*1024))
191		var envelope struct {
192			Error struct {
193				Code    string `json:"code"`
194				Message string `json:"message"`
195			} `json:"error"`
196		}
197		if json.Unmarshal(body, &envelope) == nil {
198			apiErr.Code = envelope.Error.Code
199			apiErr.Message = envelope.Error.Message
200		}
201		return apiErr
202	}

204	// retryAfter parses a Retry-After header, either delay-seconds or an HTTP
205	// date, returning zero when the header is absent or unparseable.
206	func retryAfter(header string, now time.Time) time.Duration {
207		if header == "" {
208			return 0
209		}
210		if secs, err := strconv.Atoi(header); err == nil && secs > 0 {
211			return time.Duration(secs) * time.Second
212		}
213		if t, err := http.ParseTime(header); err == nil {
214			return t.Sub(now)
215		}
216		return 0
217	}

223		resp, err := c.do(ctx, c.jsonHTTP, func(ctx context.Context) (*http.Request, error) {
224			req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, c.baseURL+path, nil)
225			if err == nil {

236			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
237		}
238		if !json.Valid(body) {
239			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read %s: response is not JSON", path)
240		}
241		return json.RawMessage(body), nil
242	}

348	// openStream opens a run's SSE stream. lastEventID, when set, resumes after
349	// that event. The returned body cancels its request once no bytes arrive for

351	// instead of hanging forever. A 410 maps to errStreamExpired.
352	func (c *apiClient) openStream(ctx context.Context, agentID, runID, lastEventID string) (io.ReadCloser, error) {
353		streamCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
354		path := "/v1/agents/" + url.PathEscape(agentID) + "/runs/" + url.PathEscape(runID) + "/stream"
355		resp, err := c.do(streamCtx, c.streamHTTP, func(ctx context.Context) (*http.Request, error) {

393		}

395	}
```

```text
package cursorcloud

import (
	"bufio"
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
)

// apiMe is the subset of GET /v1/me that Check reports.
type apiMe struct {
	APIKeyName string `json:"apiKeyName"`
}

// apiAgent is the subset of a v1 agent object the provider reads. The raw
// bytes travel alongside it (agentRecord) so unknown fields reach the mirror.
type apiAgent struct {
	ID          string    `json:"id"`
	Name        string    `json:"name"`
	Status      string    `json:"status"`
	Repos       []apiRepo `json:"repos"`
	URL         string    `json:"url"`
	CreatedAt   string    `json:"createdAt"`
	UpdatedAt   string    `json:"updatedAt"`
	LatestRunID string    `json:"latestRunId"`
}

type apiRepo struct {
	URL string `json:"url"`
}

// apiRun is the subset of a v1 run object the provider reads.
type apiRun struct {
	ID         string `json:"id"`
	AgentID    string `json:"agentId"`
	Status     string `json:"status"`
	CreatedAt  string `json:"createdAt"`
	UpdatedAt  string `json:"updatedAt"`
	DurationMs int64  `json:"durationMs"`
	Git        struct {
		Branches []struct {
			RepoURL string `json:"repoUrl"`
			Branch  string `json:"branch"`
			PrURL   string `json:"prUrl"`
		} `json:"branches"`
	} `json:"git"`
}

// isTerminal reports whether a run status is final. The non-terminal statuses
// observed are CREATING and RUNNING; anything else is treated as terminal so an
// unfamiliar final status never keeps a live stream attached forever.
func (r apiRun) isTerminal() bool {
	return r.Status != "CREATING" && r.Status != "RUNNING"
}

// v0Conversation is GET /v0/agents/{id}/conversation: text-only messages for
// every run of the agent, in order.
type v0Conversation struct {
	ID       string      `json:"id"`
	Messages []v0Message `json:"messages"`
}

type v0Message struct {
	ID   string `json:"id"`
	Type string `json:"type"`
	Text string `json:"text"`
}

// agentRecord pairs a decoded agent with its native bytes.
type agentRecord struct {
	raw   json.RawMessage
	agent apiAgent
}

// runRecord pairs a decoded run with its native bytes.
type runRecord struct {
	raw json.RawMessage
	run apiRun
}

func decodeAgent(raw json.RawMessage) (agentRecord, error) {
	var agent apiAgent
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &agent); err != nil {
		return agentRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("decode agent: %w", err)
	}
	if !validAgentID(agent.ID) {
		return agentRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("decode agent: unexpected id %q", agent.ID)
	}
	return agentRecord{raw: raw, agent: agent}, nil
}

func decodeRun(raw json.RawMessage) (runRecord, error) {
	var run apiRun
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &run); err != nil {
		return runRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("decode run: %w", err)
	}
	if !validRunID(run.ID) {
		return runRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("decode run: unexpected id %q", run.ID)
	}
	return runRecord{raw: raw, run: run}, nil
}

// sseEvent is one SSE block as the mirror stores it: one JSON object per line
// of a run's events file.
type sseEvent struct {
	ID    string          `json:"id,omitempty"`
	Event string          `json:"event"`
	Data  json.RawMessage `json:"data"`
}

// maxSSELineSize caps one SSE line, and so one block. A variable so tests can
// exercise the oversized path without allocating 64MB.
var maxSSELineSize = spi.MaxRecordLineSize

// readSSE parses an SSE byte stream, calling emit for each complete block in
// order. A block holding an oversized line is skipped with a warning rather
// than ending the stream. Comment lines (": keepalive") are ignored. emit
// returning false stops the read early (used once the done event arrives).
func readSSE(r io.Reader, source string, emit func(sseEvent) bool) error {
	reader := bufio.NewReader(r)
	var id, event string
	var data strings.Builder
	hasData, skipBlock := false, false
	lineNo := 0

	dispatch := func() bool {
		defer func() {
			id, event = "", ""
			data.Reset()
			hasData, skipBlock = false, false
		}()
		if skipBlock {
			slog.Warn("Skipping oversized SSE block", "source", source, "line", lineNo)
			return true
		}
		if event == "" && !hasData {
			return true
		}
		if event == "" {
			// The SSE default event type; never observed from this API.
			event = "message"
		}
		return emit(sseEvent{ID: id, Event: event, Data: sseData(data.String(), hasData)})
	}

	for {
		line, oversized, err := spi.ReadRecordLine(reader, maxSSELineSize)
		if len(line) > 0 || oversized {
			lineNo++
		}
		if oversized {
			skipBlock = true
		} else if len(line) > 0 || err == nil {
			text := strings.TrimRight(string(line), "\r\n")
			if text == "" {
				if !dispatch() {
					return nil
				}
			} else if !strings.HasPrefix(text, ":") {
				field, value, _ := strings.Cut(text, ":")
				value = strings.TrimPrefix(value, " ")
				switch field {
				case "id":
					id = value
				case "event":
					event = value
				case "data":
					if hasData {
						data.WriteString("\n")
					}
					data.WriteString(value)
					hasData = true
				}
			}
		}
		if err != nil {
			if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
				dispatch()
				return nil
			}
			return err
		}
	}
}

// sseData keeps a data payload as JSON. Every payload observed is a JSON
// object; anything else is preserved as a JSON string so no content is lost.
func sseData(text string, hasData bool) json.RawMessage {
	if !hasData {
		return nil
	}
	if json.Valid([]byte(text)) {
		return json.RawMessage(text)
	}
	quoted, _ := json.Marshal(text)
	return quoted
}

// eventsAreWhole reports whether a run's recorded events end with the done
// event, which the stream sends only after the run's final result.
func eventsAreWhole(events []sseEvent) bool {
	return len(events) > 0 && events[len(events)-1].Event == "done"
}

// encodeEvents renders events as JSONL for the mirror.
func encodeEvents(events []sseEvent) ([]byte, error) {
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	for _, event := range events {
		line, err := json.Marshal(event)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		buf.Write(line)
		buf.WriteByte('\n')
	}
	return buf.Bytes(), nil
}

// readEventsFile reads a run's mirrored events. A missing file is no events.
// Malformed or oversized lines are skipped with a warning so one bad record
// costs one event, not the run.
func readEventsFile(path string) ([]sseEvent, error) {
	f, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return nil, nil
		}
		return nil, err
	}
	defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()

	var events []sseEvent
	reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
	for lineNo := 1; ; lineNo++ {
		line, oversized, err := spi.ReadRecordLine(reader, spi.MaxRecordLineSize)
		if oversized {
			slog.Warn("Skipping oversized JSONL line", "file", path, "line", lineNo)
		} else if trimmed := bytes.TrimSpace(line); len(trimmed) > 0 {
			var event sseEvent
			if jsonErr := json.Unmarshal(trimmed, &event); jsonErr != nil || event.Event == "" {
				slog.Warn("Skipping corrupted JSONL line", "file", path, "line", lineNo, "error", jsonErr)
			} else {
				events = append(events, event)
			}
		}
		if err != nil {
			if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
				return events, nil
			}
			return events, err
		}
	}
}

// eventTime converts an SSE id ("<epochMillis>-<seq>") to an RFC 3339 UTC
// timestamp. The id is the only timestamp the stream carries. Returns "" when
// the id is absent (status events carry none) or malformed.
func eventTime(id string) string {
	t, ok := eventInstant(id)
	if !ok {
		return ""
	}
	return spi.RFC3339Millis(t)
}

// eventInstant parses the epoch-millisecond prefix of an SSE id.
func eventInstant(id string) (time.Time, bool) {
	millis, _, _ := strings.Cut(id, "-")
	ms, err := strconv.ParseInt(millis, 10, 64)
	if err != nil || ms <= 0 {
		return time.Time{}, false
	}
	return time.UnixMilli(ms).UTC(), true
}

// validAgentID and validRunID guard ids before they become mirror path
// components; ids come from the network and are untrusted. Observed shapes are
// bc-<uuid> and run-<uuid>.
func validAgentID(id string) bool { return validPrefixedID(id, "bc-") }
func validRunID(id string) bool   { return validPrefixedID(id, "run-") }

func validPrefixedID(id, prefix string) bool {
	rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(id, prefix)
	if !ok || rest == "" || len(rest) > 64 {
		return false
	}
	for _, r := range rest {
		isHex := (r >= '0' && r <= '9') || (r >= 'a' && r <= 'f') || (r >= 'A' && r <= 'F')
		if !isHex && r != '-' {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}
```

```text
== pkg/providers/cursorcloud/markdown_tools.go
package cursorcloud

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"sort"
	"strings"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
)

// maxResultRunes caps a rendered tool result. Results (file contents, command
// output, fetched pages) can be arbitrarily large; the mirror and RawData keep
// the full value, so the markdown preview is capped with a visible marker.
const maxResultRunes = 50000

// plumbingInputKeys are identifiers the harness copies into tool arguments on
// every call (observed on run_terminal_cmd); they say nothing about the call.
var plumbingInputKeys = []string{"toolCallId", "conversationId", "requestId"}

// shellInputNoise are run_terminal_cmd arguments that restate the command
// (parsingResult, simpleCommands) or are harness execution settings identical
// on every observed call (timeouts, output thresholds, stdin handling).
var shellInputNoise = []string{
	"parsingResult", "simpleCommands", "timeout", "hardTimeout",
	"timeoutBehavior", "fileOutputThresholdBytes", "closeStdin",
}

// toolType classifies a tool by the name recorded in tool_call events. Every
// name here was observed in a captured stream; see examples/tools.txt.
func toolType(name string) string {
	switch name {
	case "run_terminal_cmd":
		return schema.ToolTypeShell
	case "read_file", "web_fetch":
		return schema.ToolTypeRead
	case "edit_file", "delete_file":
		return schema.ToolTypeWrite
	case "file_search", "grep_search", "web_search":
		return schema.ToolTypeSearch
	case "todo_write":
		return schema.ToolTypeTask
	// Agent-state and harness tools: MCP plumbing, background waits, canvases,
	// generated assets, pull request management (seen in the research spike).
	case "mcp", "get_mcp_tools", "await", "generate_image",
		"write_canvas", "read_canvas", "pr_management":
		return schema.ToolTypeGeneric
	default:
		return schema.ToolTypeUnknown
	}
}

// cleanToolInput returns a copy of the recorded args without plumbing keys.
// Shell noise stays in the stored Input (it is real data) and is only hidden
// from the rendered body.
func cleanToolInput(args map[string]any) map[string]any {
	if args == nil {
		return nil
	}
	cleaned := make(map[string]any, len(args))
	for key, value := range args {
		if !slices.Contains(plumbingInputKeys, key) {
			cleaned[key] = value
		}
	}
	return cleaned
}

// formatTool renders a tool call. It sets tool.Summary and returns the body
// that becomes FormattedMarkdown: the rendered input, then the rendered result.
// The VM's /workspace prefix is shown relative so paths read like the repo.
func formatTool(tool *schema.ToolInfo) string {
	if tool == nil {
		return ""
	}
	if summary := toolSummary(tool); summary != "" {
		tool.Summary = &summary
	}

	body := strings.TrimSpace(formatToolInput(tool))
	result := strings.TrimSpace(formatToolResult(tool))

	var b strings.Builder
	if body != "" {
		b.WriteString("\n")
		b.WriteString(body)
	}
	if result != "" {
		if body != "" {
			b.WriteString("\n\n")
		} else {
			b.WriteString("\n")
		}
		b.WriteString(result)
	}
	if b.Len() > 0 {
		b.WriteString("\n")
	}
	return b.String()
}

// toolSummary names the call and its key argument.
func toolSummary(tool *schema.ToolInfo) string {
	in := tool.Input
	var key string
	switch tool.Name {
	case "read_file", "edit_file", "delete_file":
		key = displayPath(spi.StringValue(in, "path"))
	case "run_terminal_cmd":
		key = spi.StringValue(in, "description")
	case "file_search":
		key = spi.StringValue(in, "globPattern")
	case "grep_search":
		key = spi.StringValue(in, "pattern")
	case "web_search":
		key = spi.StringValue(in, "searchTerm")
	case "web_fetch":
		key = spi.StringValue(in, "url")
	case "mcp":
		key = spi.StringValue(in, "name")
	case "get_mcp_tools":
		key = strings.Trim(spi.StringValue(in, "server")+"/"+spi.StringValue(in, "toolName"), "/")
	case "write_canvas":
		key = spi.StringValue(in, "title")
	case "generate_image":
		key = displayPath(spi.StringValue(in, "filePath"))
	}
	if key == "" {
		return ""
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** %s", tool.Name, spi.InlineCode(key))
}

// formatToolInput renders the arguments as labeled lines. Unenumerated tools
// fall back to pretty-printed JSON so no input is ever dropped.
func formatToolInput(tool *schema.ToolInfo) string {
	in := tool.Input
	switch tool.Name {
	case "run_terminal_cmd":
		return formatShellInput(in)
	case "read_file", "delete_file", "web_fetch", "web_search", "file_search":
		return formatLabeledInput(in, tool.Name)
	case "edit_file":
		return formatEditInput(tool)
	case "grep_search":
		return formatLabeledInput(in, tool.Name)
	case "todo_write":
		return formatTodos(in["todos"])
	case "mcp":
		return formatMCPInput(in)
	case "get_mcp_tools":
		return labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"server", "Server"}, {"toolName", "Tool"}})
	case "await":
		return labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"blockUntilMs", "Wait (ms)"}})
	case "generate_image":
		return labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"description", "Description"}, {"aspectRatio", "Aspect ratio"}, {"filePath", "File"}})
	case "write_canvas":
		var b strings.Builder
		if title := spi.StringValue(in, "title"); title != "" {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Title: %s\n\n", title)
		}
		if contents := spi.StringValue(in, "contents"); contents != "" {
			b.WriteString(spi.CodeFence("jsx", contents))
		}
		return b.String()
	case "read_canvas":
		return labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"canvasId", "Canvas"}})
	default:
		return spi.RenderGenericJSON(in)
	}
}

// formatLabeledInput covers the tools whose summary already names the key
// argument; only the secondary arguments are worth a line.
func formatLabeledInput(in map[string]any, name string) string {
	switch name {
	case "file_search":
		return labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"targetDirectory", "Directory"}})
	case "grep_search":
		var b strings.Builder
		b.WriteString(labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"path", "Path"}, {"glob", "Glob"}}))
		var flags []string
		if v, _ := in["caseInsensitive"].(bool); v {
			flags = append(flags, "case-insensitive")
		}
		if v, _ := in["multiline"].(bool); v {
			flags = append(flags, "multiline")
		}
		if len(flags) > 0 {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Options: %s\n", strings.Join(flags, ", "))
		}
		return b.String()
	default:
		// read_file, delete_file, web_fetch, web_search: the summary carries it.
		return ""
	}
}

// labeledLines renders the given keys, in order, as "Label: value" lines.
// Path-valued labels are shown relative to the VM workspace.
func labeledLines(in map[string]any, keys [][2]string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, kv := range keys {
		value := spi.StringValue(in, kv[0])
		if value == "" {
			continue
		}
		if kv[0] == "path" || kv[0] == "targetDirectory" || kv[0] == "filePath" {
			value = displayPath(value)
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s: %s\n", kv[1], spi.InlineCode(value))
	}
	return b.String()
}

// formatShellInput shows the description, the command, and the directory
// when it is not the workspace root every observed call uses.
func formatShellInput(in map[string]any) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	command := spi.StringValue(in, "command")
	if dir := spi.StringValue(in, "workingDirectory"); dir != "" && dir != vmWorkspaceRoot {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Directory: %s\n\n", spi.InlineCode(displayPath(dir)))
	}
	if command != "" {
		b.WriteString(spi.CodeFence("bash", command))
	}
	// Anything beyond the known arguments is shown so a new argument is not lost.
	extra := spi.RenderGenericJSON(in, append([]string{"command", "workingDirectory", "description"}, shellInputNoise...)...)
	if extra != "" {
		b.WriteString("\n\n")
		b.WriteString(extra)
	}
	return b.String()
}

// formatEditInput prefers the diff the harness computed; while a call is still
// streaming (no result yet) the new content is the only record of the edit.
func formatEditInput(tool *schema.ToolInfo) string {
	if success := resultBranch(tool.Output, "success"); success != nil {
		if diff := spi.StringValue(success, "diffString"); diff != "" {
			return spi.CodeFence("diff", spi.CapRunes(diff, maxResultRunes))
		}
	}
	content := spi.StringValue(tool.Input, "streamContent")
	if content == "" {
		return ""
	}
	return spi.CodeFence(spi.LanguageFromPath(spi.StringValue(tool.Input, "path")), content)
}

// formatMCPInput names the server and tool; any further arguments render as JSON.
func formatMCPInput(in map[string]any) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString(labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"serverIdentifier", "Server"}, {"toolName", "Tool"}}))
	if extra := spi.RenderGenericJSON(in, "name", "serverIdentifier", "providerIdentifier", "toolName"); extra != "" {
		b.WriteString("\n")
		b.WriteString(extra)
	}
	return b.String()
}

// todoStatus maps the TODO_STATUS_* enum recorded by todo_write onto the
// shared checkbox vocabulary.
func todoStatus(status string) string {
	return strings.ToLower(strings.TrimPrefix(status, "TODO_STATUS_"))
}

// formatTodos renders a todo list; a malformed item is skipped.
func formatTodos(raw any) string {
	items, ok := raw.([]any)
	if !ok || len(items) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("Todo List:\n")
	for _, item := range items {
		todo, ok := item.(map[string]any)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		content := strings.TrimSpace(spi.StringValue(todo, "content"))
		if content == "" {
			continue
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- [%s] %s\n", spi.TodoSymbol(todoStatus(spi.StringValue(todo, "status"))), content)
	}
	return b.String()
}

// formatToolResult renders the result. Errors take priority for every tool;
// a shell command that exited non-zero records a "failure" branch instead.
func formatToolResult(tool *schema.ToolInfo) string {
	if tool.Output == nil {
		return ""
	}
	if errText := toolErrorText(tool.Output); errText != "" {
		return resultBlock("Error", errText)
	}

	if tool.Name == "run_terminal_cmd" {
		return formatShellResult(tool.Output)
	}

	success := resultBranch(tool.Output, "success")
	if success == nil {
		return formatGenericResult(tool.Output)
	}
	switch tool.Name {
	case "read_file":
		return formatReadResult(tool.Input, success)
	case "edit_file", "todo_write":
		// The body already shows the diff or the list.
		return ""
	case "delete_file":
		prev := spi.StringValue(success, "prevContent")
		if prev == "" {
			return "Result: deleted"
		}
		return "Result: deleted\n\n" + spi.FormatDiffBlock(spi.CapRunes(prev, maxResultRunes), "")
	case "file_search":
		return formatFileSearchResult(success)
	case "grep_search":
		return formatGrepResult(success)
	case "web_search":
		return formatWebSearchResult(success)
	case "web_fetch":
		if md := spi.StringValue(success, "markdown"); md != "" {
			return "Result:\n" + spi.CodeFence("markdown", spi.CapRunes(md, maxResultRunes))
		}
		return ""
	case "mcp":
		return formatMCPResult(success)
	case "get_mcp_tools":
		return formatMCPToolsResult(success)
	case "await":
		if complete, ok := success["complete"].(map[string]any); ok {
			if ms := spi.StringValue(complete, "runtimeMs"); ms != "" {
				return fmt.Sprintf("Result: completed after %s ms", ms)
			}
		}
		return formatGenericResult(tool.Output)
	case "generate_image":
		if path := spi.StringValue(success, "filePath"); path != "" {
			return "Result: saved to " + spi.InlineCode(path)
		}
		return ""
	case "write_canvas", "read_canvas":
		return formatCanvasResult(success)
	default:
		return formatGenericResult(tool.Output)
	}
}

// toolErrorText extracts a failed call's message. Observed shapes:
// {"error":{"error":"..."}} (delete_file, grep_search, web_fetch) and
// {"error":{"errorMessage":"..."}} (read_file). An error object with neither
// key is shown as JSON rather than dropped.
func toolErrorText(output map[string]any) string {
	errObj, ok := output["error"]
	if !ok {
		return ""
	}
	m, ok := errObj.(map[string]any)
	if !ok {
		if s, isString := errObj.(string); isString {
			return s
		}
		return compactJSON(errObj)
	}
	if text := spi.StringValue(m, "error", "errorMessage", "message"); text != "" {
		return text
	}
	return compactJSON(m)
}

// formatShellResult renders command output. A non-zero exit is recorded as a
// "failure" branch with exitCode and stderr; success carries stdout. The
// interleaved stream is preferred because it keeps stdout and stderr in the
// order the terminal showed them.
func formatShellResult(output map[string]any) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	branch := resultBranch(output, "success")
	if failure := resultBranch(output, "failure"); failure != nil {
		branch = failure
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Exit code: %s\n\n", spi.StringValue(failure, "exitCode"))
	}
	if branch == nil {
		return formatGenericResult(output)
	}
	if background, _ := output["isBackground"].(bool); background {
		b.WriteString("Running in the background.\n\n")
	}
	text := spi.StringValue(branch, "interleavedOutput")
	if text == "" {
		text = spi.StringValue(branch, "stdout") + spi.StringValue(branch, "stderr")
	}
	text = strings.Trim(spi.SanitizeShellOutput(text), "\n")
	if text == "" {
		b.WriteString("Result: (no output)")
		return b.String()
	}
	b.WriteString("Result:\n")
	b.WriteString(spi.CodeFence("text", spi.CapRunes(text, maxResultRunes)))
	return b.String()
}

// formatReadResult fences the file content by the file's language and notes
// when only part of the file was read.
func formatReadResult(in, success map[string]any) string {
	content := spi.StringValue(success, "content")
	if content == "" {
		return "Result: (empty file)"
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	if rng, ok := success["readRange"].(map[string]any); ok {
		start, end := spi.StringValue(rng, "startLine"), spi.StringValue(rng, "endLine")
		total := spi.StringValue(success, "totalLines")
		if start != "" && end != "" && !(start == "1" && end == total) {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Lines %s–%s of %s\n\n", start, end, total)
		}
	}
	path := spi.StringValue(in, "path")
	b.WriteString(spi.CodeFence(spi.LanguageFromPath(path), spi.CapRunes(strings.TrimRight(content, "\n"), maxResultRunes)))
	return b.String()
}

// formatFileSearchResult lists matched files.
func formatFileSearchResult(success map[string]any) string {
	files, _ := success["files"].([]any)
	if len(files) == 0 {
		return "Result: no files found"
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Result: %d %s\n", len(files), plural(len(files), "file", "files"))
	for _, f := range files {
		if name, ok := f.(string); ok {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- %s\n", spi.InlineCode(name))
		}
	}
	return b.String()
}

// formatGrepResult flattens workspaceResults into file:line: text lines. The
// map is keyed by workspace root; roots are sorted so output is deterministic.
func formatGrepResult(success map[string]any) string {
	roots, _ := success["workspaceResults"].(map[string]any)
	var lines []string
	for _, root := range sortedKeys(roots) {
		rootResult, _ := roots[root].(map[string]any)
		content, _ := rootResult["content"].(map[string]any)
		files, _ := content["matches"].([]any)
		for _, f := range files {
			file, ok := f.(map[string]any)
			if !ok {
				continue
			}
			name := spi.StringValue(file, "file")
			matches, _ := file["matches"].([]any)
			for _, m := range matches {
				match, ok := m.(map[string]any)
				if !ok {
					continue
				}
				lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s: %s", name, spi.StringValue(match, "lineNumber"), spi.StringValue(match, "content")))
			}
		}
	}
	if len(lines) == 0 {
		if roots == nil {
			return formatGenericResult(map[string]any{"success": success})
		}
		return "Result: no matches"
	}
	return "Result:\n" + spi.CodeFence("text", spi.CapRunes(strings.Join(lines, "\n"), maxResultRunes))
}

// formatWebSearchResult renders each reference. The chunk is already a
// markdown link list followed by a synthesis paragraph, so it is shown as is.
func formatWebSearchResult(success map[string]any) string {
	refs, _ := success["references"].([]any)
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, r := range refs {
		ref, ok := r.(map[string]any)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		chunk := strings.TrimSpace(spi.StringValue(ref, "chunk"))
		if chunk == "" {
			continue
		}
		if b.Len() > 0 {
			b.WriteString("\n\n")
		}
		b.WriteString(spi.CapRunes(chunk, maxResultRunes))
	}
	if b.Len() == 0 {
		return formatGenericResult(map[string]any{"success": success})
	}
	return "Result:\n\n" + b.String()
}

// formatMCPResult shows the text content parts. structuredContent repeats the
// text in every observed result, so it is shown only when there is no text.
func formatMCPResult(success map[string]any) string {
	parts, _ := success["content"].([]any)
	var texts []string
	for _, p := range parts {
		part, ok := p.(map[string]any)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		if textObj, ok := part["text"].(map[string]any); ok {
			if text := spi.StringValue(textObj, "text"); text != "" {
				texts = append(texts, text)
			}
		}
	}
	if len(texts) == 0 {
		return formatGenericResult(map[string]any{"success": success})
	}
	return "Result:\n" + spi.CodeFence("text", spi.CapRunes(strings.Join(texts, "\n\n"), maxResultRunes))
}

// formatMCPToolsResult shows a tool schema lookup. The content is a JSON
// string (a schema, or a note that output went to a file).
func formatMCPToolsResult(success map[string]any) string {
	content := spi.StringValue(success, "content")
	var b strings.Builder
	if path := spi.StringValue(success, "outputFilePath"); path != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Output file: %s\n\n", spi.InlineCode(path))
	}
	if content != "" {
		lang := "text"
		if json.Valid([]byte(content)) {
			lang = "json"
		}
		b.WriteString("Result:\n")
		b.WriteString(spi.CodeFence(lang, spi.CapRunes(content, maxResultRunes)))
	}
	return b.String()
}

// formatCanvasResult links the canvas and shows its source when returned.
func formatCanvasResult(success map[string]any) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	title := spi.StringValue(success, "title")
	if url := spi.StringValue(success, "url"); url != "" {
		if title == "" {
			title = url
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Result: [%s](%s)\n", markdownLinkTextEscaper.Replace(title), url)
	}
	if source := spi.StringValue(success, "source"); source != "" {
		b.WriteString("\n")
		b.WriteString(spi.CodeFence("jsx", spi.CapRunes(source, maxResultRunes)))
	}
	return b.String()
}

// formatGenericResult is the fallback for an unfamiliar result shape.
func formatGenericResult(output map[string]any) string {
	rendered := spi.RenderGenericJSON(output)
	if rendered == "" {
		return ""
	}
	return "Result:\n" + rendered
}

// resultBlock renders a labeled one-line or fenced multi-line result.
func resultBlock(label, text string) string {
	text = strings.TrimSpace(text)
	if strings.Contains(text, "\n") {
		return label + ":\n" + spi.CodeFence("text", spi.CapRunes(text, maxResultRunes))
	}
	return label + ": " + text
}

// resultBranch returns output[key] as an object, or nil.
func resultBranch(output map[string]any, key string) map[string]any {
	branch, _ := output[key].(map[string]any)
	return branch
}

// markdownLinkTextEscaper neutralizes the characters that would end a link's
// text early.
var markdownLinkTextEscaper = strings.NewReplacer("[", `\[`, "]", `\]`)

func compactJSON(v any) string {
	data, err := json.Marshal(v)
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	return string(data)
}

func sortedKeys(m map[string]any) []string {
	keys := make([]string, 0, len(m))
	for k := range m {
		keys = append(keys, k)
	}
	sort.Strings(keys)
	return keys
}

func plural(n int, one, many string) string {
	if n == 1 {
		return one
	}
	return many
}
```

```text
== pkg/providers/cursorcloud/agent_session.go
package cursorcloud

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
)

// ProviderID is the registry id, also used as ProviderInfo.ID.
const ProviderID = "cursorcloud"

// providerName is the product's own name.
const providerName = "Cursor Cloud Agent"

// vmWorkspaceRoot is where the cloud VM checks out the repository; every
// observed tool path and workingDirectory is under it.
const vmWorkspaceRoot = "/workspace"

// segmentKind orders what an agent produced within one run.
type segmentKind int

const (
	segmentThinking segmentKind = iota
	segmentText
	segmentTool
)

// segment is one contiguous piece of agent output: a run of thinking deltas,
// a run of assistant deltas, or one tool call.
type segment struct {
	kind segmentKind
	text strings.Builder
	time string
	call *toolCall
}

// toolCall is the merged state of every tool_call event sharing a callId.
type toolCall struct {
	callID string
	name   string
	status string
	args   map[string]any
	result map[string]any
	time   string
}

// runTranscript is one run's stream reduced to what renders.
type runTranscript struct {
	userText   string
	userTime   string
	segments   []*segment
	startTime  string
	resultTime string
}

// interactionTypesWithoutContent are interaction_update types observed in
// every capture that carry nothing to render: the *-delta types duplicate the
// thinking and assistant events, the rest are step and tool lifecycle markers.
var interactionTypesWithoutContent = []string{
	"token-delta", "text-delta", "thinking-delta", "thinking-completed",
	"step-started", "step-completed", "tool-call-started", "tool-call-completed",
	"tool-requests-listed", "partial-tool-call", "turn-ended",
}

// parseRunEvents folds a run's events, in stream order, into a transcript.
func parseRunEvents(events []sseEvent, source string) runTranscript {
	var t runTranscript
	calls := map[string]*toolCall{}

	for i, ev := range events {
		ts := eventTime(ev.ID)
		if t.startTime == "" && ts != "" {
			t.startTime = ts
		}
		switch ev.Event {
		case "status", "heartbeat", "done":
			// status opens and closes a run (the run object carries it), heartbeat
			// keeps a quiet live stream open, done marks the end of the stream.
		case "interaction_update":
			var update struct {
				Type        string `json:"type"`
				UserMessage struct {
					Text string `json:"text"`
				} `json:"userMessage"`
			}
			if err := json.Unmarshal(ev.Data, &update); err != nil {
				slog.Warn("Skipping undecodable stream event", "source", source, "index", i, "event", ev.Event, "error", err)
				continue
			}
			switch {
			case update.Type == "user-message-appended":
				// The run's prompt; the only place the stream records it.
				t.userText = update.UserMessage.Text
				t.userTime = ts
			case slices.Contains(interactionTypesWithoutContent, update.Type):
			default:
				slog.Debug("Unknown interaction_update type", "source", source, "type", update.Type)
			}
		case "thinking", "assistant":
			var delta struct {
				Text string `json:"text"`
			}
			if err := json.Unmarshal(ev.Data, &delta); err != nil {
				slog.Warn("Skipping undecodable stream event", "source", source, "index", i, "event", ev.Event, "error", err)
				continue
			}
			kind := segmentText
			if ev.Event == "thinking" {
				kind = segmentThinking
			}
			t.appendDelta(kind, delta.Text, ts)
		case "tool_call":
			t.mergeToolCall(calls, ev, ts, source, i)
		case "result":
			// The result text repeats the last assistant text, so only its time is used.
			t.resultTime = ts
		default:
			slog.Debug("Unknown stream event", "source", source, "event", ev.Event)
		}
	}
	return t
}

// appendDelta extends the current segment when it is of the same kind, so
// consecutive deltas become one part, and opens a new segment otherwise.
func (t *runTranscript) appendDelta(kind segmentKind, text, ts string) {
	if n := len(t.segments); n > 0 && t.segments[n-1].kind == kind {
		t.segments[n-1].text.WriteString(text)
		return
	}
	seg := &segment{kind: kind, time: ts}
	seg.text.WriteString(text)
	t.segments = append(t.segments, seg)
}

// mergeToolCall applies one tool_call event. A call is placed where its first
// event appears; later events update it field by field, so the last event
// wins. A result on a "running" event is provisional: the stream attaches a
// placeholder error ("Invalid arguments") while arguments are still streaming
// and replaces it when the call completes, so only results from other
// statuses are kept.
func (t *runTranscript) mergeToolCall(calls map[string]*toolCall, ev sseEvent, ts, source string, index int) {
	var payload struct {
		CallID string          `json:"callId"`
		Name   string          `json:"name"`
		Status string          `json:"status"`
		Args   json.RawMessage `json:"args"`
		Result json.RawMessage `json:"result"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(ev.Data, &payload); err != nil || payload.CallID == "" {
		slog.Warn("Skipping undecodable tool_call event", "source", source, "index", index, "error", err)
		return
	}
	call, seen := calls[payload.CallID]
	if !seen {
		call = &toolCall{callID: payload.CallID, time: ts}
		calls[payload.CallID] = call
		t.segments = append(t.segments, &segment{kind: segmentTool, time: ts, call: call})
	}
	if payload.Name != "" {
		call.name = payload.Name
	}
	if payload.Status != "" {
		call.status = payload.Status
	}
	if len(payload.Args) > 0 {
		var args map[string]any
		if err := json.Unmarshal(payload.Args, &args); err == nil {
			call.args = args
		}
	}
	if len(payload.Result) > 0 && payload.Status != "running" {
		var result map[string]any
		if err := json.Unmarshal(payload.Result, &result); err == nil {
			call.result = result
		}
	}
}

// buildSessionData converts a mirrored agent into SessionData. It returns nil
// when no run yields a user prompt, which means there is nothing to save yet.
func buildSessionData(snap *agentSnapshot, workspaceRoot string) (*schema.SessionData, string) {
	agent := snap.agent
	data := &schema.SessionData{
		SchemaVersion: schema.CurrentSchemaVersion,
		// The API exposes no agent version, so the honest value is "unknown".
		Provider:      schema.ProviderInfo{ID: ProviderID, Name: providerName, Version: "unknown"},
		SessionID:     agent.ID,
		CreatedAt:     agent.CreatedAt,
		UpdatedAt:     agent.UpdatedAt,
		WorkspaceRoot: workspaceRoot,
		Exchanges:     []schema.Exchange{},
	}

	firstPrompt := ""
	for i, run := range snap.runs {
		exchange := buildExchange(snap, i, run, workspaceRoot)
		if exchange == nil {
			continue
		}
		if firstPrompt == "" {
			firstPrompt = firstUserText(exchange)
		}
		data.Exchanges = append(data.Exchanges, *exchange)
	}
	if firstPrompt == "" {
		return nil, ""
	}
	data.Slug = spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(firstPrompt)
	return data, firstPrompt
}

// buildExchange builds one run's exchange. The stream is the full-fidelity
// source; the v0 conversation (text only) fills in when the stream is missing,
// or when a finished run's capture is partial and the stream has since expired.
func buildExchange(snap *agentSnapshot, index int, run runSnapshot, workspaceRoot string) *schema.Exchange {
	source := snap.dir + "/runs/" + run.run.ID
	useStream := len(run.events) > 0
	if useStream && run.run.isTerminal() && !eventsAreWhole(run.events) && len(v0TurnMessages(snap.conversation, index)) > 0 {
		useStream = false
	}

	var exchange *schema.Exchange
	if useStream {
		exchange = exchangeFromStream(parseRunEvents(run.events, source), run, workspaceRoot)
	}
	if exchange == nil {
		exchange = exchangeFromConversation(snap.conversation, index, run)
	}
	if exchange == nil {
		slog.Debug("Run has no recorded content yet", "agentId", snap.agent.ID, "runId", run.run.ID)
		return nil
	}
	exchange.Metadata = exchangeMetadata(snap.agent, run.run, exchange.Metadata)
	return exchange
}

// exchangeFromStream turns a transcript into messages: the prompt, then agent
// messages in stream order. Thinking and text share one agent message until a
// tool call interrupts; each tool call is its own message.
func exchangeFromStream(t runTranscript, run runSnapshot, workspaceRoot string) *schema.Exchange {
	if t.userText == "" && len(t.segments) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	runID := run.run.ID
	exchange := &schema.Exchange{ExchangeID: runID, StartTime: t.startTime, EndTime: t.resultTime}

	if t.userText != "" {
		userTime := t.userTime
		if userTime == "" {
			userTime = run.run.CreatedAt
		}
		exchange.Messages = append(exchange.Messages, schema.Message{
			ID:        runID + ":user",
			Timestamp: userTime,
			Role:      schema.RoleUser,
			Content:   []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: t.userText}},
		})
	}

	var current *schema.Message
	flush := func() {
		if current != nil && len(current.Content) > 0 {
			exchange.Messages = append(exchange.Messages, *current)
		}
		current = nil
	}
	for _, seg := range t.segments {
		switch seg.kind {
		case segmentThinking, segmentText:
			text := seg.text.String()
			if strings.TrimSpace(text) == "" {
				continue
			}
			if current == nil {
				current = &schema.Message{
					ID:        runID + ":" + strconv.Itoa(len(exchange.Messages)),
					Timestamp: seg.time,
					Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
				}
			}
			partType := schema.ContentTypeText
			if seg.kind == segmentThinking {
				partType = schema.ContentTypeThinking
			}
			current.Content = append(current.Content, schema.ContentPart{Type: partType, Text: text})
		case segmentTool:
			flush()
			exchange.Messages = append(exchange.Messages, toolMessage(seg.call, workspaceRoot))
		}
	}
	flush()
	return exchange
}

// toolMessage converts one merged tool call.
func toolMessage(call *toolCall, workspaceRoot string) schema.Message {
	tool := &schema.ToolInfo{
		Name:   call.name,
		Type:   toolType(call.name),
		UseID:  call.callID,
		Input:  cleanToolInput(call.args),
		Output: call.result,
	}
	if markdown := formatTool(tool); markdown != "" {
		tool.FormattedMarkdown = &markdown
	}
	msg := schema.Message{
		ID:        call.callID,
		Timestamp: call.time,
		Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
		Tool:      tool,
		PathHints: pathHints(call.name, tool.Input, workspaceRoot),
	}
	if call.status != "" {
		msg.Metadata = map[string]any{"status": call.status}
	}
	return msg
}

// pathHints lists the files a call wrote. Paths are recorded under the VM's
// /workspace; rewriting that prefix onto the local project lets the shared
// normalizer make them project-relative like every other provider's hints.
func pathHints(name string, input map[string]any, workspaceRoot string) []string {
	var hints []string
	switch toolType(name) {
	case schema.ToolTypeWrite:
		if path := spi.StringValue(input, "path"); path != "" {
			hints = append(hints, spi.NormalizePath(localPath(path, workspaceRoot), workspaceRoot))
		}
	case schema.ToolTypeShell:
		command := spi.StringValue(input, "command")
		cwd := localPath(spi.StringValue(input, "workingDirectory"), workspaceRoot)
		if cwd == "" {
			cwd = workspaceRoot
		}
		for _, hint := range spi.ExtractShellPathHints(command, cwd, workspaceRoot) {
			if !slices.Contains(hints, hint) {
				hints = append(hints, hint)
			}
		}
	}
	return hints
}

// localPath maps a VM path onto the local project root. The root is joined by
// shape with "/" because recorded paths are POSIX; NormalizePath accepts
// either separator.
func localPath(path, workspaceRoot string) string {
	if workspaceRoot == "" {
		return path
	}
	root := strings.TrimRight(workspaceRoot, `/\`)
	if path == vmWorkspaceRoot {
		return root
	}
	if rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(path, vmWorkspaceRoot+"/"); ok {
		return root + "/" + rest
	}
	return path
}

// displayPath shows a VM path relative to the repository.
func displayPath(path string) string {
	if path == vmWorkspaceRoot {
		return "."
	}
	if rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(path, vmWorkspaceRoot+"/"); ok {
		return rest
	}
	return path
}

// v0TurnMessages returns the v0 messages belonging to run index turn. Ids are
// "turn-N:user" and "turn-N:step:M:assistant"; the agent's very first user
// message has a bare UUID id and belongs to turn 0.
func v0TurnMessages(conv *v0Conversation, turn int) []v0Message {
	if conv == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var out []v0Message
	for _, msg := range conv.Messages {
		if v0MessageTurn(msg.ID) == turn {
			out = append(out, msg)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// v0MessageTurn parses the turn index from a v0 message id.
func v0MessageTurn(id string) int {
	rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(id, "turn-")
	if !ok {
		return 0
	}
	digits, _, _ := strings.Cut(rest, ":")
	n, err := strconv.Atoi(digits)
	if err != nil {
		return -1
	}
	return n
}

// exchangeFromConversation builds a text-only exchange from the v0
// conversation. v0 records no times, so the run's own times stand in.
func exchangeFromConversation(conv *v0Conversation, index int, run runSnapshot) *schema.Exchange {
	messages := v0TurnMessages(conv, index)
	if len(messages) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	exchange := &schema.Exchange{
		ExchangeID: run.run.ID,
		StartTime:  run.run.CreatedAt,
		EndTime:    run.run.UpdatedAt,
		Metadata:   map[string]any{"source": "v0-conversation"},
	}
	for _, msg := range messages {
		if strings.TrimSpace(msg.Text) == "" {
			continue
		}
		role := schema.RoleAgent
		timestamp := ""
		switch msg.Type {
		case "user_message":
			role = schema.RoleUser
			timestamp = run.run.CreatedAt
		case "assistant_message":
		default:
			slog.Debug("Unknown v0 message type", "type", msg.Type, "id", msg.ID)
		}
		exchange.Messages = append(exchange.Messages, schema.Message{
			ID:        msg.ID,
			Timestamp: timestamp,
			Role:      role,
			Content:   []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: msg.Text}},
		})
	}
	if len(exchange.Messages) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return exchange
}

// exchangeMetadata records what a reader wants to click: the agent page, the
// branch and pull request, and how the run ended. Token usage lives in the
// usage endpoint per run, not per message, so it stays in RawData rather than
// being forced into the per-message Usage field.
func exchangeMetadata(agent apiAgent, run apiRun, existing map[string]any) map[string]any {
	meta := existing
	if meta == nil {
		meta = map[string]any{}
	}
	meta["runId"] = run.ID
	if run.Status != "" {
		meta["status"] = run.Status
	}
	if run.DurationMs > 0 {
		meta["durationMs"] = run.DurationMs
	}
	if len(run.Git.Branches) > 0 {
		branch := run.Git.Branches[0]
		if branch.Branch != "" {
			meta["branch"] = branch.Branch
		}
		if branch.PrURL != "" {
			meta["prUrl"] = branch.PrURL
		}
	}
	if agent.URL != "" {
		meta["agentUrl"] = agent.URL
	}
	return meta
}

// firstUserText returns the text of an exchange's first user message.
func firstUserText(exchange *schema.Exchange) string {
	for _, msg := range exchange.Messages {
		if msg.Role != schema.RoleUser {
			continue
		}
		for _, part := range msg.Content {
			if part.Type == schema.ContentTypeText && strings.TrimSpace(part.Text) != "" {
				return part.Text
			}
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// sessionName prefers the agent's own name (Cursor sets one, derived from the
// prompt when the launcher gave none) over the shared generator.
func sessionName(agent apiAgent, firstPrompt string) string {
	if name := strings.TrimSpace(agent.Name); name != "" {
		return name
	}
	return spi.GenerateReadableName(firstPrompt)
}

// rawSession is the RawData envelope: the native objects of one mirror read.
type rawSession struct {
	Agent        json.RawMessage `json:"agent"`
	Runs         []rawRun        `json:"runs"`
	Conversation json.RawMessage `json:"conversation,omitempty"`
	Usage        json.RawMessage `json:"usage,omitempty"`
}

type rawRun struct {
	Run    json.RawMessage `json:"run"`
	Events []sseEvent      `json:"events"`
}

// buildRawData serializes the snapshot the session was built from, so RawData
// never describes more than the converted session saw.
func buildRawData(snap *agentSnapshot) (string, error) {
	raw := rawSession{Agent: snap.agentRaw, Conversation: snap.conversationRaw, Usage: snap.usageRaw, Runs: []rawRun{}}
	for _, run := range snap.runs {
		events := run.events
		if events == nil {
			events = []sseEvent{}
		}
		raw.Runs = append(raw.Runs, rawRun{Run: run.runRaw, Events: events})
	}
	data, err := json.Marshal(raw)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("marshal raw data: %w", err)
	}
	return string(data), nil
}
```

```text
package cursorcloud

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
)

// streamRetention is how long the API replays a finished run's stream, as
// advertised by x-cursor-stream-retention-seconds: 86400 on every capture.
const streamRetention = 24 * time.Hour

// mirrorGitignore keeps the project-local mirror out of version control. The
// mirror holds raw API transcripts, which are never redacted (redaction
// applies to markdown and cloud sync), and .specstory/ is usually committed.
const mirrorGitignore = "# Raw Cursor Cloud Agent transcripts mirrored by SpecStory; unredacted, so never committed.\n*\n"

// mirror is the local copy of the API that every read path uses as the
// provider's native store.
type mirror struct {
	root string
}

func (m mirror) agentDir(agentID string) string { return filepath.Join(m.root, "agents", agentID) }

func (m mirror) agentFile(agentID string) string {
	return filepath.Join(m.agentDir(agentID), "agent.json")
}

func (m mirror) runsDir(agentID string) string { return filepath.Join(m.agentDir(agentID), "runs") }

func (m mirror) runFile(agentID, runID string) string {
	return filepath.Join(m.runsDir(agentID), runID+".json")
}

func (m mirror) eventsFile(agentID, runID string) string {
	return filepath.Join(m.runsDir(agentID), runID+".events.jsonl")
}

// agentSnapshot is one consistent read of an agent's mirror directory: every
// conversion, RawData and debug export of a session comes from one snapshot.
type agentSnapshot struct {
	dir             string
	agentRaw        json.RawMessage
	agent           apiAgent
	conversationRaw json.RawMessage
	conversation    *v0Conversation
	usageRaw        json.RawMessage
	runs            []runSnapshot
}

type runSnapshot struct {
	runRaw json.RawMessage
	run    apiRun
	events []sseEvent
}

// loadAgentSnapshot reads an agent directory. A directory without agent.json
// is not an agent yet (a refresh writes agent.json last) and yields nil.
func loadAgentSnapshot(dir string) (*agentSnapshot, error) {
	agentRaw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "agent.json"))
	if err != nil {
		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return nil, nil
		}
		return nil, err
	}
	record, err := decodeAgent(agentRaw)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", filepath.Join(dir, "agent.json"), err)
	}
	snap := &agentSnapshot{dir: dir, agentRaw: record.raw, agent: record.agent}

	if raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "conversation.json")); err == nil {
		var conv v0Conversation
		if jsonErr := json.Unmarshal(raw, &conv); jsonErr != nil {
			slog.Warn("Ignoring undecodable conversation", "path", filepath.Join(dir, "conversation.json"), "error", jsonErr)
		} else {
			snap.conversationRaw = raw
			snap.conversation = &conv
		}
	}
	if raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "usage.json")); err == nil && json.Valid(raw) {
		snap.usageRaw = raw
	}

	runsDir := filepath.Join(dir, "runs")
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(runsDir)
	if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
		return nil, err
	}
	for _, entry := range entries {
		name := entry.Name()
		if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".json") {
			continue
		}
		raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(runsDir, name))
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		record, err := decodeRun(raw)
		if err != nil {
			slog.Warn("Skipping undecodable run", "path", filepath.Join(runsDir, name), "error", err)
			continue
		}
		events, err := readEventsFile(filepath.Join(runsDir, record.run.ID+".events.jsonl"))
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		snap.runs = append(snap.runs, runSnapshot{runRaw: record.raw, run: record.run, events: events})
	}
	// One run is one exchange in creation order. The API lists runs newest
	// first; the id breaks ties so the order never depends on directory order.
	sort.SliceStable(snap.runs, func(i, j int) bool {
		a, b := snap.runs[i].run, snap.runs[j].run
		if a.CreatedAt != b.CreatedAt {
			return a.CreatedAt < b.CreatedAt
		}
		return a.ID < b.ID
	})
	return snap, nil
}

// agentDirs lists the agent directories in the mirror, sorted by id.
func (m mirror) agentDirs() ([]string, error) {
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(filepath.Join(m.root, "agents"))
	if err != nil {
		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return nil, nil
		}
		return nil, err
	}
	var dirs []string
	for _, entry := range entries {
		if entry.IsDir() && validAgentID(entry.Name()) {
			dirs = append(dirs, filepath.Join(m.root, "agents", entry.Name()))
		}
	}
	return dirs, nil
}

// readStoredAgent returns the mirrored agent object, or nil when absent.
func (m mirror) readStoredAgent(agentID string) *apiAgent {
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(m.agentFile(agentID))
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	record, err := decodeAgent(raw)
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	return &record.agent
}

// ensureRoot creates the mirror root and, for a mirror inside the project,
// the .gitignore that keeps raw transcripts out of commits.
func (m mirror) ensureRoot(projectLocal bool) error {
	if err := os.MkdirAll(m.root, 0o755); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if !projectLocal {
		return nil
	}
	path := filepath.Join(m.root, ".gitignore")
	if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return writeFileAtomic(path, []byte(mirrorGitignore))
}

// writeFileAtomic replaces path with data via a temporary file and a rename, so
// a concurrent reader sees the old file or the new one, never a torn write.
// An unchanged file is left alone, which keeps the directory fingerprint (and
// so reindex) stable across syncs that bring nothing new.
func writeFileAtomic(path string, data []byte) error {
	if existing, err := os.ReadFile(path); err == nil && bytes.Equal(existing, data) {
		return nil
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(path), "."+filepath.Base(path)+".tmp-*")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	tmpName := tmp.Name()
	if _, err := tmp.Write(data); err != nil {
		_ = tmp.Close()
		_ = os.Remove(tmpName)
		return err
	}
	if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
		_ = os.Remove(tmpName)
		return err
	}
	if err := os.Rename(tmpName, path); err != nil {
		_ = os.Remove(tmpName)
		return err
	}
	return nil
}

// writeEvents stores a run's events atomically.
func (m mirror) writeEvents(agentID, runID string, events []sseEvent) error {
	data, err := encodeEvents(events)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return writeFileAtomic(m.eventsFile(agentID, runID), data)
}

// refreshOptions tunes a refresh for its caller.
type refreshOptions struct {
	// skipStreams names runs whose events another goroutine is writing (a live
	// attach); the refresh must not replace their files underneath it.
	skipStreams map[string]bool
	now         time.Time
}

// refreshAgent brings one agent's mirror up to date. Runs, conversation and
// usage are re-fetched only when agent.updatedAt differs from what the mirror
// holds. Streams are fetched for finished runs whose capture is missing or
// partial while the API still retains them; a whole capture is never
// re-fetched. Unfinished runs are not streamed here, because reading a live
// stream blocks until the run ends; the watcher attaches to those instead.
// agent.json is written last so an interrupted refresh is retried next time.
func (m mirror) refreshAgent(ctx context.Context, c *apiClient, record agentRecord, opts refreshOptions) error {
	agentID := record.agent.ID
	stored := m.readStoredAgent(agentID)
	changed := stored == nil || stored.UpdatedAt != record.agent.UpdatedAt

	if changed {
		runs, err := c.listRuns(ctx, agentID)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("list runs: %w", err)
		}
		for _, run := range runs {
			if err := writeFileAtomic(m.runFile(agentID, run.run.ID), run.raw); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
		if conv, err := c.conversation(ctx, agentID); err != nil {
			slog.Warn("Failed to fetch conversation", "agentId", agentID, "error", err)
		} else if err := writeFileAtomic(filepath.Join(m.agentDir(agentID), "conversation.json"), conv); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if usage, err := c.usage(ctx, agentID); err != nil {
			slog.Warn("Failed to fetch usage", "agentId", agentID, "error", err)
		} else if err := writeFileAtomic(filepath.Join(m.agentDir(agentID), "usage.json"), usage); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}

	if err := m.fetchMissingStreams(ctx, c, agentID, opts); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if changed {
		return writeFileAtomic(m.agentFile(agentID), record.raw)
	}
	return nil
}

// fetchMissingStreams replays the stream of every finished run whose mirrored
// capture is not whole, while the API still retains it.
func (m mirror) fetchMissingStreams(ctx context.Context, c *apiClient, agentID string, opts refreshOptions) error {
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(m.runsDir(agentID))
	if err != nil {
		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return nil
		}
		return err
	}
	for _, entry := range entries {
		name := entry.Name()
		if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".json") {
			continue
		}
		raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(m.runsDir(agentID), name))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		record, err := decodeRun(raw)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		run := record.run
		if !run.isTerminal() || opts.skipStreams[run.ID] || !withinRetention(run, opts.now) {
			continue
		}
		events, err := readEventsFile(m.eventsFile(agentID, run.ID))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if eventsAreWhole(events) {
			continue
		}
		replayed, err := replayStream(ctx, c, agentID, run.ID)
		if errors.Is(err, errStreamExpired) {
			// Expired after all (clock skew or an early purge): the partial
			// capture stays and the v0 conversation fills the exchange.
			slog.Debug("Run stream expired; keeping partial capture", "agentId", agentID, "runId", run.ID)
			continue
		}
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("replay stream %s: %w", run.ID, err)
		}
		if err := m.writeEvents(agentID, run.ID, replayed); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// withinRetention reports whether a finished run's stream should still be
// replayable. now is wall-clock time; this decides whether to make a network
// call and never reaches rendered output.
func withinRetention(run apiRun, now time.Time) bool {
	ended, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, run.UpdatedAt)
	if err != nil {
		// Without a parseable end time, trying is cheaper than losing the transcript.
		return true
	}
	return now.Sub(ended) < streamRetention
}

// replayStream reads a finished run's stream from the start to its done event.
func replayStream(ctx context.Context, c *apiClient, agentID, runID string) ([]sseEvent, error) {
	body, err := c.openStream(ctx, agentID, runID, "")
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer func() { _ = body.Close() }()
	var events []sseEvent
	err = readSSE(body, agentID+"/"+runID, func(ev sseEvent) bool {
		events = append(events, ev)
		return ev.Event != "done"
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return events, nil
}

// agentDirFingerprint sums sizes and takes the newest mtime across an agent
// directory: one file (agent.json) does not change when a run's events land.
func agentDirFingerprint(dir string) *spi.SessionFingerprint {
	fp := &spi.SessionFingerprint{}
	_ = filepath.WalkDir(dir, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
			return nil
		}
		info, err := d.Info()
		if err != nil {
			return nil
		}
		fp.Size += info.Size()
		if mt := info.ModTime().UnixNano(); mt > fp.Mtime {
			fp.Mtime = mt
		}
		return nil
	})
	return fp
}
```

```text
package cursorcloud

import (
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
)

// apiKeyEnvVar is the environment variable Cursor's own tooling reads the API
// key from; it overrides the config file so a one-off key needs no edit.
const apiKeyEnvVar = "CURSOR_API_KEY"

// Settings handed in by the CLI at startup. Each is set once before any
// provider method runs, so no locking is needed.
var (
	configAPIKey        string
	configMirrorDir     string
	userDataDirOverride string
)

// SetAPIKey sets the key from `cursor_api_key` in specstory.toml. The
// CURSOR_API_KEY environment variable still wins when set.
func SetAPIKey(key string) {
	configAPIKey = strings.TrimSpace(key)
}

// SetMirrorDir sets the mirror location from `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` in
// specstory.toml (tilde-expanded). Empty keeps the project-local default.
func SetMirrorDir(dir string) {
	configMirrorDir = expandHome(strings.TrimSpace(dir))
}

// SetUserDataDirOverride sets the mirror location from
// `--user-data-dir cursorcloud:<path>`, which wins over the config file.
func SetUserDataDirOverride(dir string) {
	userDataDirOverride = expandHome(strings.TrimSpace(dir))
}

// resolveAPIKey returns the key and where it came from ("" when none).
func resolveAPIKey() (key, source string) {
	if env := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(apiKeyEnvVar)); env != "" {
		return env, apiKeyEnvVar
	}
	if configAPIKey != "" {
		return configAPIKey, "cursor_api_key"
	}
	return "", ""
}

// mirrorFor returns the mirror for a project and whether it lives inside the
// project. The override and config locations are shared by every project; the
// default keeps each project's mirror next to its history.
func mirrorFor(projectPath string) (mirror, bool) {
	if userDataDirOverride != "" {
		return mirror{root: userDataDirOverride}, false
	}
	if configMirrorDir != "" {
		return mirror{root: configMirrorDir}, false
	}
	return mirror{root: filepath.Join(projectPath, ".specstory", "cursorcloud")}, true
}

// globalMirror is the mirror enumerated by reindex, which has no project: the
// shared location when one is configured, else the current project's mirror.
func globalMirror() mirror {
	if userDataDirOverride != "" || configMirrorDir != "" {
		m, _ := mirrorFor("")
		return m
	}
	cwd, err := os.Getwd()
	if err != nil {
		slog.Warn("ListAllAgentChatSessions: cannot resolve working directory", "error", err)
		return mirror{}
	}
	m, _ := mirrorFor(spi.CanonicalizePathOrClean(cwd))
	return m
}

// projectOrigin returns the normalized origin URL of the project's repository,
// or "" when the project has none. Agents are matched to projects by
// repository, because the API records a repository and never a directory.
func projectOrigin(projectPath string) string {
	origin := spi.GitOriginURL(projectPath)
	if origin == "" {
		return ""
	}
	return spi.NormalizeGitRemoteURL(origin)
}

// agentMatchesOrigin reports whether any of the agent's repositories is the
// project's origin.
func agentMatchesOrigin(agent apiAgent, origin string) bool {
	if origin == "" {
		return false
	}
	for _, repo := range agent.Repos {
		if spi.NormalizeGitRemoteURL(repo.URL) == origin {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// workspaceRootFor is the SessionData workspace root: the caller's project,
// else the process working directory as the documented last resort.
func workspaceRootFor(projectPath string) string {
	if projectPath != "" {
		return projectPath
	}
	if cwd, err := os.Getwd(); err == nil {
		return cwd
	}
	return "."
}

// expandHome expands a leading ~ so config and flag values can use it.
func expandHome(path string) string {
	if path != "~" && !strings.HasPrefix(path, "~/") && !strings.HasPrefix(path, `~\`) {
		return path
	}
	home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
	if err != nil {
		return path
	}
	return filepath.Join(home, strings.TrimLeft(path[1:], `/\`))
}
```
