== pkg/providers/cursorcloud/provider.go
package cursorcloud

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/analytics"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/log"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
)

// Compile-time assertions that Provider satisfies the full spi.Provider
// contract plus the optional by-path reader used by reindex.
var (
	_ spi.Provider          = (*Provider)(nil)
	_ spi.PathSessionReader = (*Provider)(nil)
)

// checkProbe names the endpoint Check calls, reported in analytics where a
// binary provider reports its version flag.
const checkProbe = "GET /v1/me"

// apiKeyPage is where a user creates a key.
const apiKeyPage = "https://cursor.com/dashboard/api"

// Provider implements spi.Provider for Cursor Cloud Agents, whose
// conversations exist only in Cursor's backend. The Cloud Agents API is the
// native store; a local mirror of it is what every read path parses.
type Provider struct{}

// NewProvider creates a Cursor Cloud Agent provider.
func NewProvider() *Provider {
	return &Provider{}
}

// Name returns the product's name.
func (p *Provider) Name() string {
	return providerName
}

// Check verifies a key is configured and accepted by probing GET /v1/me.
// There is no binary; customCommand is the dashboard opener used by run, so a
// custom one is checked for existence.
func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
	attempt := analytics.CheckAttempt{
		Provider:      ProviderID,
		CustomCommand: customCommand != "",
		CommandPath:   customCommand,
		VersionFlag:   checkProbe,
	}
	slog.Info("Check: verifying Cursor Cloud Agent access", "customCommand", customCommand != "")

	fail := func(errorType, detail, message string) spi.CheckResult {
		slog.Info("Check: failed", "errorType", errorType, "error", detail)
		analytics.TrackCheckFailure(attempt, errorType, detail, "")
		return spi.CheckResult{Success: false, ErrorType: errorType, ErrorMessage: message}
	}

	if customCommand != "" {
		opener := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
		if len(opener) == 0 {
			return fail(spi.CheckErrorNotFound, "empty command", "The custom command is empty.\n")
		}
		resolved, err := spi.LookPathForCheck(opener[0])
		if err != nil {
			errorType := spi.ClassifyCheckError(err)
			return fail(errorType, err.Error(), fmt.Sprintf(
				"Could not find the dashboard opener: %s\n\n"+
					"• cursorcloud_cmd (or -c) is the command run cursorcloud uses to open https://cursor.com/agents.\n"+
					"• Check the path, or remove the setting to use the system URL opener.\n", opener[0]))
		}
		attempt.ResolvedPath = resolved
	}

	key, source := resolveAPIKey()
	if key == "" {
		return fail(spi.CheckErrorNotFound, "no API key configured", missingKeyMessage())
	}

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), jsonTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	me, err := newAPIClient(key).me(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		var ae *apiError
		if errors.As(err, &ae) && (ae.Status == http.StatusUnauthorized || ae.Status == http.StatusForbidden) {
			return fail(spi.CheckErrorPermissionDenied, err.Error(), fmt.Sprintf(
				"Cursor rejected the API key from %s (HTTP %d).\n\n"+
					"• Create a new key at %s and set %s or cursor_api_key under [providers] in specstory.toml.\n",
				source, ae.Status, apiKeyPage, apiKeyEnvVar))
		}
		return fail(spi.CheckErrorUnknown, err.Error(), fmt.Sprintf(
			"Could not reach the Cursor Cloud Agents API (%s).\n\nError: %v\n\n"+
				"• Accounts on Privacy Mode (Legacy) cannot use cloud agents; switch to standard Privacy Mode.\n"+
				"• Check your network connection and try again.\n", checkProbe, err))
	}

	// The API exposes no agent version; "unknown" says so honestly.
	version := "unknown"
	location := defaultAPIBaseURL
	if me.APIKeyName != "" {
		location = fmt.Sprintf("%s (key %q)", defaultAPIBaseURL, me.APIKeyName)
	}
	slog.Info("Check: succeeded", "keySource", source, "location", location)
	analytics.TrackCheckSuccess(attempt, version)
	return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: location}
}

func missingKeyMessage() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("No Cursor API key is configured.\n\n"+
		"• Create a key at %s\n"+
		"• Then set the %s environment variable, or add it to specstory.toml:\n\n"+
		"    [providers]\n    cursor_api_key = \"crsr_...\"\n", apiKeyPage, apiKeyEnvVar)
}

// DetectAgent reports whether this project has cloud agents: a key is
// configured, the project has a git origin, and either the mirror already
// holds an agent for that repository or the first page of the agent list
// names one.
func (p *Provider) DetectAgent(projectPath string, helpOutput bool) bool {
	key, _ := resolveAPIKey()
	origin := projectOrigin(projectPath)
	found := false
	if key != "" && origin != "" {
		m, _ := mirrorFor(projectPath)
		found = len(m.matchingSnapshots(origin)) > 0
		if !found {
			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), jsonTimeout)
			agents, err := newAPIClient(key).listAgents(ctx, 1)
			cancel()
			if err != nil {
				slog.Warn("DetectAgent: listing cloud agents failed", "error", err)
			}
			for _, record := range agents {
				if agentMatchesOrigin(record.agent, origin) {
					found = true
					break
				}
			}
		}
	}

	if helpOutput && !found {
		log.UserWarn("\nNo Cursor Cloud Agents were found for this project.\n")
		switch {
		case key == "":
			log.UserMessage("%s\n", missingKeyMessage())
		case origin == "":
			log.UserMessage("Cloud agents are matched to a project by its git origin URL, and this directory has no origin remote.\n")
			log.UserMessage("Run SpecStory from a clone of the repository the cloud agents worked on.\n\n")
		default:
			log.UserMessage("Cloud agents are matched to a project by repository URL. None of your agents worked on %s.\n", origin)
			log.UserMessage("Launch one at https://cursor.com/agents for this repository, then sync again.\n\n")
		}
	}
	return found
}

// GetAgentChatSessions refreshes the mirror for this project's agents, then
// builds every matching session from the mirror. Without a key or network it
// still returns what the mirror already holds.
func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
	origin := projectOrigin(projectPath)
	if origin == "" {
		slog.Debug("GetAgentChatSessions: project has no git origin; no cloud agents can match", "projectPath", projectPath)
		return []spi.AgentChatSession{}, nil
	}
	m, projectLocal := mirrorFor(projectPath)
	refreshed := p.refreshProject(context.Background(), m, projectLocal, origin)

	snapshots := m.matchingSnapshots(origin)
	total := max(len(snapshots), refreshed)
	var sessions []spi.AgentChatSession
	for i, snap := range snapshots {
		if session := convertSnapshot(snap, projectPath, debugRaw); session != nil {
			sessions = append(sessions, *session)
		}
		if progress != nil {
			progress(i+1, total)
		}
	}
	// Agents that failed to refresh and were never mirrored still count, so
	// the progress bar reaches its total.
	if progress != nil && total > len(snapshots) {
		progress(total, total)
	}
	return sessions, nil
}

// refreshProject refreshes every agent for origin and returns how many were
// attempted. Failures are logged per agent; the mirror still serves the rest.
func (p *Provider) refreshProject(ctx context.Context, m mirror, projectLocal bool, origin string) int {
	key, _ := resolveAPIKey()
	if key == "" {
		slog.Debug("No Cursor API key; reading the mirror only")
		return 0
	}
	client := newAPIClient(key)
	agents, err := client.listAgents(ctx, 0)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Warn("Failed to list cloud agents; using the mirror only", "error", err)
		return 0
	}
	attempted := 0
	for _, record := range agents {
		if !agentMatchesOrigin(record.agent, origin) {
			continue
		}
		attempted++
		if err := m.ensureRoot(projectLocal); err != nil {
			slog.Error("Failed to create mirror", "path", m.root, "error", err)
			return attempted
		}
		if err := m.refreshAgent(ctx, client, record, refreshOptions{now: time.Now()}); err != nil {
			slog.Error("Failed to refresh cloud agent", "agentId", record.agent.ID, "error", err)
		}
	}
	return attempted
}

// matchingSnapshots loads every mirrored agent whose repository is origin.
func (m mirror) matchingSnapshots(origin string) []*agentSnapshot {
	dirs, err := m.agentDirs()
	if err != nil {
		slog.Warn("Failed to read mirror", "path", m.root, "error", err)
		return nil
	}
	var snaps []*agentSnapshot
	for _, dir := range dirs {
		snap, err := loadAgentSnapshot(dir)
		if err != nil {
			slog.Warn("Skipping unreadable mirrored agent", "path", dir, "error", err)
			continue
		}
		if snap != nil && agentMatchesOrigin(snap.agent, origin) {
			snaps = append(snaps, snap)
		}
	}
	return snaps
}

// GetAgentChatSession refreshes and returns one agent when it belongs to this
// project, else nil. Membership is checked because the agent list is global
// to the key: an id alone could name another repository's agent.
func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSession(projectPath string, sessionID string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
	if !validAgentID(sessionID) {
		return nil, nil
	}
	origin := projectOrigin(projectPath)
	if origin == "" {
		return nil, nil
	}
	m, projectLocal := mirrorFor(projectPath)

	if key, _ := resolveAPIKey(); key != "" {
		ctx := context.Background()
		client := newAPIClient(key)
		record, err := client.getAgent(ctx, sessionID)
		switch {
		case isNotFound(err):
			return nil, nil
		case err != nil:
			slog.Warn("GetAgentChatSession: fetch failed; using the mirror", "sessionId", sessionID, "error", err)
		case !agentMatchesOrigin(record.agent, origin):
			return nil, nil
		default:
			if err := m.ensureRoot(projectLocal); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			if err := m.refreshAgent(ctx, client, record, refreshOptions{now: time.Now()}); err != nil {
				slog.Error("GetAgentChatSession: refresh failed", "sessionId", sessionID, "error", err)
			}
		}
	}

	snap, err := loadAgentSnapshot(m.agentDir(sessionID))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if snap == nil || !agentMatchesOrigin(snap.agent, origin) {
		return nil, nil
	}
	return convertSnapshot(snap, projectPath, debugRaw), nil
}

// GetAgentChatSessionByPath reads the agent whose agent.json is nativePath.
func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath string, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
	snap, err := loadAgentSnapshot(filepath.Dir(nativePath))
	if err != nil || snap == nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return convertSnapshot(snap, originCwd, debugRaw), nil
}

// convertSnapshot builds the session, its RawData and, when asked, the
// native debug export, all from one snapshot.
func convertSnapshot(snap *agentSnapshot, projectPath string, debugRaw bool) *spi.AgentChatSession {
	data, _ := buildSessionData(snap, workspaceRootFor(projectPath))
	if data == nil {
		slog.Debug("Skipping cloud agent with no recorded prompt yet", "agentId", snap.agent.ID)
		return nil
	}
	raw, err := buildRawData(snap)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Error("Failed to build raw data", "sessionId", snap.agent.ID, "error", err)
		return nil
	}
	if debugRaw {
		if err := writeDebugOutput(snap); err != nil {
			slog.Warn("Failed to write debug output", "sessionId", snap.agent.ID, "path", spi.GetDebugDir(snap.agent.ID), "error", err)
		}
	}
	return &spi.AgentChatSession{
		SessionID:   snap.agent.ID,
		CreatedAt:   snap.agent.CreatedAt,
		Slug:        data.Slug,
		SessionData: data,
		RawData:     raw,
	}
}

// ListAgentChatSessions lists this project's mirrored agents without any
// network access.
func (p *Provider) ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
	origin := projectOrigin(projectPath)
	result := []spi.SessionMetadata{}
	if origin == "" {
		return result, nil
	}
	m, _ := mirrorFor(projectPath)
	for _, snap := range m.matchingSnapshots(origin) {
		data, firstPrompt := buildSessionData(snap, workspaceRootFor(projectPath))
		if data == nil {
			continue
		}
		result = append(result, spi.SessionMetadata{
			SessionID: snap.agent.ID,
			CreatedAt: snap.agent.CreatedAt,
			Slug:      data.Slug,
			Name:      sessionName(snap.agent, firstPrompt),
		})
	}
	return result, nil
}

// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates the mirror across every project.
// OriginCwd stays empty: the API records a repository, never a directory, so
// reindex files these sessions under the unknown project.
func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
	m := globalMirror()
	refs := []spi.GlobalSessionRef{}
	if m.root == "" {
		return refs, nil
	}
	dirs, err := m.agentDirs()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	for _, dir := range dirs {
		snap, err := loadAgentSnapshot(dir)
		if err != nil {
			slog.Warn("reindex: skipping unreadable mirrored agent", "path", dir, "error", err)
			continue
		}
		if snap == nil {
			continue
		}
		data, firstPrompt := buildSessionData(snap, workspaceRootFor(""))
		if data == nil {
			continue
		}
		refs = append(refs, spi.GlobalSessionRef{
			SessionID:   snap.agent.ID,
			CreatedAt:   snap.agent.CreatedAt,
			Slug:        data.Slug,
			Name:        sessionName(snap.agent, firstPrompt),
			NativePath:  filepath.Join(dir, "agent.json"),
			Fingerprint: agentDirFingerprint(dir),
		})
	}
	return refs, nil
}

// runDebugFileRe matches the per-run debug files this provider writes.
var runDebugFileRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^run-[1-9][0-9]*-run-[0-9A-Fa-f-]+\.json$`)

// ownsDebugFile identifies provider-owned debug files, so a refresh removes
// stale ones (a run file from a longer earlier export) and leaves the
// CLI-owned session-data.json alone.
func ownsDebugFile(name string) bool {
	switch name {
	case "agent.json", "conversation.json", "usage.json":
		return true
	}
	return runDebugFileRe.MatchString(name)
}

// writeDebugOutput exports the snapshot's native objects pretty-printed:
// agent.json, conversation.json, usage.json and run-<n>-<runId>.json holding
// the run object and its events, numbered in run order.
func writeDebugOutput(snap *agentSnapshot) error {
	dir := spi.GetDebugDir(snap.agent.ID)
	if err := spi.PrepareDebugDir(dir, ownsDebugFile); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	write := func(name string, raw []byte) error {
		var pretty bytes.Buffer
		if err := json.Indent(&pretty, raw, "", "  "); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("format debug file %s: %w", name, err)
		}
		path := filepath.Join(dir, name)
		if err := os.WriteFile(path, pretty.Bytes(), 0o644); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("write debug file %s: %w", path, err)
		}
		return nil
	}
	if err := write("agent.json", snap.agentRaw); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if len(snap.conversationRaw) > 0 {
		if err := write("conversation.json", snap.conversationRaw); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	if len(snap.usageRaw) > 0 {
		if err := write("usage.json", snap.usageRaw); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	for i, run := range snap.runs {
		events := run.events
		if events == nil {
			events = []sseEvent{}
		}
		raw, err := json.Marshal(rawRun{Run: run.runRaw, Events: events})
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := write(fmt.Sprintf("run-%d-%s.json", i+1, run.run.ID), raw); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// noProjectOriginError explains why watch cannot start in a directory with no
// git origin.
func noProjectOriginError(projectPath string) error {
	return fmt.Errorf("cursor cloud agents are matched by repository, and %s has no git origin remote", strings.TrimSpace(projectPath))
}

== pkg/providers/cursorcloud/watcher.go
package cursorcloud

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"log/slog"
	"maps"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
)

// Watcher tuning. A remote store has no filesystem events, so a poll of the
// agent list is the change signal. Variables so tests can run in milliseconds.
var (
	// pollInterval keeps the poll (one request per page) far inside the
	// 20-requests-per-minute budget, leaving room for refreshes and streams.
	pollInterval = 60 * time.Second
	// emitDebounce coalesces a burst of stream events into one save; the
	// burst's last event is usually the completed text.
	emitDebounce = 2 * time.Second
	// reconnectDelay is the first wait before reattaching a dropped stream.
	reconnectDelay = 5 * time.Second
)

const (
	// maxLiveStreams bounds concurrent stream connections; each holds a
	// connection open for the length of a run.
	maxLiveStreams = 4
	// maxStreamReconnects bounds reattaching one dropped stream.
	maxStreamReconnects = 5
	// maxPollPages bounds the agents scanned per poll. The list is newest
	// first, so 300 agents covers any agent a person is actively running.
	maxPollPages = 3
)

// cloudWatcher polls the agent list and follows running runs live.
type cloudWatcher struct {
	origin       string
	projectPath  string
	mirror       mirror
	projectLocal bool
	client       *apiClient
	debugRaw     bool
	callback     func(*spi.AgentChatSession)

	ctx       context.Context
	cancel    context.CancelFunc
	startedAt time.Time

	mu      sync.Mutex
	seen    map[string]string // agent id -> updatedAt last acted on
	live    map[string]bool   // run ids with an attached stream
	pending map[string]bool   // agent ids queued for emission
	emitCh  chan string

	workers  sync.WaitGroup // poll loop and stream followers
	emitter  sync.WaitGroup // the single delivery worker
	stopOnce sync.Once
}

func newCloudWatcher(projectPath, origin string, client *apiClient, debugRaw bool, callback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) *cloudWatcher {
	m, projectLocal := mirrorFor(projectPath)
	return &cloudWatcher{
		origin:       origin,
		projectPath:  projectPath,
		mirror:       m,
		projectLocal: projectLocal,
		client:       client,
		debugRaw:     debugRaw,
		callback:     callback,
		seen:         map[string]string{},
		live:         map[string]bool{},
		pending:      map[string]bool{},
	}
}

// start begins polling. The context is created per start so a stopped
// watcher can be started again.
func (w *cloudWatcher) start(parent context.Context) {
	w.ctx, w.cancel = context.WithCancel(parent)
	w.startedAt = time.Now()
	w.emitCh = make(chan string, 64)
	w.stopOnce = sync.Once{}
	w.emitter.Go(w.emitLoop)
	w.workers.Go(w.pollLoop)
}

// stop cancels polling and streams, waits for every follower to write its
// final events and queue any update not yet delivered, then drains delivery.
func (w *cloudWatcher) stop() {
	w.stopOnce.Do(func() {
		w.cancel()
		w.workers.Wait()
		close(w.emitCh)
		w.emitter.Wait()
	})
}

// pollLoop runs the baseline poll, then polls every pollInterval.
func (w *cloudWatcher) pollLoop() {
	baseline := true
	for {
		w.poll(baseline)
		baseline = false
		if sleepContext(w.ctx, pollInterval) != nil {
			return
		}
	}
}

// poll lists agents and acts on the ones for this project. The baseline poll
// mirrors whatever is new but emits nothing: existing sessions are not news
// because the watcher started. Afterwards an agent seen for the first time or
// whose updatedAt moved is refreshed and emitted. An agent changing during the
// baseline is caught by the next poll, because the baseline records the
// updatedAt it listed, not what the agent became.
func (w *cloudWatcher) poll(baseline bool) {
	agents, err := w.client.listAgents(w.ctx, maxPollPages)
	if err != nil {
		if w.ctx.Err() == nil {
			slog.Warn("WatchAgent: listing cloud agents failed; retrying next poll", "error", err)
		}
		return
	}
	for _, record := range agents {
		if w.ctx.Err() != nil {
			return
		}
		agent := record.agent
		if !agentMatchesOrigin(agent, w.origin) {
			continue
		}
		w.mu.Lock()
		prev, known := w.seen[agent.ID]
		skip := w.liveSnapshot()
		w.mu.Unlock()
		if known && prev == agent.UpdatedAt {
			continue
		}

		if err := w.mirror.ensureRoot(w.projectLocal); err != nil {
			slog.Error("WatchAgent: cannot create mirror", "path", w.mirror.root, "error", err)
			return
		}
		if err := w.mirror.refreshAgent(w.ctx, w.client, record, refreshOptions{skipStreams: skip, now: time.Now()}); err != nil {
			if w.ctx.Err() == nil {
				slog.Error("WatchAgent: refreshing cloud agent failed", "agentId", agent.ID, "error", err)
			}
			continue
		}
		w.mu.Lock()
		w.seen[agent.ID] = agent.UpdatedAt
		w.mu.Unlock()
		if baseline {
			slog.Debug("WatchAgent: baseline", "agentId", agent.ID, "updatedAt", agent.UpdatedAt)
		} else {
			slog.Info("WatchAgent: cloud agent updated", "agentId", agent.ID, "updatedAt", agent.UpdatedAt)
			w.enqueue(agent.ID)
		}
	}
	w.attachRunning()
}

// liveSnapshot copies the attached-run set; callers hold w.mu.
func (w *cloudWatcher) liveSnapshot() map[string]bool {
	return maps.Clone(w.live)
}

// attachRunning starts a follower for every unfinished run in this project's
// mirror that has none, up to maxLiveStreams.
func (w *cloudWatcher) attachRunning() {
	for _, snap := range w.mirror.matchingSnapshots(w.origin) {
		for _, run := range snap.runs {
			if run.run.isTerminal() {
				continue
			}
			w.mu.Lock()
			attach := !w.live[run.run.ID] && len(w.live) < maxLiveStreams && w.ctx.Err() == nil
			if attach {
				w.live[run.run.ID] = true
			}
			w.mu.Unlock()
			if !attach {
				continue
			}
			agentID, runID := snap.agent.ID, run.run.ID
			slog.Info("WatchAgent: following live run", "agentId", agentID, "runId", runID)
			w.workers.Go(func() {
				w.followRun(agentID, runID)
				w.mu.Lock()
				delete(w.live, runID)
				w.mu.Unlock()
			})
		}
	}
}

// followRun streams a run into its events file until the run ends or the
// watcher stops. Events are flushed and the session queued for delivery after
// each burst (debounced), once more when the run ends, and on stop if an
// update is still undelivered. Only events stamped after the watcher started
// count as activity: attaching replays the run from its start.
func (w *cloudWatcher) followRun(agentID, runID string) {
	events, err := readEventsFile(w.mirror.eventsFile(agentID, runID))
	if err != nil {
		slog.Error("WatchAgent: reading mirrored events failed", "runId", runID, "error", err)
		return
	}
	if eventsAreWhole(events) {
		return
	}
	undelivered := false
	flush := func() {
		if err := w.mirror.writeEvents(agentID, runID, events); err != nil {
			slog.Error("WatchAgent: writing events failed", "runId", runID, "error", err)
		}
		if undelivered {
			w.enqueue(agentID)
			undelivered = false
		}
	}

	done := false
	delay := reconnectDelay
	for attempt := 0; !done && w.ctx.Err() == nil && attempt <= maxStreamReconnects; attempt++ {
		lastID := lastEventID(events)
		body, err := w.client.openStream(w.ctx, agentID, runID, lastID)
		if errors.Is(err, errStreamExpired) {
			slog.Info("WatchAgent: run stream expired", "runId", runID)
			break
		}
		if err != nil {
			if w.ctx.Err() == nil {
				slog.Warn("WatchAgent: stream connect failed", "runId", runID, "attempt", attempt+1, "error", err)
				_ = sleepContext(w.ctx, delay)
				delay = min(delay*2, maxBackoff)
			}
			continue
		}

		// A resumed stream may repeat events carrying the resume id: ids are
		// not unique (a thinking event and its interaction_update share one).
		repeats := eventsWithID(events, lastID)
		incoming := make(chan sseEvent)
		var reader sync.WaitGroup
		var readErr error
		reader.Go(func() {
			defer close(incoming)
			readErr = readSSE(body, agentID+"/"+runID, func(ev sseEvent) bool {
				select {
				case incoming <- ev:
					return ev.Event != "done"
				case <-w.ctx.Done():
					return false
				}
			})
		})

		debounce := time.NewTimer(emitDebounce)
		debounce.Stop()
	receive:
		for {
			select {
			case ev, ok := <-incoming:
				if !ok {
					break receive
				}
				if lastID != "" && ev.ID == lastID && repeats[eventKey(ev)] {
					continue
				}
				events = append(events, ev)
				if t, ok := eventInstant(ev.ID); ok && !t.Before(w.startedAt) {
					undelivered = true
				}
				if ev.Event == "done" {
					done = true
				}
				debounce.Reset(emitDebounce)
			case <-debounce.C:
				flush()
			case <-w.ctx.Done():
				break receive
			}
		}
		debounce.Stop()
		_ = body.Close()
		reader.Wait()
		if readErr != nil && w.ctx.Err() == nil && !done {
			slog.Warn("WatchAgent: stream dropped; reconnecting", "runId", runID, "error", readErr)
		}
	}

	if done {
		// The run object now says how the run ended; fetch it so the exchange
		// carries the final status and branch.
		if runs, err := w.client.listRuns(w.ctx, agentID); err == nil {
			for _, run := range runs {
				if err := writeFileAtomic(w.mirror.runFile(agentID, run.run.ID), run.raw); err != nil {
					slog.Error("WatchAgent: writing run failed", "runId", run.run.ID, "error", err)
				}
			}
		} else if w.ctx.Err() == nil {
			slog.Warn("WatchAgent: refreshing finished run failed", "runId", runID, "error", err)
		}
		slog.Info("WatchAgent: live run finished", "agentId", agentID, "runId", runID)
	}
	flush()
}

// lastEventID returns the id of the last event that carries one.
func lastEventID(events []sseEvent) string {
	for i := len(events) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		if events[i].ID != "" {
			return events[i].ID
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// eventsWithID returns the identities of recorded events with the given id.
func eventsWithID(events []sseEvent, id string) map[string]bool {
	set := map[string]bool{}
	if id == "" {
		return set
	}
	for _, ev := range events {
		if ev.ID == id {
			set[eventKey(ev)] = true
		}
	}
	return set
}

func eventKey(ev sseEvent) string {
	data, _ := json.Marshal(ev)
	return string(data)
}

// enqueue queues an agent for delivery, coalescing repeats still waiting.
func (w *cloudWatcher) enqueue(agentID string) {
	w.mu.Lock()
	if w.pending[agentID] {
		w.mu.Unlock()
		return
	}
	w.pending[agentID] = true
	w.mu.Unlock()
	w.emitCh <- agentID
}

// emitLoop delivers sessions one at a time, in queue order, from the mirror.
func (w *cloudWatcher) emitLoop() {
	for agentID := range w.emitCh {
		w.mu.Lock()
		delete(w.pending, agentID)
		w.mu.Unlock()
		snap, err := loadAgentSnapshot(w.mirror.agentDir(agentID))
		if err != nil || snap == nil {
			slog.Warn("WatchAgent: cannot read mirrored agent", "agentId", agentID, "error", err)
			continue
		}
		session := convertSnapshot(snap, w.projectPath, w.debugRaw)
		if session == nil {
			continue
		}
		spi.DeliverSession("WatchAgent", w.callback, session)
	}
}

package cursorcloud

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"os/signal"
	"runtime"
	"syscall"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
)

// dashboardURL is where cloud agents are launched and followed.
const dashboardURL = "https://cursor.com/agents"

// ExecAgentAndWatch is `run` for a hosted agent. No local process exists, so
// it opens the cloud agents dashboard (or one agent's page when resuming) with
// the configured opener and then watches until Ctrl-C exactly like WatchAgent.
func (p *Provider) ExecAgentAndWatch(projectPath string, customCommand string, resumeSessionID string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
	slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: starting", "projectPath", projectPath, "customCommand", customCommand, "resumeSessionID", resumeSessionID, "debugRaw", debugRaw)

	target := dashboardURL
	if resumeSessionID != "" {
		if validAgentID(resumeSessionID) {
			target = dashboardURL + "/" + resumeSessionID
		} else {
			slog.Warn("ExecAgentAndWatch: ignoring malformed agent id", "resumeSessionID", resumeSessionID)
		}
	}
	if err := openURL(customCommand, target); err != nil {
		// Watching still works when the browser could not be opened; the
		// user can follow the printed URL.
		slog.Warn("ExecAgentAndWatch: opening the dashboard failed", "url", target, "error", err)
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Could not open %s (%v). Open it in a browser; watching for Cursor Cloud Agent activity — press Ctrl-C to stop.\n", target, err)
	} else {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Opened %s — watching for Cursor Cloud Agent activity, press Ctrl-C to stop.\n", target)
	}

	ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer cancel()
	err := p.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
	if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
		err = nil
	}
	slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: exiting", "error", err)
	return err
}

// openURL runs the opener with url appended. The default is the platform's
// URL handler; a custom command (cursorcloud_cmd or -c) replaces it.
func openURL(customCommand, url string) error {
	args := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
	if len(args) == 0 {
		args = defaultOpener()
	}
	if len(args) == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("no URL opener for %s", runtime.GOOS)
	}
	cmd := exec.Command(args[0], append(args[1:], url)...)
	slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: opening dashboard", "command", args[0], "url", url)
	return cmd.Run()
}

// defaultOpener is the platform's own URL handler.
func defaultOpener() []string {
	switch runtime.GOOS {
	case "darwin":
		return []string{"open"}
	case "windows":
		return []string{"rundll32", "url.dll,FileProtocolHandler"}
	default:
		return []string{"xdg-open"}
	}
}

// WatchAgent polls for cloud agent activity on this project's repository and
// delivers each new or updated session until ctx is cancelled.
func (p *Provider) WatchAgent(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
	slog.Info("WatchAgent: starting Cursor Cloud Agent polling", "projectPath", projectPath, "debugRaw", debugRaw)
	key, source := resolveAPIKey()
	if key == "" {
		slog.Info("WatchAgent: no API key configured")
		return errors.New("no Cursor API key: set CURSOR_API_KEY or cursor_api_key under [providers] in specstory.toml")
	}
	origin := projectOrigin(projectPath)
	if origin == "" {
		slog.Info("WatchAgent: project has no git origin", "projectPath", projectPath)
		return noProjectOriginError(projectPath)
	}

	watcher := newCloudWatcher(projectPath, origin, newAPIClient(key), debugRaw, sessionCallback)
	watcher.start(ctx)
	slog.Info("WatchAgent: polling", "origin", origin, "keySource", source, "mirror", watcher.mirror.root, "interval", pollInterval)

	<-ctx.Done()
	slog.Info("WatchAgent: context cancelled, stopping")
	watcher.stop()
	slog.Info("WatchAgent: stopped")
	return ctx.Err()
}

func TestRateLimiterSpacesRequests(t *testing.T) {
	clock := &fakeClock{now: time.Unix(1_800_000_000, 0)}
	limiter := &rateLimiter{interval: 3 * time.Second, now: clock.Now, sleep: clock.Sleep}

	for range 3 {
		if err := limiter.wait(context.Background()); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	// The first request goes at once; each later one waits out the interval.
	want := []time.Duration{3 * time.Second, 3 * time.Second}
	if len(clock.slept) != len(want) || clock.slept[0] != want[0] || clock.slept[1] != want[1] {
		t.Errorf("slept %v, want %v", clock.slept, want)
	}

	// A 429 seen by one caller pushes every later slot past its Retry-After.
	limiter.holdUntil(clock.Now().Add(20 * time.Second))
	clock.slept = nil
	if err := limiter.wait(context.Background()); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(clock.slept) != 1 || clock.slept[0] != 20*time.Second {
		t.Errorf("after holdUntil slept %v, want [20s]", clock.slept)
	}
}

_**Agent (claude-fable-5-1 2026-10-13 16:48:03Z)**_

Confirmed the cause of the one failing test, and it is a real, small fidelity issue rather than a test bug: the event payload contains `&`, and `encodeEvents` goes through `json.Marshal`, which HTML-escapes `&`, `<` and `>` inside a `RawMessage` to `\u0026` and friends. The mirror file therefore no longer holds the API's exact bytes. The fix is a `json.Encoder` with `SetEscapeHTML(false)` for the events file, and the same for any other place raw API bytes are re-serialised, such as `buildRawData`. I'll hold this for the session to find on its own test run and confirm it gets fixed; if it is still failing at the next checkpoint I'll flag it to you to relay.

Nothing else needed right now. Monitor remains armed.

func TestCapturedFailuresRenderTheError(t *testing.T) {
	// The failure-run capture's deliberate failures, keyed by call id.
	want := map[string]string{
		"read_file":   "Error: File not found",
		"delete_file": "Error: File not found: /workspace/missing-file.txt",
		"grep_search": "Error: Path does not exist: /nonexistent-path",
		"web_fetch":   "Error: Error fetching URL, status code: 500 Internal Server Error",
	}
	found := map[string]bool{}
	for _, msg := range renderedCalls(t) {
		md := ""
		if msg.Tool.FormattedMarkdown != nil {
			md = *msg.Tool.FormattedMarkdown
		}
		if text, ok := want[msg.Tool.Name]; ok && strings.Contains(md, text) {
			found[msg.Tool.Name] = true
		}
		if msg.Tool.Name == "run_terminal_cmd" && strings.Contains(md, "cat /nonexistent-file") {
			found["shell failure"] = true
			if !strings.Contains(md, "Exit code: 1") || !strings.Contains(md, "No such file or directory") {
				t.Errorf("shell failure lacks exit code or stderr:\n%s", md)
			}
		}
	}
	for name := range want {
		if !found[name] {
			t.Errorf("no %s call rendered %q", name, want[name])
		}
	}
	if !found["shell failure"] {
		t.Error("the failing shell command was not rendered")
	}
}

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Latest published version of the Cursor Cloud Agents API.
#
# Channel: the OpenAPI document Cursor publishes for the API,
# https://cursor.com/docs-static/cloud-agents-openapi.yaml; its info.version is
# the only version string the hosted service exposes. Cloud agents run in
# Cursor's backend, so there is no binary, npm tag, GitHub release or installer
# to track. Rejected: GET /v1/me (needs a key and reports no version) and the
# cursor-agent installer (that is the local CLI, tracked by cursorcli).
#
# There is no install or list-tools script: nothing installs locally, and the
# tool inventory is recorded from a paid cloud run (see examples/tools.txt),
# which an unattended factory job must not launch.
#
# Factory SPI contract: print the current released version to stdout and exit 0.
# Non-zero exit means "sensor failure", never "no change". Output is opaque to
# the factory — byte-compared against the stored reading, never parsed.
set -euo pipefail
# awk reads the whole document (no early exit) so curl never sees a closed
# pipe, which pipefail would report as a sensor failure.
version=$(curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 --retry 2 --retry-delay 2 https://cursor.com/docs-static/cloud-agents-openapi.yaml \
  | awk '/^info:/ { in_info = 1; next } in_info && /^[^ ]/ { in_info = 0 } in_info && !found && $1 == "version:" { print $2; found = 1 }' \
  | tr -d "\"'")
if [ -z "$version" ]; then
  echo "could not read info.version from cloud-agents-openapi.yaml (document format changed?)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' "$version"
=== run under isolated home
1.0.0
exit=0
=== negative case (unreachable)
1.0.0
exit=0

````text
1	# Cursor Cloud Agent session format
2	
3	A Cursor Cloud Agent runs in Cursor's backend. Its conversation is never written to the user's machine, so the provider's native store is the Cloud Agents REST API at `https://api.cursor.com`, and a local mirror of that API is what every read path parses. Everything below was observed against the live API on 2026-10-13 (API `info.version` 1.0.0, v1 public beta plus legacy v0). The captures are in `testdata/` and `examples/captures/`.
4	
5	## Baseline version
6	
7	The API exposes no agent version. `CheckResult.Version` and `ProviderInfo.Version` are `"unknown"`. The factory sensor tracks the OpenAPI document's `info.version` (`1.0.0`). Hook payloads inside the VM report `cursor_version 1.0.0`, which is not reachable from outside the VM.
8	
9	## Authentication and limits
10	
11	- `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, where the key comes from `https://cursor.com/dashboard/api`. The provider reads `CURSOR_API_KEY`, and otherwise `cursor_api_key` under `[providers]` in `specstory.toml`.
12	- The documented limit is 20 requests per minute. The OpenAPI document promises `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-*` headers on `429`, but no rate-limit headers appeared on successful responses. The client spaces every request 3 s apart across the whole process and retries `429` and `5xx` responses, honouring `Retry-After` when it is present.
13	- Accounts on Privacy Mode (Legacy) get `400 validation_error` "Cloud agent is not supported in Privacy Mode (Legacy)" from every agent call.
14	
15	## Endpoints read
16	
17	| Call | Shape |
18	| --- | --- |
19	| `GET /v1/me` | `{apiKeyName, userId, createdAt, userEmail, userFirstName, userLastName}`. Check reports `apiKeyName` only |
20	| `GET /v1/agents?limit=100&cursor=` | `{items:[agent], nextCursor?}`, newest first. `agent` = `{id: "bc-<uuid>", name, status: ACTIVE\|IDLE\|ARCHIVED, env, repos:[{url}], workOnCurrentBranch, autoCreatePR?, openAsCursorGithubApp, skipReviewerRequest, url, createdAt, updatedAt, latestRunId}` |
21	| `GET /v1/agents/{id}` | one `agent` |
22	| `GET /v1/agents/{id}/runs` | `{items:[run]}`, newest first. `run` = `{id: "run-<uuid>", agentId, status: CREATING\|RUNNING\|FINISHED\|ERROR\|CANCELLED\|EXPIRED, createdAt, updatedAt, durationMs?, git:{branches:[{repoUrl, branch, prUrl?}]}}`. The single-run GET adds `result` (the final text); the list omits it |
23	| `GET /v1/agents/{id}/runs/{runId}/stream` | SSE, described below. Returns `410 {"error":{"code":"stream_expired","message":"Run stream is no longer available"}}` once retention has passed |
24	| `GET /v0/agents/{id}/conversation` | `{id, messages:[{id, type: user_message\|assistant_message, text}]}`, covering every run of the agent, text only, with no timestamps. Kept indefinitely |
25	| `GET /v1/agents/{id}/usage` | `{totalUsage:{inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheWriteTokens, cacheReadTokens, totalTokens}, cost:{rawCostCents, chargedCents}, runs:[{id, usageUuid, usage, cost}]}` |
26	
27	`repos[].url` on v1 is `https://github.com/org/repo`, while `git.branches[].repoUrl` and v0 `source.repository` are `github.com/org/repo`. Both normalize to the same string as the project's origin.
28	
29	## Run stream grammar
30	
31	Each SSE block has an optional `id: <epochMillis>-<seq>`, an `event: <name>` and a `data: <json>` line. The id is the only timestamp in the stream. Ids are not unique: a `thinking` event and its `interaction_update` `thinking-delta` share one. The stream is retained for `x-cursor-stream-retention-seconds: 86400` after a run ends. A finished run replays in full from the start, and the replay matches the live capture block for block, except that the opening `status` says `FINISHED` and live-only `heartbeat` events are absent.
32	
33	| Event | Data | Rendering |
34	| --- | --- | --- |
35	| `status` | `{runId, status}` (no id) | none; the first and last block of a stream |
36	| `heartbeat` | `{}` (no id) | none; sent on a quiet live stream |
37	| `interaction_update` `user-message-appended` | `{userMessage:{type, session_id, text}}` | the user prompt, which is the only place the stream records it |
38	| `interaction_update` `token-delta`, `text-delta`, `thinking-delta` | deltas | none; these duplicate the typed events |
39	| `interaction_update` `step-started`, `step-completed`, `thinking-completed`, `tool-call-started`, `tool-call-completed`, `tool-requests-listed`, `partial-tool-call`, `turn-ended` | lifecycle | none |
40	| `thinking` | `{text}` delta | consecutive deltas concatenate into one thinking part |
41	| `assistant` | `{text}` delta | consecutive deltas concatenate into one text part |
42	| `tool_call` | `{callId, name, status: running\|completed, args?, result?}` | one tool message per `callId`, placed at its first event |
43	| `result` | `{runId, status, text, durationMs, git}` | its time ends the exchange; `text` repeats the final assistant text and is not rendered |
44	| `done` | `{}` | marks the end of the stream; a mirrored capture ending in `done` is whole |
45	
46	A `tool_call` arrives several times per call. A `running` event may have no `args` yet while they stream in. The last event's fields win. A `running` event can carry a provisional `result: {error: {error: "Invalid arguments"}}` with `args: {toolCallId: "unknown-tool-call-id"}`, which the completed event then replaces, so results are taken only from non-`running` events.
47	
48	Result shapes:
49	
50	- Success: `{success: {...}}`.
51	- Tool failure: `{error: {error: "..."}}` (`delete_file`, `grep_search`, `web_fetch`, which also adds `url`) or `{error: {errorMessage: "..."}}` (`read_file`).
52	- A shell command that exits non-zero: `{failure: {command, exitCode, stderr, interleavedOutput, executionTime}, isBackground}`.
53	
54	The provider removes the plumbing keys `toolCallId`, `conversationId` and `requestId` from inputs. Every tool path sits under the VM checkout `/workspace`. Paths are rendered relative to it, and path hints are rewritten onto the local project before they are made relative.
55	
56	## Tools
57	
58	The names recorded in `tool_call.name` differ from the names the model sees. `examples/tools.txt` holds both lists and the mapping between them.
59	
60	| Name | Type | Input rendered | Result rendered |
61	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
62	| `run_terminal_cmd` | shell | `command` in a bash fence, plus `workingDirectory` when it is not `/workspace`. The summary uses `description` | `interleavedOutput` (or `stdout` + `stderr`) in a text fence. `failure` adds `Exit code`, and `isBackground` adds a note |
63	| `read_file` | read | `path` in the summary | `content` fenced by file extension, with a line range when partial |
64	| `edit_file` | write | the result's `diffString` as a diff, or `streamContent` while the call is still streaming | none (the diff is the body) |
65	| `delete_file` | write | `path` | `prevContent` as removed lines |
66	| `file_search` | search | `globPattern` in the summary, plus `targetDirectory` | file list |
67	| `grep_search` | search | `pattern` in the summary, plus `path` and flags | `file:line: content` lines from `workspaceResults` |
68	| `web_search` | search | `searchTerm` | each reference's `chunk`, which is already a markdown link list plus a synthesis |
69	| `web_fetch` | read | `url` | `markdown` in a markdown fence |
70	| `todo_write` | task | `todos[]` as a checklist (`TODO_STATUS_*` mapped) | none |
71	| `mcp` | generic | `serverIdentifier`, `toolName`; other arguments as JSON | `content[].text.text`; `structuredContent` repeats it and is omitted |
72	| `get_mcp_tools` | generic | `server`, `toolName` | `content` (a JSON string), plus `outputFilePath` |
73	| `await` | generic | `blockUntilMs` | `complete.runtimeMs` |
74	| `generate_image` | generic | `description`, `aspectRatio`, `filePath` | saved `filePath` |
75	| `write_canvas` / `read_canvas` | generic | `title` and `contents` / `canvasId` | link to the canvas `url`, plus `source` |
76	| `pr_management` | generic | seen once in the research spike, but not captured; rendered generically | generic |
77	
78	Any other name renders as JSON with type `unknown`.
79	
80	## Session model
81	
82	- One agent is one session. The id is `bc-…`, `CreatedAt` is `agent.createdAt`, `UpdatedAt` is `agent.updatedAt`, and the slug comes from the first user prompt. `Name` is `agent.name`, which Cursor derives from the prompt when the launcher gives none.
83	- One run is one exchange, in `createdAt` order, and `ExchangeID` is the run id. `StartTime` is the first event id, and `EndTime` is the `result` event id. Metadata holds `runId`, `status`, `durationMs`, `branch`, `prUrl` and `agentUrl`.
84	- `Model` is empty because the API does not expose it. `Usage` is nil because usage is per run, not per message. Both stay in `RawData`.
85	- When a run's stream was never captured, or a finished run's capture is partial and the stream has expired, the exchange is built from the v0 conversation instead. That fallback is text only, and the exchange is marked `"source": "v0-conversation"`. Messages with ids `turn-N:…` belong to run index N; the first user message has a bare UUID id and belongs to turn 0. The user message takes the run's `createdAt` as its time, and agent messages have none.
86	- `WorkspaceRoot` is the caller's project path. `GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd` is empty: the API records a repository and never a directory, so reindex attributes these sessions to the `unknown` project.
87	
88	## The mirror (write lifecycle)
89	
90	The mirror defaults to `<project>/.specstory/cursorcloud/`. The `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` setting or `--user-data-dir cursorcloud:<path>` relocates it. A project-local mirror gets a `.gitignore` of `*`, because it holds unredacted raw transcripts.
91	
92	```text
93	agents/<agentId>/agent.json                  agent object (written last in a refresh)
94	agents/<agentId>/conversation.json           v0 conversation
95	agents/<agentId>/usage.json                  usage
96	agents/<agentId>/runs/<runId>.json           run object from the run list
97	agents/<agentId>/runs/<runId>.events.jsonl   one {"id","event","data"} object per SSE block
98	```
99	
100	- Every write is atomic (a temporary file, then a rename), and a file whose bytes are unchanged is not rewritten, so a sync that finds nothing new leaves every byte and mtime as it was.
101	- Runs, conversation and usage are re-fetched only when `agent.updatedAt` differs from the mirrored `agent.json`.
102	- A finished run whose events are missing or partial is replayed while it is within 24 h of its `updatedAt`. A `410` leaves the partial capture in place. A whole capture is never fetched again.
103	- `sync` never attaches to an unfinished run, because reading its stream blocks until the run ends. `watch` attaches live, appends events, and rewrites the file atomically after each burst.
104	- An agent directory without `agent.json` is not an agent yet. Readers skip it.
105	
106	## Resume
107	
108	Same-agent resume (`specstory resume` of a cloud session into `cursorcloud`) opens `https://cursor.com/agents/<id>`, where a follow-up run can be started, and then watches. Resuming another agent's session into `cursorcloud` is unsupported: the only way to create a cloud agent conversation is to launch a new paid run, so `ReconstructSession` returns `spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported`. Resuming a cloud session into a local agent works through the shared `SessionData` flattening.
109
````

+### Notes on Cursor Cloud Agents
+
+Cursor Cloud Agents run in Cursor's backend, and their conversations are never written to your machine. --- impl entries
Entries added during planning are marked (plan); the implementation session appends its own and marks them (impl).

## 1. "Learn the agent's on-disk session format" (plan)

Assumes a session is written to disk and that the write lifecycle is file-based. A hosted agent has no local files; the contract is an API, with its own lifecycle (a stream that is retained for 24 hours, a text-only endpoint that lasts forever, an `updatedAt` that signals change).

Proposed: rename to "Learn the agent's native session store" and add one sentence: "For a hosted agent the store is its API. Document the endpoints, response shapes, retention windows, rate limits and the freshness signal in `<AGENT>-FORMAT.md` exactly as you would files and timestamps, and keep a local mirror so that reads, reindex and debug output still work offline."

## 2. Exemplar table (plan)

No row covers a remote or API-backed provider. Once `cursorcloud` lands, add a row: "Remote/API store: credential resolution, rate limiting, SSE streaming, a local mirror, and a polling watcher: `pkg/providers/cursorcloud`."

## 3. "The watcher" and the self-review checklist (plan)

Every rule is phrased in terms of fsnotify, and the checklist says "fsnotify events are the primary change signal". A remote store has no filesystem events; the only signal is polling. The acceptance cases (baseline at startup, activity during initialisation, late arrivals, nothing on stop) are still the right contract and map cleanly onto a poller.

Proposed: open the section with "For a file-based store, filesystem events through fsnotify are the primary change signal… For a remote store, a bounded poll of the agent list is the primary signal; the same acceptance cases apply, with 'file written' read as 'agent updated'." Then mark the fsnotify-specific bullets (NewFSWatcher, Windows deadlock, descriptor bounds, date windows) as "file-based stores only" and add two remote-store bullets: stay inside the documented rate limit with a client-side limiter and honour `429` and `Retry-After`; a live stream that disconnects is resumed, never restarted from a blank state.

## 4. "Run and exec" (plan)

Assumes `run` launches a terminal process or an IDE. A hosted agent is launched from a web dashboard or an API, so `run` can only open that dashboard and then watch. The `<id>_cmd` config key, which the wiring tests require, then means "the command used to open the dashboard URL", which is a stretch of its documented meaning.

Proposed: add "For a hosted agent, `run` opens the agent's web surface with the configured `<id>_cmd` (default: the OS URL opener) and then behaves as `watch`. Say so in the README row." Alternatively allow the wiring tests to accept a provider that declares it has no launch command.

## 5. "Check and analytics" (plan)

`Check` is defined as resolving a binary and probing `--version`. A remote provider resolves a credential and probes an identity endpoint. The guide's error taxonomy (`not_found`, `permission_denied`, `unknown`) still fits: missing key, rejected key, other.

Proposed: add "A remote provider's `Check` resolves its credential instead of a binary: a missing credential is `CheckErrorNotFound` with guidance on where to create it, a rejected one is `CheckErrorPermissionDenied`, and any other probe failure is `CheckErrorUnknown`. Name the endpoint probed in `CheckAttempt.VersionFlag`."

## 6. Honest data: `CheckResult.Version` and `ProviderInfo.Version` (plan)

"`CheckResult.Version` is the agent's version string or empty. Never a label." and later "Empty `--version` output on a successful run is a success reported as `"unknown"`." Those two sentences disagree, and the check command already omits an empty version for IDE providers. A hosted service has no version at all.

Proposed: pick one. Recommended: `CheckResult.Version` empty when nothing is discoverable (the CLI omits the line), `ProviderInfo.Version` the literal `"unknown"` as today, and drop the "reported as unknown" sentence from the Check bullet.

## 7. Credentials and settings reaching a provider (plan)

The guide's only configuration channel is `<id>_cmd` passed as `customCommand`. An API provider needs a credential and a mirror location. Nothing says where those live or how they reach the provider, and providers cannot import `pkg/config`.

Proposed: add a "Provider settings" subsection: "Settings other than the launch command are read by the CLI from `[providers]` and handed to the provider through package-level setters called at startup (the pattern `cursoride.SetUserDataDirOverride` already uses). Environment variables override the config file. Secrets never appear in generated artifacts, debug output or logs."

## 8. "Enumerate the agent's real tools yourself" (plan)

The tools.txt instructions assume the model's self-reported names are what sessions record. For Cursor Cloud the model-facing names (`Shell`, `Read`, `StrReplace`) differ from the names the API records (`run_terminal_cmd`, `read_file`, `edit_file`), so a tools.txt built from the self-report would match nothing.

Proposed: add "If the harness records tool names that differ from the names the model sees, list the recorded names, since those are what the provider matches, and keep the model's inventory alongside with the mapping."

## 9. `GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd` and project identity (plan)

Global enumeration attributes sessions to projects only through a working directory. A hosted agent knows its repository URL and never a directory, so every cloud session lands in the `unknown` project even though the CLI's own `git_id` is derived from exactly that URL.

Proposed: an SPI addition, `GlobalSessionRef.OriginRepoURL`, which reindex hashes with the same normalization as `git_id` when `OriginCwd` is empty. Until then the guide should say that a provider with only a repository identity leaves `OriginCwd` empty and documents the limitation.

## 10. Shared git-origin helpers (plan)

Matching an agent to a project needs the origin URL normalization that lives in `pkg/utils/project_identity.go`, which providers may not import. The guide lists the shared helpers in `pkg/spi` but has no git helper.

Proposed: move `normalizeGitURL`, `readOriginURL`, `findGitRoot` and `resolveGitConfigPath` to `pkg/spi` (`spi.GitOriginURL`, `spi.NormalizeGitRemoteURL`) with `pkg/utils` delegating, and list them under "Reuse the shared helpers".

## 11. Software factory affordances (plan)

`latest-version` assumes a release channel (npm tag, GitHub release, installer manifest). A hosted API has none; the nearest sensor is the OpenAPI document's `info.version`. `install` and `list-tools` cannot exist.

Proposed: add "A hosted agent ships `latest-version` reading the vendor's published API specification version, and states in the header that there is no binary to install or enumerate."

## 12. Manual test table (plan)

Rows assume a terminal agent takes over the terminal, and that resume into the agent is possible. For a hosted agent `run` cannot take the terminal, and resume into it would launch a paid run.

Proposed: a short note under the table: "A hosted agent substitutes 'opens its web surface and watches' for the `run` row, and 'refuses with a clear message' for the resume-into-agent rows, and records both in the PR."

## 13. `.specstory/` contents and raw mirrors (plan)

"`.specstory/history` is committed in this repository; do not add `.specstory/` to any `.gitignore`" does not say what a provider-owned directory under `.specstory/` may contain. A mirror of raw API transcripts is unredacted data; redaction only applies to markdown and cloud sync.

Proposed: state whether a provider may keep raw data under `.specstory/` and, if so, whether it must be ignored from git by the provider or by documentation. (Decision pending with Sean.)

## 14. "Rendering": failure is not always an error branch (impl)

"A failed call renders the agent's error text; the error branch takes priority over the success formatter for every tool" assumes one failure shape. Cursor Cloud records three: `result.error.error` (delete, grep, web fetch), `result.error.errorMessage` (read), and, for a shell command that exits non-zero, a separate `result.failure` branch carrying `exitCode` and `stderr` rather than an error. A renderer that only checks the error branch shows a failed command as a success with no output.

Proposed: "Capture at least one deliberately failed call per tool family and render every failure shape you observe, including non-zero shell exits recorded outside the error branch. Show the exit code with the output."

## 15. "Parsing": provisional results on in-progress records (impl)

The guide says results are paired by native correlation fields and does not cover a record that is updated several times. Cursor Cloud emits several `tool_call` events per call id. A `running` event can carry a placeholder `{"error":{"error":"Invalid arguments"}}` while arguments are still streaming, and the completed event later replaces it. A naive "last field wins" merge is correct only when the call completes. For a call interrupted mid-stream it would render a fake error.

Proposed: "When a call is re-serialized on every state update, merge field by field, and take results only from records the native format marks as final. Test an interrupted call."

## 16. "The watcher": mapping the acceptance cases onto a poller (impl)

The acceptance cases held up, but each needed a translation that the guide could state once:

| Guide case | Poller equivalent used |
| --- | --- |
| File written before startup, unchanged | Agent listed at the baseline poll, `updatedAt` unchanged afterwards |
| File changes while the baseline is established | The baseline records the `updatedAt` it listed; a change during the baseline's own fetches is seen as an advance by the next poll |
| Directory appears after startup with old mtimes | Agent first listed after the baseline, whatever its `createdAt` |
| Pre-existing directory discovered late in the initial scan | Agent on a later page of the baseline listing |
| Shutdown with nothing pending | Stop joins every poll and stream goroutine; an undelivered burst is drained, nothing else is emitted |

Two additions only a remote store needs: live events replayed on attach must not count as new activity (the provider counts only events stamped after the watcher started), and a resumed stream (`Last-Event-ID`) may repeat events, because SSE ids are not unique in this API. Proposed: add the table above under "For a remote store" next to entry 3.

## 17. Wiring tests assume every `[providers]` key is a command (impl)

`TestProvidersConfigIsFullyWired` derives a provider id from every `ProvidersConfig` field by stripping `_cmd`. The two new settings, `cursor_api_key` and `cursorcloud_mirror_dir`, made it fail. The test now skips non-`_cmd` keys that are listed in an explicit `nonCommandProviderSettings` allowlist, so a new key is still a deliberate choice. The settings reach the provider through `cmd.ApplyProviderSettings`, called from `main.go` right after the config loads.

Proposed: in "Wiring outside the package", add "A provider setting that is not a launch command goes in `ProvidersConfig`, in the template, in `nonCommandProviderSettings` in the config test, and in `cmd.ApplyProviderSettings`, which hands it to a package-level setter."

## 18. `check <id> -c` for a provider with no binary (impl)

The manual table says "`-c` with a bad path fails with guidance naming that path". For `cursorcloud`, `-c`/`cursorcloud_cmd` is the URL opener that `run` uses. `Check` therefore resolves a custom opener with `spi.LookPathForCheck` and fails as `not_found` naming it, then probes the API. The guide should say what `-c` means for a provider with no binary.

## 19. Global enumeration with a per-project store (impl)

`ListAllAgentChatSessions` takes no project and assumes one global native store. The plan puts the mirror inside each project by default, so reindex sees only the mirror under the current working directory, plus any shared `cursorcloud_mirror_dir`, unless the user configures a shared location. This is a consequence of choosing a project-local store and is documented in the format doc. The guide could note that a provider whose store is per-project can enumerate only the store it can locate.

## 20. Path hints from a remote workspace (impl)

The guide covers recorded paths from another OS but not from another machine with a different root. Every Cursor Cloud tool path is under the VM checkout `/workspace`. The provider rewrites that prefix onto the local project before `spi.NormalizePath`, so hints become project-relative like every other provider's, and it renders paths relative to `/workspace`. Proposed: "If the agent runs in a remote checkout with a fixed root, map that root onto the local project for hints and rendering. Never treat it as a local path."

## 21. Per-save feedback during `run` is keyed to IDE ids (impl)

"IDE providers only: the per-save line during `run` … keyed to the registry id in `main.go`". The real criterion is "the provider does not own the terminal", which also covers a hosted agent followed from a browser. `cursorcloud` was added to that branch. Proposed: reword to "Providers whose `run` does not hand the terminal to an agent (IDEs, hosted agents)".

## 22. `tools.txt` placement (impl)

The sweep test reads section 1 of `examples/tools.txt` so that the expected-type table cannot drift from the inventory. The guide says examples are review artifacts and that `testdata/` holds what tests consume. A test-consumed `tools.txt` therefore arguably belongs in `testdata/`, but every other provider keeps it with the review artifacts. Proposed: state where a test-consumed inventory lives.

## 23. Mirror and git (impl, resolves 13 provisionally)

The implementation writes `.specstory/cursorcloud/.gitignore` containing `*` when the mirror is project-local. The mirror holds unredacted transcripts, and cloud tool output can include environment dumps. A shared mirror location gets no `.gitignore`. This is a reversible default chosen to avoid committing secrets; Sean's decision on entry 13 can change it to documentation-only.

The installed `golangci-lint` 2.13.2 cannot read Go 1.27.2 export data ("export data version 5 is greater than maximum supported version 4"), even when rebuilt with the local toolchain. v2.14.0 works and reports 0 issues. // liveSnapshot copies the attached-run set; callers hold w.mu.
func (w *cloudWatcher) liveSnapshot() map[string]bool {
	return maps.Clone(w.live)
}

// attachRunning starts a follower for every unfinished run in this project's
// mirror that has none, up to maxLiveStreams.
func (w *cloudWatcher) attachRunning() {
	for _, snap := range w.mirror.matchingSnapshots(w.origin) {
		for _, run := range snap.runs {
			if run.run.isTerminal() {
				continue
			}
			w.mu.Lock()
			attach := !w.live[run.run.ID] && len(w.live) < maxLiveStreams && w.ctx.Err() == nil
			if attach {
				w.live[run.run.ID] = true
			}
			w.mu.Unlock()
			if !attach {
				continue
			}
			agentID, runID := snap.agent.ID, run.run.ID
			slog.Info("WatchAgent: following live run", "agentId", agentID, "runId", runID)
			w.workers.Go(func() {
				w.followRun(agentID, runID)
				w.mu.Lock()
				delete(w.live, runID)
				w.mu.Unlock()
			})
		}
	}
}

_**Agent (claude-fable-5-1 2026-10-13 21:29:23Z)**_

Two answers, and a correction to what I told you about the third item.

**2. Why "cosmetic"**

The line in the config template is commented out, and the comment beside it correctly says the default is the system URL opener. When the setting is absent, the code picks `open` on macOS, `xdg-open` on Linux and `rundll32` on Windows, so no user is affected unless they uncomment the example verbatim on Linux or Windows. On Linux that would run a program called `open`, which on several distros is an alias for `openvt` and does something unrelated. So it is a documentation defect that only bites a user who copies the example without reading it, not a runtime defect. "Cosmetic" undersold that. Every other `*_cmd` example in the template is a cross-platform binary name, so this one is also inconsistent with its neighbours. The fix is to change the comment to name the per-OS defaults and drop the macOS-only example value. I recommend doing that.

**3. Transport errors**

A transport error is anything that makes the HTTP call fail before a status code arrives: DNS lookup failure, connection refused, a TCP reset, a TLS handshake failure, the 30 second request timeout, Wi-Fi or VPN dropping, or the server closing the socket mid-body. In the client's request loop these are returned to the caller at once, while a 429 or 5xx gets up to three retries with backoff.

I misstated what happens next. There are two paths:

- The live SSE follower in `watch` and `run` already handles this. On a dropped stream it reconnects with exponential backoff, resumes from the last event id, and dedupes repeats. That is the case that matters most, because a run can stream for many minutes.
- The short JSON calls (list agents, list runs, conversation, usage) are the ones not retried. In `sync`, a failed agent list falls back to the mirror and a failed refresh of one agent is logged and the others continue. Because `agent.json` is written last, the failed agent is refreshed on the next sync. In `watch`, the same failure is logged and retried at the next 60 second poll.

Why I called it defensible: nothing is lost or corrupted, every caller already has an outer retry, Go's HTTP transport already retries a GET once when a kept-alive connection turns out to be dead, and the common transport failures (offline, DNS, VPN) are not fixed by a few seconds of backoff. The counterargument is that a single reset during a 30-agent sync leaves one agent stale until the next run, and the backoff machinery is already there, so extending it to transport errors is a handful of lines. The one thing to guard is never retrying when the context itself is cancelled or timed out.

Options: leave it as is, or retry transport errors with the same backoff as 5xx, skipping context cancellation. I lean toward the retry since it is cheap and makes `sync` finish clean on a flaky connection, but it is a nice-to-have, not a bug.

Items 1, 4 and 5 are noted. I'll make neither change until you say which way you want to go on 2 and 3.

// Network constants. The request interval keeps every caller inside the
// documented 20-requests-per-minute limit of the Cloud Agents API; the API
// returns no rate-limit headers to pace against, so the client paces itself.
const (
	defaultAPIBaseURL = "https://api.cursor.com"
	requestInterval   = 3 * time.Second
	jsonTimeout       = 30 * time.Second
	maxRetries        = 4
	maxBackoff        = 60 * time.Second
	initialBackoff    = 5 * time.Second
	// listPageSize is the API's maximum page size for GET /v1/agents.
	listPageSize = 100
)

// apiBaseURL is a variable so tests can point the client at an httptest server.
var apiBaseURL = defaultAPIBaseURL

// streamIdleTimeout bounds how long a stream read may see no bytes before the
// connection is treated as dead. The live stream sends a heartbeat event while
// the agent is quiet, so 90 seconds of silence means the connection is gone.
// A variable so tests can shorten it.
var streamIdleTimeout = 90 * time.Second

func TestClientRetriesThrottledRequests(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name       string
		status     int
		retryAfter string
		wantDelay  time.Duration
	}{
		{"429 with Retry-After seconds", http.StatusTooManyRequests, "7", 7 * time.Second},
		{"429 without Retry-After backs off", http.StatusTooManyRequests, "", initialBackoff},
		{"503 retried", http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "", initialBackoff},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			calls := 0
			server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
				calls++
				if calls == 1 {
					if tt.retryAfter != "" {
						w.Header().Set("Retry-After", tt.retryAfter)
					}
					writeAPIError(w, tt.status, "rate_limited", "slow down")
					return
				}
				_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"apiKeyName":"k"}`))
			}))
			defer server.Close()

			clock := &fakeClock{now: time.Unix(1_800_000_000, 0)}
			c := newAPIClient("test-key")
			c.baseURL = server.URL
			c.limiter = &rateLimiter{interval: 0, now: clock.Now, sleep: clock.Sleep}

			me, err := c.me(context.Background())
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("me: %v", err)
			}
			if me.APIKeyName != "k" || calls != 2 {
				t.Errorf("got key %q after %d calls, want k after 2", me.APIKeyName, calls)
			}
			if len(clock.slept) != 1 || clock.slept[0] != tt.wantDelay {
				t.Errorf("slept %v, want [%v]", clock.slept, tt.wantDelay)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestClientGivesUpAfterMaxRetries(t *testing.T) {
	calls := 0
	server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		calls++

	}
	if calls != maxRetries+1 {
		t.Errorf("calls = %d, want %d", calls, maxRetries+1)
	}
}

		// Skip prose comment lines that happen to contain = (e.g. examples in parentheses)
		isSection := strings.HasPrefix(stripped, "[")
		isKeyValue := strings.Contains(stripped, " = ") && !strings.Contains(stripped, "(")
		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") && !isSection && !isKeyValue {
			continue
		}
		uncommented.WriteString(stripped)
'''
new = '''// TestDefaultConfigTemplateParsesWhenUncommented verifies the default config
// template is valid TOML when all comment prefixes are removed. This guards
// against template syntax rot. We process the template first to strip markers.
// A key the template lists more than once in a section (alternative values,
// such as one URL opener per operating system) is kept only the first time,
// because uncommenting every alternative would be a duplicate-key error that
// no real user would write.
func TestDefaultConfigTemplateParsesWhenUncommented(t *testing.T) {
	// Process template to strip {u ...} / {p ...} markers before uncommenting
	processed := processTemplate(defaultConfigTemplate, "user")

	var uncommented strings.Builder
	seenKeys := map[string]bool{}
	for line := range strings.SplitSeq(processed, "\\n") {
		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
		// Skip blank lines
		if trimmed == "" {
			continue
		}
		// Strip leading "# " to inspect the content
		stripped := strings.TrimPrefix(trimmed, "# ")
		// Keep section headers like [logging] and key = value lines
		// A TOML key-value line starts with a word character before the =
		// Skip prose comment lines that happen to contain = (e.g. examples in parentheses)
		isSection := strings.HasPrefix(stripped, "[")
		isKeyValue := strings.Contains(stripped, " = ") && !strings.Contains(stripped, "(")
		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") && !isSection && !isKeyValue {
			continue
		}
		if isSection {
			seenKeys = map[string]bool{}
		}
		if isKeyValue {
			key, _, _ := strings.Cut(stripped, " = ")
			if seenKeys[key] {
				continue
			}
			seenKeys[key] = true
		}
		uncommented.WriteString(stripped)
'''
assert s.count(old) == 1
p.write_text(s.replace(old, new))
print("ok")
EOF

_**Agent (claude-fable-5-1 2026-10-13 21:34:58Z)**_

Both items are done and verified. Nothing is committed.

**Config template, item 2**

The `cursorcloud_cmd` block in the template and in the README now reads:

```toml
# Cursor Cloud Agent: command used by specstory run cursorcloud to open
# https://cursor.com/agents. The default is the system URL opener for your OS,
# shown below; set it to open a specific browser instead.
# cursorcloud_cmd = "open"                                  # macOS default
# cursorcloud_cmd = "xdg-open"                              # Linux default
# cursorcloud_cmd = "rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler"  # Windows default
```

That exposed one test, which uncomments every example line in the template and parses the result as TOML. Three lines with the same key became a duplicate-key error. I taught the test to keep only the first occurrence of a repeated key within a section, with a comment explaining why. It still catches syntax rot in every other line.

**Transport retries, item 3**

In the API client's request loop, a failed `httpClient.Do` call now takes the same exponential backoff as a 5xx, up to the same retry cap, and shares the process-wide rate limiter hold so other callers also pause. A cancelled or timed-out context returns at once. Two tests cover this: one where the server hijacks and closes the socket on the first attempt and the second attempt succeeds after one backoff, and one where a pre-cancelled context sends no request and sleeps nowhere. The format doc and the plan now say transport errors are retried.

**Verification**

- gofmt clean, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test ./...` passes, Windows cross-build passes.
- `golangci-lint run` with your upgraded 2.14.0 reports zero issues.

specstory-cli/docs/PROVIDER-GUIDE-FEEDBACK.md:158:Resume had the same blind spot: it loaded the source with `GetAgentChatSession(OriginCwd or the current directory)`. That lookup is scoped to the current directory's project, so a cloud session picked from the all-projects browser, or by `--session` from another directory, was "not found". Per Sean's decision, the resume plan now carries the index row's `native_path`, and `loadResumeSource` reads the source through `spi.PathSessionReader` when the row has no `OriginCwd`. That is the same by-path preference reindex uses. Verified: `resume claude --session bc-cac9a149-…` run from a directory with no git origin reconstructs the cloud session, and Claude Code opens with its history. Proposed guide note: "A provider whose sessions carry no cwd should implement `spi.PathSessionReader`; reindex and resume rely on it."
specstory-cli/docs/PROVIDER-GUIDE-FEEDBACK.md:162:`pkg/cmd/session_uri.go` validated session ids against a UUID pattern, which rejected `specstory resume --session bc-<uuid>` and cloud permalinks to cloud agent sessions. Per Sean's decision, the pattern now accepts an optional `bc-` prefix in all three forms (bare, `specstory://`, permalink), with test rows for each. Verified manually: `resume claude --session bc-a2a25972-…` reconstructs the cloud session into Claude Code. The guide never says session ids must be UUIDs, and `spi.AgentChatSession.SessionID` only says "often a UUID". Proposed: the guide should say a provider whose ids are not UUIDs extends that pattern, or the pattern should be generalized to the id shapes providers use.

**Commit message**

```text
feat(cli): add Cursor Cloud Agent provider

Cloud agents keep their transcripts only in Cursor's backend, so no local
provider could see them. The new cursorcloud provider reads the Cloud
Agents API, mirrors each agent under .specstory/cursorcloud/ and renders
one history per agent, with one exchange per run. watch and run poll the
API rather than fsnotify, and run opens the cloud dashboard.

Sessions carry a repository rather than a cwd, so GlobalSessionRef gains
OriginRepoURL and the git-origin helpers move to pkg/spi; reindex,
resume and search attribute cloud sessions by origin URL and accept
bc-prefixed session ids.

PROVIDER-GUIDE-FEEDBACK.md logs the guide gaps found while building the
first HTTP-backed provider.
```
