```text
// lastEventID returns the id of the last event that carries one.
func lastEventID(events []sseEvent) string {
	for i := len(events) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		if events[i].ID != "" {
			return events[i].ID
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// eventsWithID returns the identities of recorded events with the given id.
func eventsWithID(events []sseEvent, id string) map[string]bool {
	set := map[string]bool{}
	if id == "" {
		return set
	}
	for _, ev := range events {
		if ev.ID == id {
			set[eventKey(ev)] = true
		}
	}
	return set
}

func eventKey(ev sseEvent) string {
	data, _ := json.Marshal(ev)
	return string(data)
}

// enqueue queues an agent for delivery, coalescing repeats still waiting.
func (w *cloudWatcher) enqueue(agentID string) {
	w.mu.Lock()
	if w.pending[agentID] {
		w.mu.Unlock()
		return
	}
	w.pending[agentID] = true
	w.mu.Unlock()
	w.emitCh <- agentID
}

// emitLoop delivers sessions one at a time, in queue order, from the mirror.
func (w *cloudWatcher) emitLoop() {
	for agentID := range w.emitCh {
		w.mu.Lock()
		delete(w.pending, agentID)
		w.mu.Unlock()
		snap, err := loadAgentSnapshot(w.mirror.agentDir(agentID))
		if err != nil || snap == nil {
			slog.Warn("WatchAgent: cannot read mirrored agent", "agentId", agentID, "error", err)
			continue
		}
		session := convertSnapshot(snap, w.projectPath, w.debugRaw)
		if session == nil {
			continue
		}
		spi.DeliverSession("WatchAgent", w.callback, session)
```

```text
// localPath maps a VM path onto the local project root. The root is joined by
// shape with "/" because recorded paths are POSIX; NormalizePath accepts
// either separator.
func localPath(path, workspaceRoot string) string {
	if workspaceRoot == "" {
		return path
	}
	root := strings.TrimRight(workspaceRoot, `/\`)
	if path == vmWorkspaceRoot {
		return root
	}
	if rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(path, vmWorkspaceRoot+"/"); ok {
		return root + "/" + rest
	}
	return path
}

// displayPath shows a VM path relative to the repository.
func displayPath(path string) string {
	if path == vmWorkspaceRoot {
		return "."
	}
	if rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(path, vmWorkspaceRoot+"/"); ok {
		return rest
	}
	return path
}
```

```text
##### id=4265908030 specstory-cli/pkg/config/config.go:145
This adds a bearer credential to config files that the CLI creates with mode `0644` (`config.go:538` and `config.go:576`), including the project-level `.specstory/cli/config.toml`. On multi-user systems the key can be readable by other users, and a project config can be committed unless the repository separately ignores it. Store the key only in a permission-restricted user config/secret store (and enforce `0600` on existing files), or require the environment variable instead of advertising a project-config secret.
##### id=4265908098 specstory-cli/pkg/providers/cursorcloud/mirror.go:178
The unredacted-mirror guarantee is bypassed when this file already exists with empty or insufficient rules: the function accepts any existing `.gitignore` and proceeds to write raw transcripts that Git may track. Verify that the provider-owned file contains the required rule (or replace it atomically); if it cannot be verified or corrected, abort before writing transcript data.
##### id=4265908164 specstory-cli/pkg/providers/cursorcloud/stream_parser.go:182
The advertised block-size cap only applies to each individual line. SSE permits multiple `data:` lines, and this builder appends an unlimited number of individually valid lines, so one block can still consume unbounded memory. Track the cumulative data length and mark the block skipped once adding the separator and value would exceed `maxSSELineSize`.
##### id=4265908184 specstory-cli/pkg/config/config_test.go:914
This suppresses every duplicate key in the template, not just the three intentional OS-specific `cursorcloud_cmd` alternatives. An accidental duplicate provider setting will now be removed before TOML parsing, so the test no longer catches the syntax regression it is meant to guard. Limit the exception to `cursorcloud_cmd` and leave all other duplicates for the parser to reject.
##### id=4265908220 specstory-cli/pkg/providers/cursorcloud/api_client.go:142
The stream client has no timeout while waiting for response headers. The idle reader is installed only after `Do` returns, so a server that accepts the connection but never sends headers can hang `sync` forever because replay uses a background context. Clone the default transport and set a `ResponseHeaderTimeout`; keep the response body itself unbounded for live streams.
##### id=4265908259 specstory-cli/pkg/providers/cursorcloud/mirror.go:256
A transient conversation fetch failure is only logged, after which `agent.json` is still written with the new `updatedAt`. Future syncs then consider the agent unchanged and never retry this endpoint. If an older/new run needs the v0 fallback, that exchange can remain missing indefinitely. Return the fetch error (leaving the marker stale) so the next sync retries.
This issue also appears on line 257 of the same file.
##### id=4265908282 specstory-cli/pkg/providers/cursorcloud/watcher.go:107
`baseline` is cleared even when the initial list request fails. A transient startup failure therefore makes the next successful poll treat every pre-existing agent as a new arrival and emit all histories, contradicting the watcher's “existing sessions are not news” contract. Have `poll` report whether baseline discovery succeeded and retain baseline mode until it does (with equivalent handling for agents whose baseline refresh fails).
##### id=4265908315 specstory-cli/pkg/spi/git_origin.go:26
URI-form SSH remotes with a user, such as `ssh://git@github.com/org/repo.git`, do not normalize to the same value as Cursor's HTTPS URL. The scp branch cannot split this form, and the scheme branch leaves `git@` in the result, so these valid checkouts never match their cloud agents and hash to a different project ID. Parse scheme URLs before scp-style URLs and strip URL userinfo; update the test that currently codifies the mismatch.
```

```text
// ensureRoot creates the mirror root and, for a mirror inside the project,
// the .gitignore that keeps raw transcripts out of commits.
func (m mirror) ensureRoot(projectLocal bool) error {
	if err := os.MkdirAll(m.root, 0o755); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if !projectLocal {
		return nil
	}
	path := filepath.Join(m.root, ".gitignore")
	if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return writeFileAtomic(path, []byte(mirrorGitignore))
}

// writeFileAtomic replaces path with data via a temporary file and a rename, so
// a concurrent reader sees the old file or the new one, never a torn write.
// An unchanged file is left alone, which keeps the directory fingerprint (and
// so reindex) stable across syncs that bring nothing new.
=== refreshAgent 237-290
func (m mirror) refreshAgent(ctx context.Context, c *apiClient, record agentRecord, opts refreshOptions) error {
	agentID := record.agent.ID
	stored := m.readStoredAgent(agentID)
	changed := stored == nil || stored.UpdatedAt != record.agent.UpdatedAt

	if changed {
		runs, err := c.listRuns(ctx, agentID)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("list runs: %w", err)
		}
		for _, run := range runs {
			if err := writeFileAtomic(m.runFile(agentID, run.run.ID), run.raw); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
		if conv, err := c.conversation(ctx, agentID); err != nil {
			slog.Warn("Failed to fetch conversation", "agentId", agentID, "error", err)
		} else if err := writeFileAtomic(filepath.Join(m.agentDir(agentID), "conversation.json"), conv); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if usage, err := c.usage(ctx, agentID); err != nil {
			slog.Warn("Failed to fetch usage", "agentId", agentID, "error", err)
		} else if err := writeFileAtomic(filepath.Join(m.agentDir(agentID), "usage.json"), usage); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}

	if err := m.fetchMissingStreams(ctx, c, agentID, opts); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if changed {
		return writeFileAtomic(m.agentFile(agentID), record.raw)
	}
	return nil
}
```

```text
47:Cursor Cloud Agents run in Cursor's backend, and their conversations are never written to your machine. The `cursorcloud` provider reads them from the [Cloud Agents API](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints) with your Cursor API key (create one at https://cursor.com/dashboard/api, then set `CURSOR_API_KEY` or `cursor_api_key` under `[providers]`). Agents are matched to the current project by repository: an agent belongs to the project when one of its repositories is the project's git `origin`. The provider keeps a local mirror of what it has read in `.specstory/cursorcloud/` (it writes its own `.gitignore` there, because the mirror holds unredacted transcripts); `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` or `--user-data-dir cursorcloud:<path>` moves it. A finished run's full transcript, including tool calls and output, is available from the API for 24 hours; after that only its text remains, so sync at least daily or keep `specstory watch` running. `specstory run cursorcloud` opens https://cursor.com/agents in your browser and then watches until interrupted with `ctrl-c`. Resuming another agent's session into a cloud agent is not supported, because that would launch a new paid run; cloud sessions can be resumed into local agents.
```

```bash
// gitignoreExcludesAll reports whether a .gitignore carries the bare "*" rule
// the mirror relies on. A file that exists without it (edited, truncated) would
// let git track raw transcripts, so ensureRoot rewrites it rather than trusting
// its presence.
func gitignoreExcludesAll(content []byte) bool {
	for _, line := range strings.Split(string(content), "\\n") {

		}
	}
	return false

'''// permanentAPIError reports a 4xx other than 429: the API refused the request
// itself, so repeating it with the same inputs cannot succeed. Every other
// failure (5xx, throttling, transport) may pass on a later attempt.
func permanentAPIError(err error) bool {
	var ae *apiError
	return errors.As(err, &ae) && ae.Status >= 400 && ae.Status < 500 && ae.Status != http.StatusTooManyRequests
}

// timeout; stream calls cannot (a live run streams for minutes), so they rely
// on the idle deadline in openStream for the body and on streamTransport for
// the headers.
func newAPIClient(key string) *apiClient {
	return &apiClient{
		key:        key,
		baseURL:    apiBaseURL,
		jsonHTTP:   &http.Client{Timeout: jsonTimeout},
		streamHTTP: &http.Client{Transport: streamTransport()},
		limiter:    sharedLimiter,
	}
}

// streamTransport is the default transport with a response-header deadline. The
// idle reader only guards the body after Do returns, so without this a server
// that accepts the connection and never answers would hang a replay forever.
func streamTransport() *http.Transport {
	tr := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport).Clone()
	tr.ResponseHeaderTimeout = jsonTimeout
	return tr
}
```

```bash
func TestEnsureRootRepairsGitignore(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tt := range []struct {
		name     string
		existing string
		wantKept bool
	}{
		{"missing file is written", "", false},
		{"empty file is rewritten", "# nothing ignored\\n", false},

				if err := os.MkdirAll(m.root, 0o755); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(tt.existing), 0o644); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}

			got, err := os.ReadFile(path)

			}
			if tt.wantKept && string(got) != tt.existing {
				t.Errorf("rewrote a sufficient .gitignore: %q", got)
			}
			if !gitignoreExcludesAll(got) {
				t.Errorf(".gitignore = %q, want the * rule", got)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

**CI: the Windows failures**

Two of the three come from one cause. The repo has no `.gitattributes`, and Git for Windows on the runner converts text files to CRLF at checkout. The golden JSON then differs byte for byte, and the live-stream test splits its SSE fixture on blank lines that are no longer `\n\n`. Linux and macOS never see this. The SSE reader itself already tolerates CRLF, so production is unaffected.

- **Recommended:** add a repo-root `.gitattributes` with `specstory-cli/pkg/providers/*/testdata/** -text`. Fixtures are raw captures and git should never rewrite them. This is a new file, so I need your yes.
- Alternative: normalize CRLF inside the two tests. No new file, but every future byte-exact fixture needs the same workaround.

The third failure, the custom-opener test, is fixed: the command splitter treats backslashes as escapes, so the assertion now checks the basename, as OpenCode's does.

**CodeQL** is fixed by renaming the identity field to `KeyLabel`, which is what it holds. The key itself never reaches a log.

**Copilot: seven of eight accepted and fixed locally, with tests**

1. API key in a 0644 config file: new config files are now created 0600, and the template says to prefer the env var or the user config. Existing files are not chmodded. Reverse this if you'd rather not touch file modes.
2. Mirror `.gitignore` is now verified to contain `*` and rewritten if not.
3. SSE block cap now applies to the total of all data lines.
4. The template test now allows a repeat only for `cursorcloud_cmd` and fails on any other duplicate.
5. Stream client has a 30 second response-header timeout.
6. A transient conversation or usage failure now fails the refresh so the next sync retries. A permanent 4xx still logs and mirrors the agent, so an agent whose endpoint refuses cannot vanish forever.
7. A failed baseline listing keeps the watcher in baseline mode until a listing succeeds.

**The eighth is yours:** `ssh://git@github.com/org/repo.git` normalizes to a value that keeps `git@`, so such remotes never match their cloud agents. Copilot is right, but this helper was moved unchanged from `pkg/utils` and its output is hashed into the persisted `git_id`. Fixing it changes the project identity for every user with a user-prefixed `ssh://` remote and splits their cloud history. I recommend closing it with a comment and filing a follow-up issue rather than changing persisted ids in a provider PR.

```bash
## Problem

`spi.NormalizeGitRemoteURL` (moved unchanged from `pkg/utils` in #357) handles `git@github.com:org/repo.git` and `https://github.com/org/repo.git`, but a URI-form SSH remote with a user, such as `ssh://git@github.com/org/repo.git`, keeps `git@` in the normalized value. Such checkouts hash to a different `git_id` than an HTTPS clone of the same repository, and the `cursorcloud` provider cannot match them to their cloud agents (whose `repos[].url` is HTTPS).

Raised by Copilot on #357: https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/357#discussion_r-git-origin

## Why it was not fixed in #357

The normalized value is hashed into the persisted `git_id`. Changing it in a provider PR would silently change the project identity for every user with a user-prefixed `ssh://` remote and split their existing cloud history. The fix needs its own migration story (re-key or alias the old id) rather than a drive-by change.

## Suggested fix

Strip the `user@` prefix in the scheme branch (`ssh://`, `git+ssh://`) before building `host/path`, add table cases for `ssh://git@github.com/org/repo.git`, `ssh://git@github.com:22/org/repo.git` and `git+ssh://`, and decide how existing `git_id` values for those remotes migrate.
EOF
```

```text
## Summary

Cursor Cloud Agents keep their transcripts only in Cursor's backend, so no local provider could see them and users got no histories. This adds `cursorcloud`, the first provider whose native store is a remote HTTP API. It reads the Cloud Agents API with the user's key, mirrors each agent under `.specstory/cursorcloud/` (ignored by its own `.gitignore`, because the mirror is unredacted), and renders one history per agent with one exchange per run. `watch` and `run` poll the API and follow live run streams over SSE; `run` opens cursor.com/agents and then watches.

Research behind the design: `specstory-cli/docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md`. Format and lifecycle: `pkg/providers/cursorcloud/CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md`.

## Built and tested against

- Cloud Agents API `1.0.0` (v1 public beta plus legacy v0), live on 2026-10-13.
- Manually exercised on macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6.0) against real cloud agents in a throwaway repository. Linux and Windows were cross-compiled and vetted (`GOOS=windows` build and vet pass) but not exercised manually.

## Manual test table rows run

- `check cursorcloud`: location reported, no version line (the API exposes none); `-c` with a bad path fails naming it; missing or rejected key gives guidance.
- `sync`, `sync cursorcloud`, `sync -s <id>`, `sync -s <id> --print`: one file per agent; a second sync changes no bytes and rewrites no mirror files.
- `sync --debug-raw --log --debug`: `agent.json`, `conversation.json`, `usage.json` and one file per run under `.specstory/debug/<id>/`.
- `watch cursorcloud`: existing agents left alone at startup; live runs followed and saved as they stream.
- `run cursorcloud`: opens the dashboard and behaves as `watch` (hosted-agent substitution).
- `resume cursorcloud` of its own session: opens the agent's page and watches. Resume of another agent's session into `cursorcloud` refuses with a clear message.
- `resume claude --session bc-…`: the cloud session reconstructs into Claude Code with its history, from a directory with no git origin.
- `list`, `search`, `reindex`: cloud sessions attributed to the right project by origin URL with full searchable bodies.

## Enumeration artifacts and audit

Under `pkg/providers/cursorcloud/`: `testdata/tools.txt` (recorded and model-facing names with the mapping), `examples/versions.txt`, `examples/TOOL-AUDIT.md` (every rendered block graded, failures included), and the synced histories under `examples/history/`. Fixtures in `testdata/` are real captures, scrubbed of account identifiers.

## SPI and shared-code changes

- `GlobalSessionRef.OriginRepoURL`: a hosted agent records a repository, never a directory. Reindex resolves the project from it with the same `git_id` normalization, parses bodies through `spi.PathSessionReader`, and resume reads such sessions by path. Without this, cloud sessions were indexed metadata-only under `unknown`.
- Git-origin helpers moved from `pkg/utils` to `pkg/spi` (`GitOriginURL`, `NormalizeGitRemoteURL`, `FindGitRoot`) with `pkg/utils` delegating, so providers use the exact normalization the CLI hashes.
- `pkg/cmd/session_uri.go` accepts `bc-`-prefixed session ids.
- Config: `cursor_api_key` and `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` settings reach the provider through `cmd.ApplyProviderSettings`; the config wiring test gained an allowlist for non-command settings.
- `NEW-PROVIDER-GUIDE.md` now covers hosted agents: remote stores, polling watchers with the acceptance-case mapping, credential-based `Check`, provider settings, remote checkout paths, provider-owned stores under `.specstory/`, and the rules this provider surfaced. Every guide gap found during the build was reviewed one by one and folded in.

## Known limitations

- Full transcripts are retained by Cursor for 24 hours after a run; after that only the v0 conversation text remains, so histories of older runs are text only. Sync daily or keep `watch` running.
- `Model` is empty and per-message `Usage` is nil because the API exposes neither; both stay in `RawData`.
- Resume into `cursorcloud` from another agent is unsupported: creating a cloud conversation launches a paid run.
- The default mirror is per project, so `reindex` sees the current project's mirror plus any configured shared `cursorcloud_mirror_dir`.
- SpecStory Cloud needs an exact agent-name entry for `cursorcloud` on the sync side (`specstory-sync`), handled separately.

## Review

The code was reviewed file by file against the provider guide during the build. The `/code-review` pass was not run before opening this PR; `/pr-review` is the next step.
```

```text
=== PRRT_kwDONdK4HM6sKOBw specstory-cli/pkg/config/config.go lines 540-540 r4266691575
This protects only newly created configs. Existing user configs generated by earlier releases are already mode 0644, and `os.WriteFile(..., 0600)` also preserves permissions when `SaveResumePrefs` or `SaveSkillsPrefs` rewrites an existing file. Users adding the new `cursor_api_key` to an upgraded installation can therefore expose it to other local users. Tighten the existing user config's permissions during load (and test the upgrade case), not only at creation.

=== PRRT_kwDONdK4HM6sKOCR specstory-cli/pkg/providers/cursorcloud/path_utils.go lines 57-62 r4266691620
Every configured path is marked non-project-local, even when it points inside the project. Setting `cursorcloud_mirror_dir = ".specstory/cursorcloud"` (the documented default) or an in-project `--user-data-dir` therefore disables the protective `.gitignore` while still writing unredacted transcripts there. Determine locality from the resolved path versus `projectPath`, or write the mirror `.gitignore` for configured locations as well.

=== PRRT_kwDONdK4HM6sKOCc specstory-cli/pkg/providers/cursorcloud/watcher.go lines 155-160 r4266691637
A transient refresh failure during the baseline is never retried. Recording this `updatedAt` in `seen` makes the equality check at lines 143–145 skip the agent on every later poll, so its mirror stays incomplete and a running stream may never be attached until Cursor changes `updatedAt` again. Track “known at startup” separately from “successfully refreshed,” so retries remain silent but continue until the mirror is populated.
```

```text
=== watcher.go 120-200
// updatedAt it listed, not what the agent became. The result reports whether
// the listing succeeded: pollLoop keeps the baseline open until it has, so a
// failed first poll cannot turn every pre-existing agent into news.
func (w *cloudWatcher) poll(baseline bool) bool {
	agents, err := w.client.listAgents(w.ctx, maxPollPages)
	if err != nil {
		if w.ctx.Err() == nil {
			slog.Warn("WatchAgent: listing cloud agents failed; retrying next poll", "error", err)
		}
		return false
	}
	for _, record := range agents {
		if w.ctx.Err() != nil {
			return false
		}
		agent := record.agent
		if !agentMatchesOrigin(agent, w.origin) {
			continue
		}
		w.mu.Lock()
		prev, known := w.seen[agent.ID]
		skip := w.liveSnapshot()
		w.mu.Unlock()
		if known && prev == agent.UpdatedAt {
			continue
		}

		if err := w.mirror.ensureRoot(w.projectLocal); err != nil {
			slog.Error("WatchAgent: cannot create mirror", "path", w.mirror.root, "error", err)
			return false
		}
		if err := w.mirror.refreshAgent(w.ctx, w.client, record, refreshOptions{skipStreams: skip, now: time.Now()}); err != nil {
			if w.ctx.Err() == nil {
				slog.Error("WatchAgent: refreshing cloud agent failed", "agentId", agent.ID, "error", err)
			}
			if baseline {
				// The agent existed before the watcher started, so it is part
				// of the baseline even though its mirror could not be filled;
				// a later successful refresh of the same updatedAt is not news.
				w.mu.Lock()
				w.seen[agent.ID] = agent.UpdatedAt
				w.mu.Unlock()
			}
			continue
		}
		w.mu.Lock()
		w.seen[agent.ID] = agent.UpdatedAt
		w.mu.Unlock()
		if baseline {
			slog.Debug("WatchAgent: baseline", "agentId", agent.ID, "updatedAt", agent.UpdatedAt)
		} else {
			slog.Info("WatchAgent: cloud agent updated", "agentId", agent.ID, "updatedAt", agent.UpdatedAt)
			w.enqueue(agent.ID)
		}
	}
	w.attachRunning()
	return true
}

// liveSnapshot copies the attached-run set; callers hold w.mu.
func (w *cloudWatcher) liveSnapshot() map[string]bool {
	return maps.Clone(w.live)
}

// attachRunning starts a follower for every unfinished run in this project's
// mirror that has none, up to maxLiveStreams.
func (w *cloudWatcher) attachRunning() {
	for _, snap := range w.mirror.matchingSnapshots(w.origin) {
		for _, run := range snap.runs {
			if run.run.isTerminal() {
				continue
			}
			w.mu.Lock()
			attach := !w.live[run.run.ID] && len(w.live) < maxLiveStreams && w.ctx.Err() == nil
			if attach {
				w.live[run.run.ID] = true
			}
			w.mu.Unlock()
			if !attach {
				continue
			}
```

```text
package cursorcloud

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"log/slog"
	"maps"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"

// Watcher tuning. A remote store has no filesystem events, so a poll of the
// agent list is the change signal. Variables so tests can run in milliseconds.
var (
	// pollInterval keeps the poll (one request per page) far inside the
	// 20-requests-per-minute budget, leaving room for refreshes and streams.
	pollInterval = 60 * time.Second
	// emitDebounce coalesces a burst of stream events into one save; the
	// burst's last event is usually the completed text.
	emitDebounce = 2 * time.Second
	// reconnectDelay is the first wait before reattaching a dropped stream.
	reconnectDelay = 5 * time.Second
)

const (
	// maxLiveStreams bounds concurrent stream connections; each holds a
	// connection open for the length of a run.
	maxLiveStreams = 4
	// maxStreamReconnects bounds reattaching one dropped stream.
	maxStreamReconnects = 5
	// maxPollPages bounds the agents scanned per poll. The list is newest
	// first, so 300 agents covers any agent a person is actively running.
	maxPollPages = 3
)

// cloudWatcher polls the agent list and follows running runs live.
type cloudWatcher struct {
	origin       string
	projectPath  string
	mirror       mirror
	projectLocal bool
	client       *apiClient
	debugRaw     bool
	callback     func(*spi.AgentChatSession)

	ctx       context.Context
	cancel    context.CancelFunc
	startedAt time.Time

	mu      sync.Mutex
	seen    map[string]string // agent id -> updatedAt last acted on
	live    map[string]bool   // run ids with an attached stream
	pending map[string]bool   // agent ids queued for emission
	emitCh  chan string

	workers  sync.WaitGroup // poll loop and stream followers
	emitter  sync.WaitGroup // the single delivery worker
	stopOnce sync.Once
}

func newCloudWatcher(projectPath, origin string, client *apiClient, debugRaw bool, callback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) *cloudWatcher {
	m, projectLocal := mirrorFor(projectPath)
	return &cloudWatcher{
		origin:       origin,
		projectPath:  projectPath,
		mirror:       m,
		projectLocal: projectLocal,
		client:       client,
		debugRaw:     debugRaw,
		callback:     callback,
		seen:         map[string]string{},
		live:         map[string]bool{},
		pending:      map[string]bool{},
	}
}

// start begins polling. The context is created per start so a stopped
// watcher can be started again.
func (w *cloudWatcher) start(parent context.Context) {
	w.ctx, w.cancel = context.WithCancel(parent)
	w.startedAt = time.Now()
	w.emitCh = make(chan string, 64)
	w.stopOnce = sync.Once{}
	w.emitter.Go(w.emitLoop)
	w.workers.Go(w.pollLoop)
}

// stop cancels polling and streams, waits for every follower to write its
// final events and queue any update not yet delivered, then drains delivery.
func (w *cloudWatcher) stop() {
	w.stopOnce.Do(func() {
		w.cancel()
		w.workers.Wait()
		close(w.emitCh)
		w.emitter.Wait()
	})
}

// pollLoop runs the baseline poll, then polls every pollInterval.
func (w *cloudWatcher) pollLoop() {
	baseline := true
	for {
		if w.poll(baseline) {
			baseline = false
		}
		if sleepContext(w.ctx, pollInterval) != nil {
			return
		}
	}
}

func Load(cliOverrides *CLIOverrides) (*Config, error) {
	cfg := &Config{}

	// Load user-level config first (lowest priority)
	userConfigPath := getUserConfigPath()
	if userConfigPath != "" {
		if err := loadTOMLFile(userConfigPath, cfg); err != nil {
			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
				slog.Debug("No user-level config file found", "path", userConfigPath)
				ensureDefaultUserConfig(userConfigPath)
			} else {
				// Parse error or permission denied - return error to caller
				return cfg, fmt.Errorf("failed to load user config %s: %w", userConfigPath, err)
			}
		} else {
			slog.Debug("Loaded user-level config", "path", userConfigPath)
		}
	}

	// Load local project config (overwrites user-level)
	localConfigPath := getLocalConfigPath()
	// --config-dir relocates the project-level config; without this, a config
	// created there via EnsureDefaultProjectConfig would never be read back.
	if cliOverrides != nil && cliOverrides.ConfigDir != "" {
		localConfigPath = filepath.Join(cliOverrides.ConfigDir, ConfigFileName)
	}
	if localConfigPath != "" {
		if err := loadTOMLFile(localConfigPath, cfg); err != nil {
			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
				slog.Debug("No local project config file found", "path", localConfigPath)
			} else {
				// Parse error or permission denied - return error to caller
				return cfg, fmt.Errorf("failed to load project config %s: %w", localConfigPath, err)
			}
		} else {
			slog.Debug("Loaded local project config", "path", localConfigPath)
		}
	}

	// Apply CLI flag overrides (highest priority for most settings)
	if cliOverrides != nil {
		applyCLIOverrides(cfg, cliOverrides)
	}

	// Apply OTel environment variables (highest priority for telemetry only)
	applyTelemetryEnvOverrides(cfg)

	return cfg, nil
}

// GetUserConfigPath returns the path to ~/.specstory/cli/config.toml
func GetUserConfigPath() string {
	return getUserConfigPath()
}

// GetLocalConfigPath returns the path to .specstory/cli/config.toml in the current directory
func GetLocalConfigPath() string {
	return getLocalConfigPath()
}

// getUserConfigPath returns the path to ~/.specstory/cli/config.toml
func getUserConfigPath() string {
	home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
	if err != nil {
		slog.Debug("Could not determine home directory", "error", err)
		return ""
	}
	return filepath.Join(home, SpecStoryDir, CLIDir, ConfigFileName)
}

// loadTOMLFile reads a TOML file and decodes it into the config struct.
// Fields are merged (later calls overwrite earlier values).
func loadTOMLFile(path string, cfg *Config) error {
	_, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, cfg)
	return err
}

// applyTelemetryEnvOverrides applies OTel environment variable overrides.
// Per OTel conventions, these take highest priority for telemetry settings.
func applyTelemetryEnvOverrides(cfg *Config) {
	if endpoint := os.Getenv("OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT"); endpoint != "" {
		cfg.Telemetry.Endpoint = endpoint
	}

	if serviceName := os.Getenv("OTEL_SERVICE_NAME"); serviceName != "" {
		cfg.Telemetry.ServiceName = serviceName
	}

	// Note: OTEL_SDK_DISABLED is handled in IsTelemetryEnabled() rather than
	// stored in the config struct, since there is no Enabled field — telemetry
	// is enabled when an endpoint is configured.
}

// ConfigValidationResult holds the result of validating a config file.
type ConfigValidationResult struct {
	Path        string   // Path to the config file
	Exists      bool     // Whether the file exists
	ValidTOML   bool     // Whether the file is valid TOML
	ParseError  string   // TOML parse error message, if any
	UnknownKeys []string // Keys in the file that don't map to any known config field
}

// ValidateConfigFile checks a config file for validity and schema conformance.
// Returns a result indicating whether the file exists, is valid TOML, and
// whether it contains any unknown sections or properties.
func ValidateConfigFile(path string) ConfigValidationResult {
	result := ConfigValidationResult{Path: path}

	// Check if file exists
	if _, err := os.Stat(path); os.IsNotExist(err) {
		return result
	}
	result.Exists = true

	// Try to decode and check for unknown keys
	var cfg Config
	md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
	if err != nil {
		result.ParseError = err.Error()
		return result
	}
	result.ValidTOML = true

	// Check for keys in the TOML that didn't map to any struct field.
	// Filter out child keys when the parent section is already unknown
	// (e.g., if [bogus] is unknown, don't also report bogus.foo).
```

```text
func TestWatcherBaselineSurvivesListFailure(t *testing.T) {
	useSettings(t, "test-key")
	fastWatcher(t)
	f := newFakeAPI(t)
	fx := loadFixture(t, "fixture-run")
	f.agents = append(f.agents, fx.agent.raw)
	f.runs[fx.agent.agent.ID] = []json.RawMessage{fx.runs[0].raw}
	f.convs[fx.agent.agent.ID] = fx.conversation
	f.usages[fx.agent.agent.ID] = fx.usage
	f.streams = fx.streams
	// 403 is not retried by the client, so the poll itself sees the failure.
	f.listStatus = http.StatusForbidden

	w, got := startWatcher(t)
	waitFor(t, "two refused listings", func() bool { return f.count("/v1/agents") >= 2 })
	f.mu.Lock()
	f.listStatus = 0
	f.mu.Unlock()
	waitFor(t, "the agent to be mirrored", func() bool {
		snap, _ := loadAgentSnapshot(w.mirror.agentDir(fx.agent.agent.ID))
		return snap != nil
	})
	waitFor(t, "one more poll", func() bool { return f.count("/v1/agents") >= 5 })
	w.stop()

	if n := len(got.all()); n != 0 {
		t.Errorf("emitted %d sessions after a failed baseline, want none", n)
	}
}
```

```text
	var agent map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &agent); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	agent["updatedAt"] = updatedAt
	out, _ := json.Marshal(agent)
	return out
}
```

```text
// ensureRoot creates the mirror root and, for a mirror inside the project,
// the .gitignore that keeps raw transcripts out of commits.
func (m mirror) ensureRoot(projectLocal bool) error {
	if err := os.MkdirAll(m.root, 0o755); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if !projectLocal {
		return nil
	}
	path := filepath.Join(m.root, ".gitignore")
	if existing, err := os.ReadFile(path); err == nil && gitignoreExcludesAll(existing) {
		return nil
	}
	return writeFileAtomic(path, []byte(mirrorGitignore))
}

// gitignoreExcludesAll reports whether a .gitignore carries the bare "*" rule
// the mirror relies on. A file that exists without it (edited, truncated) would
// let git track raw transcripts, so ensureRoot rewrites it rather than trusting
// its presence.
func gitignoreExcludesAll(content []byte) bool {
```

```bash
func tightenUserConfigMode(path string) {
	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {

		return
	}
	slog.Debug("Tightened user config permissions", "path", path, "was", perm.String())

func mirrorFor(projectPath string) (mirror, bool) {
	root := userDataDirOverride
	if root == "" {

	}
	if root == "" {

// insideProject reports whether path resolves to a directory strictly below
// projectPath. The project root itself does not count: a "*" .gitignore there
// would hide the whole project from git, which is worse than an unprotected
// mirror, so that misconfiguration is left to the user.
func insideProject(path, projectPath string) bool {
	if projectPath == "" {
		return false
	}
	abs, err := filepath.Abs(path)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	rel, err := filepath.Rel(filepath.Clean(projectPath), abs)
	if err != nil || rel == "." || rel == ".." || filepath.IsAbs(rel) {
		return false
	}
	return !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))
}
```

```bash
// TestWatcherRetriesBaselineRefreshQuietly: an agent whose baseline refresh
// fails transiently is retried on later polls until its mirror is filled, and
// those retries emit nothing because the agent has not changed since startup.
func TestWatcherRetriesBaselineRefreshQuietly(t *testing.T) {
	useSettings(t, "test-key")
	fastWatcher(t)
	prev := initialBackoff
	initialBackoff = time.Millisecond
	t.Cleanup(func() { initialBackoff = prev })
	f := newFakeAPI(t)
	fx := loadFixture(t, "fixture-run")
	f.addFixture(fx)
	agentID := fx.agent.agent.ID
	convPath := "/v0/agents/" + agentID + "/conversation"
	// 503 is transient, so the refresh fails and agent.json is never written.
	f.convStatus = http.StatusServiceUnavailable

	w, got := startWatcher(t)
	waitFor(t, "two polls with a failing refresh", func() bool {
		return f.count("/v1/agents") >= 2 && f.count(convPath) >= 1
	})
	if snap, _ := loadAgentSnapshot(w.mirror.agentDir(agentID)); snap != nil {
		t.Fatal("agent mirrored although its conversation fetch kept failing")
	}
	f.mu.Lock()
	f.convStatus = 0
	f.mu.Unlock()
	waitFor(t, "the retried refresh to fill the mirror", func() bool {
		snap, _ := loadAgentSnapshot(w.mirror.agentDir(agentID))
		return snap != nil
	})
	polls := f.count("/v1/agents")
	waitFor(t, "one more poll", func() bool { return f.count("/v1/agents") > polls })
	w.stop()

	if n := len(got.all()); n != 0 {
		t.Errorf("emitted %d sessions for an unchanged baseline agent, want none", n)
	}
	w.mu.Lock()
	seenAt, ok := w.seen[agentID]
	w.mu.Unlock()
	if !ok || seenAt != fx.agent.agent.UpdatedAt {
		t.Errorf("seen[%s] = %q %v, want the listed updatedAt after the successful retry", agentID, seenAt, ok)
	}
}
```

```bash
  configs are left alone; Windows has no mode bits.
- Decide mirror locality from the resolved path, so a configured mirror
  inside the project still gets the protective .gitignore. The project
  root itself never does: a "*" there would hide the whole project.
- Track "listed at startup" apart from "refreshed" in the watcher, so an
  agent whose baseline refresh failed is retried on every poll, silently
  while unchanged, until its mirror is filled.
```

```text
<details>
<summary> Apply config permissions before parsing</summary>

`specstory-cli/​pkg/​config/​config.go:366`

Tighten the user config before parsing it. If an upgraded `0644` config contains `cursor_api_key` plus a TOML error, `loadTOMLFile` returns at line 362 and this chmod never runs, leaving the credential world-readable until the syntax is fixed.
</details>

<details>
<summary> Allow mirror-only reads without an API key</summary>

`specstory-cli/​pkg/​providers/​cursorcloud/​provider.go:150`

Check the mirror even when no API key is currently configured. `GetAgentChatSessions` explicitly supports mirror-only reads, but this gate makes `sync cursorcloud` return before reaching it after a user unsets or rotates the key, so already-mirrored histories cannot be rendered offline.
</details>

<details>
<summary> Preserve the matched repository for multi-repo agents</summary>

`specstory-cli/​pkg/​providers/​cursorcloud/​provider.go:382`

This attributes every multi-repository agent to `repos[0]`, although project matching accepts any entry in `repos`. If an agent was mirrored while the current project matched `repos[1]`, reindex assigns it to the first repository instead, so list/search/resume grouping is wrong for the project that synced it. Preserve the matched repository in the mirror or extend the index model to represent all associated repositories.
</details>

<details>
<summary> Propagate permanent API failures from the watcher</summary>

`specstory-cli/​pkg/​providers/​cursorcloud/​watcher.go:137`

Permanent API failures are retried forever. With a rejected key or Privacy Mode response, `listAgents` returns a non-retryable 4xx on every poll, but `pollLoop` never reports it to `WatchAgent`; `run cursorcloud` therefore prints that it is watching and hangs until interrupted without ever being able to save. Propagate permanent API errors out of the watcher while retaining retries for transport, 429, and 5xx failures.
</details>

<details>
<summary> Clarify creation of nonexistent mirror overrides</summary>

`specstory-cli/​README.md:119`

The fallback statement is not true for `cursorcloud`: a nonexistent mirror override is a valid new destination and `ensureRoot` creates it rather than warning and falling back. Distinguish this from the IDE provider behavior so users know their configured mirror path will be created.
</details>
</details>
```

````text
// DetectAgent reports whether this project has cloud agents: a key is
// configured, the project has a git origin, and either the mirror already
// holds an agent for that repository or the first page of the agent list
// names one.
func (p *Provider) DetectAgent(projectPath string, helpOutput bool) bool {
	key, _ := resolveAPIKey()
	origin := projectOrigin(projectPath)
	found := false
	if key != "" && origin != "" {
		m, _ := mirrorFor(projectPath)
		found = len(m.matchingSnapshots(origin)) > 0
		if !found {
			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), jsonTimeout)
			agents, err := newAPIClient(key).listAgents(ctx, 1)
			cancel()
			if err != nil {
				slog.Warn("DetectAgent: listing cloud agents failed", "error", err)
			}
			for _, record := range agents {
				if agentMatchesOrigin(record.agent, origin) {
					found = true
					break
				}
			}
		}
	}

	if helpOutput && !found {
		log.UserWarn("\nNo Cursor Cloud Agents were found for this project.\n")
		switch {
		case key == "":
			log.UserMessage("%s\n", missingKeyMessage())
		case origin == "":
			log.UserMessage("Cloud agents are matched to a project by its git origin URL, and this directory has no origin remote.\n")
			log.UserMessage("Run SpecStory from a clone of the repository the cloud agents worked on.\n\n")
		default:
			log.UserMessage("Cloud agents are matched to a project by repository URL. None of your agents worked on %s.\n", origin)
			log.UserMessage("Launch one at https://cursor.com/agents for this repository, then sync again.\n\n")
		}
	}
	return found
}

// GetAgentChatSessions refreshes the mirror for this project's agents, then
// builds every matching session from the mirror. Without a key or network it
// still returns what the mirror already holds.
func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
	origin := projectOrigin(projectPath)
	if origin == "" {
		slog.Debug("GetAgentChatSessions: project has no git origin; no cloud agents can match", "projectPath", projectPath)
		return []spi.AgentChatSession{}, nil
	}
	m, projectLocal := mirrorFor(projectPath)
	refreshProject(context.Background(), m, projectLocal, origin)

	// Progress is reported once per mirrored agent, including those that fail
	// to convert, so the bar reaches its total. An agent whose refresh failed
	// is still read from whatever the mirror held before.
	snapshots := m.matchingSnapshots(origin)
	var sessions []spi.AgentChatSession
	for i, snap := range snapshots {
		if session := convertSnapshot(snap, projectPath, debugRaw); session != nil {
			sessions = append(sessions, *session)
		}
		if progress != nil {
			progress(i+1, len(snapshots))
		}
	}
	return sessions, nil
}

=== README 105-125
With a specific session UUID:

```zsh
specstory sync -s <session-uuid>
```

### Non-default IDE install locations (`--user-data-dir`)

The `sync`, `check`, `list` and `watch` commands accept a repeatable `--user-data-dir` flag that points an IDE provider at a non-default install location — useful for portable installs and for reading a Windows-side install from WSL. It takes a `provider_id:path` pair where the path is the IDE's user-data-dir itself (the parent of the `User` directory), the same value the IDE's own `--user-data-dir` argument takes:

```zsh
specstory sync --user-data-dir cursoride:/opt/cursor/data --user-data-dir copilotide:/opt/vscode/data
```

Supported provider IDs are `cursoride`, `cursorcloud` (where the path is the location of its local API mirror), `copilotide`, `copilotide-insiders`, `copilotide-vscodium` and `copilotide-vscodium-insiders`. If the override path doesn't exist, SpecStory warns and falls back to the standard location for your OS.

### Resume & Search

SpecStory indexes every session it sees into `~/.specstory/sessions.db` so you can pick up
a past session — in the same agent or a different one — without re-reading the transcript. Two
commands share the same interactive picker:
````

```text
=== watch_agents.go 60-140

			// Wrap the callback to deduplicate and include provider ID
			wrappedCallback := func(session *spi.AgentChatSession) {
				if session == nil || session.SessionData == nil {
					return
				}

				fingerprint := fingerprintSession(session)

				// Key by provider as well as session: the map is shared across all
				// provider goroutines, and without the scope two providers emitting
				// the same session ID would suppress each other's callbacks.
				dedupKey := providerID + "/" + session.SessionID

				// Skip if the parsed content hasn't changed for this session
				mu.Lock()
				prev, seen := lastFingerprint[dedupKey]
				if seen && prev == fingerprint {
					mu.Unlock()
					slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Skipping duplicate callback",
						"providerID", providerID,
						"sessionID", session.SessionID,
						"messages", fingerprint.messages,
						"contentBytes", fingerprint.contentBytes)
					return
				}
				lastFingerprint[dedupKey] = fingerprint
				mu.Unlock()

				slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Provider callback fired",
					"providerID", providerID,
					"sessionID", session.SessionID,
					"messages", fingerprint.messages,
					"contentBytes", fingerprint.contentBytes)

				sessionCallback(providerID, session)
			}

			err := provider.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, wrappedCallback)
			if err != nil {
				// Context cancellation is expected when user presses Ctrl+C, not an error
				if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
					slog.Info("WatchProviders: Provider watcher stopped", "provider", provider.Name())
					errChan <- nil
				} else {
					slog.Error("WatchProviders: Provider watcher failed", "provider", provider.Name(), "error", err)
					errChan <- fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", provider.Name(), err)
				}
			} else {
				errChan <- nil
			}
		})
	}

	// Wait for all watchers to complete (they run until Ctrl+C)
	wg.Wait()

	// Individual watcher failures are already logged in the goroutines with
	// full context and must not kill the surviving watchers' results. But when
	// EVERY watcher failed (e.g. `specstory watch <provider>` on a provider
	// whose watch is unsupported), returning nil would print the watching
	// banner and then silently exit 0 — surface the failure instead.
	var failures []error
	for range len(providers) {
		if err := <-errChan; err != nil {
			failures = append(failures, err)
		}
	}
	if len(providers) > 0 && len(failures) == len(providers) {
		return errors.Join(failures...)
	}

	return nil
}

// sessionFingerprint summarizes the parsed content of a session for callback
// deduplication. Comparable by value.
type sessionFingerprint struct {
	messages     int    // total messages across all exchanges
	contentBytes int    // total bytes of message text, tool summaries, and pre-rendered tool markdown
	contentHash  uint64 // FNV-1a over the same content; catches edits that keep the total length identical
```

```bash
// insideProject reports whether path resolves to a directory strictly below
// projectPath. The project root itself does not count: a "*" .gitignore there
// would hide the whole project from git, which is worse than an unprotected
// mirror, so that misconfiguration is left to the user.
func insideProject(path, projectPath string) bool {
	if projectPath == "" {
		return false
	}
	abs, err := filepath.Abs(path)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	rel, err := filepath.Rel(filepath.Clean(projectPath), abs)
	if err != nil || rel == "." || rel == ".." || filepath.IsAbs(rel) {
		return false
	}
	return !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))

'''func mirrorFor(projectPath string) (mirror, bool) {
	root := userDataDirOverride
	if root == "" {
		root = configMirrorDir
	}
	if root == "" {
		return mirror{root: filepath.Join(projectPath, ".specstory", "cursorcloud")}, true
	}
	root = canonicalMirrorRoot(root)
	return mirror{root: root}, insideProject(root, projectPath)
}

// canonicalMirrorRoot resolves a configured root to an absolute path with
// symlinks evaluated. Session refs carry mirror paths as NativePath, which must
// be absolute so a resume from another directory still finds them, and the
// locality check must see where a symlink really points. The directory may not
// exist yet (ensureRoot creates it), so the nearest existing ancestor is
// resolved and the missing tail re-appended.
func canonicalMirrorRoot(path string) string {
	abs, err := filepath.Abs(path)
	if err != nil {
		return filepath.Clean(path)
	}
	tail := ""
	for dir := abs; ; {
		if _, err := os.Stat(dir); err == nil {
			return filepath.Join(spi.CanonicalizePathOrClean(dir), tail)
		}
		parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
		if parent == dir {
			return abs
		}
		tail = filepath.Join(filepath.Base(dir), tail)
		dir = parent
	}
}

// insideProject reports whether root, already canonical, lies strictly below
// projectPath. The project root itself does not count: a "*" .gitignore there
// would hide the whole project from git, which is worse than an unprotected
// mirror, so that misconfiguration is left to the user.
func insideProject(root, projectPath string) bool {
	if projectPath == "" {
		return false
	}
	rel, err := filepath.Rel(spi.CanonicalizePathOrClean(projectPath), root)
	if err != nil || rel == "." || rel == ".." || filepath.IsAbs(rel) {
		return false
	}
	return !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))
}
''')])

'''// pollLoop runs the baseline poll, then polls every pollInterval. It ends with
// the context, or when the API refuses the listing for good: a rejected key or
// an account on Privacy Mode fails every poll the same way, and polling on
// would leave `run` and `watch` claiming to watch while nothing can ever be
// saved. That error is handed to WatchAgent through fatal.
func (w *cloudWatcher) pollLoop() {
	baseline := true
	for {
		listed, err := w.poll(baseline)
		if err != nil {
			w.fatal <- err
			return
		}
		if listed {
			baseline = false

	}
}
```

```bash
cd /Users/sean/Source/SpecStory/getspecstory && export GH_TOKEN="$(gh auth token --user belucid)" && gh issue create -R specstoryai/getspecstory --title "cursorcloud: multi-repository agents are attributed to repos[0] on reindex" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

`ListAllAgentChatSessions` in `pkg/providers/cursorcloud/provider.go` sets `GlobalSessionRef.OriginRepoURL` from `agent.repos[0]`, while project matching (`agentMatchesOrigin`) accepts any entry in `repos`. For an agent that lists several repositories, reindex attributes the session to the first one even if the project that mirrored it matched a later entry, so `list`, `search` and `resume` group it under the wrong project.

Raised by Copilot on #357 (review of 2026-10-14, "previously missed" list).

## Why it was not fixed in #357

Every agent observed against the live API (2026-10-13) has exactly one repository; the Cursor dashboard launches an agent against one repository. The index model carries a single `OriginRepoURL` per session, so a real fix either records which repository matched when the agent was mirrored (which a shared `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` serving several projects makes ambiguous) or extends the index to hold several repositories per session. Both are changes to the session index, not to the provider.

## Suggested fix

Decide at the index level: either allow a `GlobalSessionRef` to carry several origin repositories and let reindex attribute the session to each matching project, or record the matched repository in the mirror's `agent.json` sidecar at refresh time and prefer it on reindex.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1
```

_**Agent (claude-fable-5-1 2026-10-14 04:55:35Z)**_

PR #357 is green and every review thread is resolved. Copilot reviewed each push and I worked three rounds; it has posted nothing new in the twenty minutes since the last two pushes, so it looks finished. Four fix-up commits went onto `cloud-agent-provider`.

**Round one (657a76e)** was the seven accepted findings plus CodeQL and the Windows CI fixes already described. I added the repo-root `.gitattributes` on your "yes", since that was the recommended option in the message you approved. Say so if you'd rather normalize in the tests instead and I'll swap it. The `ssh://git@host` normalization finding is closed with a comment and tracked as issue #358.

**Round two (f74478b)**, three new findings, all accepted:

- An existing user config is tightened to owner-only on load, since files from earlier releases are 0644. Project configs are never touched and Windows is skipped.
- Mirror locality is decided from the resolved path, so a configured mirror inside the project still gets the `.gitignore`. The project root itself never does, because a `*` there would hide the whole project.
- The watcher tracks "listed at startup" apart from "refreshed", so a failed baseline refresh is retried on every poll, silently while the agent is unchanged.

**Round three (c4353b0, test fix 117fa56)**, one thread plus five "previously missed" notes with no threads:

- Configured mirror roots are canonicalized through the nearest existing ancestor, so a relative setting gives an absolute native path and a symlink into the project is treated as inside it.
- The user config's mode is tightened before parsing, so a broken TOML file with a key in it is still protected.
- Detection consults the mirror before requiring a key, so already-mirrored histories still sync after a key is unset or rotated. This mattered because `sync` and `list` gate on it.
- A permanently refused agent listing, such as a rejected key or Privacy Mode, now ends `watch` and `run` with that error instead of polling forever behind the banner. Transient failures still retry.
- README now says a `cursorcloud` user-data-dir path is created rather than fallen back from.
- Multi-repository agents attributing to the first repository is deferred to issue #359, since a correct fix is an index-model change. The untreaded notes are answered in a PR comment.

The one Windows failure along the way was my test creating a symlink before its target existed, which on Windows yields a file symlink that cannot be followed as a directory. Fixed by creating the target first.

Two things reach beyond the provider and are called out in the PR description: the config file mode change, now including the on-load chmod, and the watch exit on permanent API refusal. The PR is ready for your review and merge into `dev`. Locally, the root `.gitignore` edit, the runstory files and the plan doc remain uncommitted as before.
